articles.title: Open to investigation: on the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and its Rules, has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.title: Deemed ineligible: on the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls. If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Small fish: On Operation Trident
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: River pollution from industrial effluents indicates state failure

The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods.

The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. The Court has also upbraided local authorities for failing to enforce pollution norms by citing the Court’s own stay of a 2022 National Green Tribunal order imposing a compensation on the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation and the local administration in Jodhpur and Barmer. The State regulatory apparatus has been dysfunctional: officials were aware of illegal mining operations in some areas, yet they regularised leases in those areas. Given the dereliction in play, the Court is correct to treat the possibility of collusion between State officials and industrial mafias seriously. Justice Mehta’s observation that the State could be held liable under the ‘polluter pays’ principle is also a significant indictment of state failure, through negligence. Now, importantly, the State still has to restore the Jojari and attend to its wellbeing, which is relevant to a recent tendency by the Court to substitute itself for regulators rather than disciplining them into discharging their functions. This needs to change.

The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. The Court has also upbraided local authorities for failing to enforce pollution norms by citing the Court’s own stay of a 2022 National Green Tribunal order imposing a compensation on the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation and the local administration in Jodhpur and Barmer. The State regulatory apparatus has been dysfunctional: officials were aware of illegal mining operations in some areas, yet they regularised leases in those areas. Given the dereliction in play, the Court is correct to treat the possibility of collusion between State officials and industrial mafias seriously. Justice Mehta’s observation that the State could be held liable under the ‘polluter pays’ principle is also a significant indictment of state failure, through negligence. Now, importantly, the State still has to restore the Jojari and attend to its wellbeing, which is relevant to a recent tendency by the Court to substitute itself for regulators rather than disciplining them into discharging their functions. This needs to change.

fullParagraphs: Aavin will plough back 90% of the proceeds from the sale of sweets this festive season to invest in the welfare of dairy farmers, official sources said. “We have not increased milk prices, despite the procurement prices having gone up. We are balancing the welfare of the farmers’ cooperatives and our loyal consumers with quality goods at affordable prices,” a source said.
People have been supporting Aavin for its quality. Many corporates have booked sweets and savouries in bulk for supply in the run up to Deepavali, the source added.

All of Aavin’s major outlets in the city and elsewhere are already stocking 250 gram packets of ghee badhusha (₹205), nuts halwa (₹200), kaju pista roll (₹340) and kaju katli (₹280). The sweets come in assorted packets too – 250 grams and 500 grams priced at ₹240 and ₹475 each. They also have savouries – 200 gram packets of butter murukku priced at ₹95 each and similar sized packets of special mixture priced at ₹110 each.

Like in the previous years, Aavin is producing sweets using its own ghee, butter, and khoa at its Ambattur dairy. “We are following FSSAI norms and are ensuring that sugar is added in the right proportions. Single use oil is used to fry the eatables. We do not use hydrogenated vegetable oil. Quality check is being done at all stages,” another source said.

articles.title: ED searches premises linked to Mudrex, Instadapp over alleged ₹4,600-crore FEMA violations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials of the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Thursday conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh in connection with an investigation into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) involving unauthorised cross-border money transfers through cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins.

The searches were conducted by the ED’s Bengaluru Zonal Office on October 27 under Section 37 of FEMA. The investigation concerns entities associated with cryptocurrency platforms Mudrex and Instadapp, which allegedly facilitated cross-border financial transactions by using virtual digital assets (VDAs) to bypass authorised banking channels.

According to an ED press release issued on October 29, the investigation was initiated following complaints alleging large-scale FEMA violations by Bengaluru-based RPAS Technologies Private Limited, which operates the platforms Mudrex and Saber.money.

The agency said its preliminary findings revealed the alleged circumvention of FEMA regulations through an unauthorised cross-border payment system using crypto tokens, particularly USDT/USDC stablecoins. The entities allegedly advertised instant international money transfers through cryptocurrencies without the required authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The platforms reportedly offered services to buy, sell, and swap cryptocurrencies, as well as convert fiat currency into crypto assets and back, facilitating international transfers.

The ED said its investigation had identified large-volume over-the-counter (OTC) deals involving shell entities, particularly those incorporated in Canada, Lithuania, the United States and other jurisdictions. These entities allegedly operated foreign-based cryptocurrency trading platforms to facilitate unauthorised cross-border transfers.

The agency also alleged that the entities used foreign-based cryptocurrency platforms to purchase or sell foreign-based crypto assets and settle transactions through Indian bank accounts, in violation of FEMA provisions. It further alleged that expenses in foreign countries were being paid using cryptocurrencies in contravention of the law.
The ED said its preliminary findings indicated that unauthorised cross-border transfers and crypto balances held on foreign platforms amounted to more than ₹4,600 crore. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: DVAC searches premises linked to ex-Minister K.N. Nehru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The search at Mr. Nehru’s residence, carried out by a team headed by a Deputy Superintendent of Police, began around 7 a.m.

Multiple teams of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted searches at the residence of former Minister K.N. Nehru of the DMK in Tiruchi, and four other places in the district on Thursday in connection with the alleged multi-crore cash-for-jobs scam. Searches were also conducted at multiple locations across the State.

Headed by a Deputy Superintendent of Police of the agency, the searches at Mr. Nehru’s residence at Thillai Nagar in Tiruchi commenced around 7 a.m. Several DMK members gathered in front of his residence. The searches came against the backdrop of the Madras High Court clearing the decks for the DVAC to investigate the case filed against the former Minister.
K.N. Nehru cash-for-jobs scam case: Madras High Court clears decks for DVAC probe
What did the ED dossiers against T.N. Minister K.N. Nehru contain | Explained

During the nearly eight-hour operation, investigators seized a tablet computer and a few documents connected with the case, DVAC sources said. Mr. Nehru, who was the Municipal Administration Minister in the DMK government of 2021-2026, was present at the time.

Similar searches were conducted at the residence of DMK town secretary Murali at Thuraiyur in Tiruchi district, and the residence of a person named Mohanraj at Manapparai. Searches were also conducted at the residences of two individuals at Srirangam and Tiruvanaikoil in Tiruchi, police sources said.
DVAC officials also conducted searches on the premises belonging to Mr. Nehru’s brother on Tiruchi Road and at GV Residency in Coimbatore.
DVAC conducts searches at the residence of businessman J. Sekar alias Sekar Reddy at Gandhi Nagar, Katpadi in Vellore on October 29, 2026 | Photo Credit: C. Venkatachalapathy

The DVAC had registered a case against Mr. Nehru and others on the basis of a complaint filed by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED). In a letter to the then Director-General of Police and Head of Police Force, the central agency had levelled serious allegations of corruption in the recruitment of 2,538 Assistant Engineers, Junior Engineers, and Town Planning Officers in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department when Mr. Nehru was holding the portfolio.
In Namakkal, the DVAC officials searched the residence of former DMK MLA Ramalingam. They also visited the house of Durai, a relative of Mr. Nehru, but it was locked.

Searches were also conducted at premises linked to former DMK MLA from Vellore’s Anaicut Assembly constituency A.P. Nandakumar, and industrialist and former member of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) J. Sekar Reddy at Katpadi in Vellore. It is learnt that the searches were part of the ongoing probe against Mr. Nehru.
Mr. Nehru said the searches at his residence could be a diversionary tactic by the TVK-led government in the wake of a spike in crimes in the State and a jailbreak in Theni.

articles.title: NIA takes over probe into alleged arson attack at Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Keralam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police cite suspected cryptocurrency payments, alleged reconnaissance videos and possible international terror links as grounds for a wider probe
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the investigation into the alleged arson attack on the premises of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in Ernakulam.
The move follows a directive issued by the Union Home Ministry.
Last week, the Kochi City police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against Ebin Paul, the accused in the case.

He was charged under Sections 15 and 18 of the Act, which deal with offences relating to a terrorist act and conspiracy, respectively. The provisions were invoked in view of the sensitive nature of the site allegedly targeted by the accused.

The police found that instructions had allegedly been passed on to the accused by other individuals. He is also suspected to have received certain payments in cryptocurrency. The police further claimed to have recovered videos showing him conducting reconnaissance of the location and rehearsing the crime.
The accused is suspected to have been involved in three arson incidents in Ernakulam district. Investigators had also found indications that he had identified targets outside the district.

Alleged communications recovered from the accused’s phone, containing references to sensitive targets, including Jewish places of worship, were among the reasons cited for a wider probe by the NIA. The police believed that the possibility of international terror links, the identities of individuals suspected of sending messages to the accused, and the financial transactions connected to the case warranted a thorough examination.

He was charged under Sections 15 and 18 of the Act, which deal with offences relating to a terrorist act and conspiracy, respectively. The provisions were invoked in view of the sensitive nature of the site allegedly targeted by the accused.

The police found that instructions had allegedly been passed on to the accused by other individuals. He is also suspected to have received certain payments in cryptocurrency. The police further claimed to have recovered videos showing him conducting reconnaissance of the location and rehearsing the crime.

The accused is suspected to have been involved in three arson incidents in Ernakulam district. Investigators had also found indications that he had identified targets outside the district.

Alleged communications recovered from the accused’s phone, containing references to sensitive targets, including Jewish places of worship, were among the reasons cited for a wider probe by the NIA. The police believed that the possibility of international terror links, the identities of individuals suspected of sending messages to the accused, and the financial transactions connected to the case warranted a thorough examination.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary to visit Kathmandu as plans get underway for Nepal PM’s India visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nepal PM Balendra Shah is expected to visit Delhi by the end of the year, in what would be his first bilateral visit abroad, as he has been focused on domestic issues

In a visit to fine-tune the details of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah ’s planned trip to India, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri is expected to reach Kathmandu on November 4, along with newly designated Indian ambassador Sudhakar Dalela, a Nepali diplomatic source has told The Hindu .

Mr. Shah is expected to visit India by the end of the year, even as his seven-month-old government continues to deal with the aftermath of the devastating floods in the Bhote Koshi River while also planning a slew of administrative and political reforms.

If it materialises, this will be the first bilateral visit abroad by Mr. Shah, who rose to prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising in Nepal that overthrew the government of former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Shah, who belongs to the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) led by former media personality Rabi Lamichhane, had vowed to focus on domestic priorities while deprioritising foreign interlocutors. In fact, Mr. Misri was earlier scheduled to travel to Kathmandu to meet Prime Minister Shah in May but the visit was postponed, ostensibly because of the new leader’s resolve to focus on domestic challenges.

Subsequently, RSP chairman Mr. Lamichhane was hosted in New Delhi and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 3, after which Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal visited Delhi on June 5, in the first Minister-level representation to India from the new government, and met his Indian counterpart S. Jaishankar. This was followed by the visits of Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle in September and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who participated in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) Home Ministers’ meeting held on October 13. Mr. Gurung also met Mr. Jaishankar before he returned to Kathmandu. Mr. Wagle paid a repeat visit to New Delhi to participate in a private media conclave on October 23, when he also had a courtesy meeting with the Prime Minister.

Despite the flurry of visits, the Embassy of Nepal here has been left without an Ambassador for some months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Diplomatic sources said that the appointment of a new Nepali Ambassador to India will feature in the talks with Mr. Misri.

Nepal now has a complex new process to appoint envoys, as the new government announced that top ambassadorial posts would be selected through a public application process. In all, around 4,400 candidates had applied for the vacant ambassadorial positions. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu that Kathmandu is awaiting the agrément (diplomatic permission) from India for Nischal Nath Pandey’s arrival in the Nepali Embassy in Delhi. Of the top ambassadorial posts in 13 Nepali missions, three remain uncertain, while Mr. Pandey’s name, along with nine others, has received the necessary clearance in Kathmandu.

Mr. Misri’s upcoming visit is also expected to review Nepal’s requirements for dealing with the aftermath of the disaster in the Bhote Koshi River, which affected hundreds of Indian families as well, as many individuals remain missing.

The Foreign Secretary is likely to meet Mr. Lamichhane, who earlier this week paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati. The RSP chairman, who travelled to Uttarakhand by road from western Nepal, had described his visit to these pilgrimage centres as “personal and not political”.

“There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” he said, before starting his pilgrimage in his second visit to India in six months.

Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu may also include stakeholders from other political parties, though a final outlook on that is yet to be firmed up. It is understood that discussions may include a review of the Balendra Shah-led government, which came to power in March after the RSP’s sweeping electoral victory, defeating the Maoist parties and the Nepali Congress. Since coming to power, Mr. Shah has attempted several new initiatives, the latest of which includes an ordinance that will revise retirement age for government officials, bringing it down to 55 years from 58 years.

articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: With Deepavali falling in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to begin shopping after receiving their monthly salaries and festival bonuses; the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is likely to witness massive retail activity
Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

Though gold and silver prices saw a decline recently, jewellery retailers are yet to see business picking up. “We were hoping for better sales as the prices fell. But, consumers are waiting for further fall in prices,” said B. Sabarinath, president of the Coimbatore Jewellers Association.
The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Cost of input materials increased 20% during the quarter.
Coal India’s net profit surged 57% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,547 crore in the second quarter, driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations that offset an increase in input costs.
The state-owned coal miner declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

Offtake during the quarter ended September increased 12% YoY to 186.34 million tonnes (MT), primarily driven by higher power demand. Average price realisation, covering fuel supply agreements, e-auctions, washed coal and other categories, rose 7% YoY to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.
The Kolkata-headquartered company’s overall production grew 4% YoY to 151.37 MT in the reported quarter, falling short of its target of 157.83 MT.
Revenue from the sale of products increased 21% YoY to ₹43,724 crore. Overall revenue also rose 21% to ₹44,179 crore.

The company’s cost of materials -- which primarily includes expenditure on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares and timber, among other items -- increased 20% YoY to ₹2,752 crore during the quarter.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Fed is expected to keep the rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market economies for foreign investors

The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4.0% at its October policy meeting. The 12-member committee had a 10:2 voting pattern for maintaining the status quo, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal President Beth Hammack voted in favour of a 25 basis points hike.
The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.
While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.
“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

The stock market too traded lower in early trade but trimmed losses, with the Sensex trading 852.58 points higher to 74,098.61 at 2.30 p.m. The Nifty 50 was trading above 22,900. Analysts note that the Nifty must trade below 22,500 for bearishness to pertain.

The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.

While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.

“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.

On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

The stock market too traded lower in early trade but trimmed losses, with the Sensex trading 852.58 points higher to 74,098.61 at 2.30 p.m. The Nifty 50 was trading above 22,900. Analysts note that the Nifty must trade below 22,500 for bearishness to pertain.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The 12-member FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation

The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market -- the Fed’s other mandate -- has been largely stable.
“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

France is in turmoil. And Albania. And Spain. Even India. As were Bangladesh or Sri Lanka earlier. The list goes on. While the specific demands may vary, one thing is common across these mobilisations: the young are on the streets. Why are the young angry the world over? articles.title: India votes in favour of UNGA resolution calling for end to US embargo on Cuba
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The 193-member General Assembly adopted the resolution on October 28, with 130 countries voting in favour, 17 against and 25 abstaining

India voted in favour of a UN General Assembly resolution calling for an end to the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the U.S. against Cuba, reiterating that the restrictions should be lifted to help the Caribbean nation pursue its development aspirations.
The 193-member General Assembly adopted the resolution on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) with 130 countries voting in favour, 17 against and 25 abstaining.

Delivering India's statement, Counsellor at India's Permanent Mission to the UN Soumya Nair said the General Assembly has repeatedly called for an end to the embargo and rejected laws and regulations with extraterritorial effects that adversely affect the sovereignty of other states and the progress and prosperity of their peoples.

"India reiterates the Assembly's call to all states to refrain from promulgating and applying, and to repeal and invalidate, such laws and measures in conformity with their obligations under the Charter of the United Nations and international law," she said.
Ms. Nair said India's commitment to multilateralism is rooted in the belief that international challenges are best addressed through dialogue and diplomacy, in accordance with the UN Charter.

"It is in this spirit that India hopes that the embargo will be lifted at the earliest to help create an environment that would enable the people of Cuba to participate more fully in international cooperation and pursue their legitimate development aspirations,” she said.
Citing a report by the UN Secretary-General, Ms. Nair highlighted the impact of the restrictions on Cuba's economy and essential services.
Cuba's health system faces shortages of over 60% of essential medicines, while food production has declined by more than 50% in the past five years, she said.

“The restrictions on fuel exports to Cuba have also aggravated the country's ongoing energy crisis. The shortages have disrupted essential services, including healthcare, education, water supplies, food distribution, and transportation,” Ms. Nair said.

The conflict between America and Cuba stems from a decades-old political, economic, and ideological divide that began when Fidel Castro overthrew a U.S.-backed government in 1959 and aligned the island with the Soviet Union.

Washington has maintained a strict trade embargo and sanctions against Cuba for over six decades to pressure its communist regime. Cuba blames these restrictions for crippling its economy, causing severe fuel shortages, blackouts, and deep poverty.

The resolution, titled "Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba", reflects the General Assembly's longstanding opposition to the U.S. restrictions. However, General Assembly resolutions of this nature are not legally binding.

At least four tankers have caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to navigate the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's armed forces said on Thursday (October 29, 2026), a day after the U.S. military said it had cleared key routes through the waterway.

"Over the past 24 hours, three violating oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines while attempting to pass through the unauthorised southern route of the Strait of Hormuz," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement.
The vessels had "switched off all their radar and navigation systems" and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said.
It was not immediately clear when the incidents occurred or which flags the tankers were flying.
Later on Thursday (October 29, 2026), Iran's army reported that another tanker had caught fire east of the strait.

"A tanker that was illegally operating in a restricted and dangerous area east of the Strait of Hormuz was damaged and caught fire after striking naval mines, rendering it unable to move," the army said in a statement carried by State television.

In recent weeks, Iran has reported multiple vessels striking sea mines, prompting U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), which runs military operations in the region, to reaffirm on social media its insistence that all mines in "primary transit routes" have been cleared.

On Thursday (October 29, 2026), Hossein Mohebi, the spokesman for the IRGC challenged the claim, saying, "Prove your Hormuz mine-clearing claim with independent evidence, not statements!" in a post on X.
Since the outbreak of the war on February 28, Iran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil and gas consumption.

The United States has in response imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait. On Sunday (October 25, 2026), CENTCOM said it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
Iran considers ships using the southern corridor near the Omani coast unauthorised.

In their statement on Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Guards said "the IRGC Navy states that the unauthorised route through the Strait of Hormuz is mined, and that vessel owners and crews are responsible for transiting these routes and should not pay attention to CENTCOM's delusions on social media".

fullParagraphs: The GOP has a 53–47 majority in the Senate currently, with 35 seats being contested this year. Of these, seven are “toss ups”, according to a non-partisan election analyser. These seats are in Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. All of these – except Michigan – are seats which are currently held by Republicans

As the U.S. heads towards midterm elections next week, the presidency of Donald Trump faces an inflection point, with the prospect of Republican control of the U.S. Congress weakening. Since early 2026 at least, forecasts have suggested the GOP would lose the U.S. House of Representatives. Recently, however, trends suggest that the Senate too is within reach of the Democrats.

articles.title: Serbia’s students demand resignations in police, judiciary as they prepare to take power
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Students’ List movement swept the parliamentary election on October 25, 2026 against Vucic’s right-wing Serbian Progressive Party, which has ruled unchallenged for 14 years

Serbia 's student movement on Thursday (October 29, 2026) demanded the resignations of top officials in the police, intelligence agencies, and the judiciary as they prepare to take power after a historic election win last weekend against former strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic.

The students at a news conference also urged Serbia's election authorities to officially declare the final results of Sunday's (October 25, 2026) ballot without delay after a rerun at some 50 polling stations next Sunday (November 1, 2026), so that a new Parliament and government can be formed.

The Students’ List movement swept the parliamentary election on Sunday (October 25, 2026) against Mr. Vucic’s right-wing Serbian Progressive Party, which has ruled unchallenged for 14 years. The outgoing authorities remain in control as the formal transition of power will take several weeks.

“Changes are starting now,” student Filip Ubovic said at the news conference held at a central Belgrade park that used to be a sealed-off area occupied by Mr. Vucic's loyalists. “Institutions belong to the citizens and the law applies to everyone.”

Mr. Vucic's party has gradually taken control over all State institutions since it came to power in 2012. The SNS party has been accused of rampant corruption and cronyism, links to organised crime, and pressure on the judiciary, police, and the media, which the populists have denied.
The students on Thursday (October 29, 2026) asked public servants to prevent outgoing officials from destroying documentation or evidence of potential wrongdoing.

Mr. Vucic on Thursday (October 29, 2026) held a news conference of his own, accusing the election winners of “revolutionary terror" after groups of people stormed the Informer TV station that led the pre-election propaganda branding the students as traitors and enemies of the State.

Suspicions of State corruption in infrastructure projects two years ago set off a wave of street protests after a collapsed canopy at a train station in Serbia's north killed 16 people after a renovation. The students led those protests before challenging and defeating Mr. Vucic at the early ballot on Sunday (October 25, 2026).

The students' win on Sunday (October 25, 2026) marks the first time that a grassroot youth movement toppled a well-established political leader. It comes at the moment when similar movements are mushrooming across Europe.

The students said in their briefing that top police officials and the intelligence agencies had served Mr. Vucic's party during the protests in violation of the law. They have been accused of using excessive force against protesters, illegal surveillance, detention and pressure on Mr. Vucic's political opponents.

The students also demanded changes in the judiciary and urgent investigations in top-level corruption cases that might have been sidelined due to political pressure under Mr. Vucic. They promised that all contracts and public spending deals will be reviewed.
“The Students' List is not here to take revenge,” Mr. Ubovic said. “We are not asking for political service but for the adherence to the laws, professionalism and responsibility.”

articles.title: The rise of industrial tourism in China
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Industrial tours showcase showcase innovation and manufacturing prowess to instil national pride, while presenting STEM as a sustainable career option for the youth

China’s factory floors have turned out to be sought after destinations during summer vacation this year. There has been a visible rise in tours to hi-tech manufacturing facilities like electric vehicles, electronics, and high-speed trains, with shipyards and breweries also in the mix. According to a popular Chinese online travel booking platform, Tongcheng, bookings for factory tours rose more than 36 per cent year-on-year during this summer season, with families accounting for 68 per cent of bookings.

These factory-technology tours are part of the growing phenomenon of industrial tourism ( gongye luyou ) – a policy initiative actively promoted by the ruling Communist Party-state. Rather than make these tours from a sightseeing perspective, The state seeks to make them niche tourism an instrument for showcasing industrial capability, strengthening industrial brands, and educating young people about technology. According to Beijing city’s municipal bureau, in 2024, the city had 15 million industrial tourists and generated 1.7 billion yuan ($248 million) in revenue.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: The rise of industrial tourism in China. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: Palestinian President says hopes for peace talks with new Israeli government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas said on Thursday (October 29, 2026) that he hoped the election of a new Israeli government would allow for the resumption of peace talks.

"For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace," Mr. Abbas said during a meeting with Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia.
"We hope that, immediately after a new Israeli government is formed, we will be able to engage in dialogue together," he added.

With almost all ballots counted from Israel's pivotal election, neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in parliament.
The uncertain outcome might mean weeks of trying to cobble together coalitions.
The Israeli-Palestinian peace process has been stalled for years, despite the recognition of the State of Palestine by a growing number of countries.
Under Mr. Netanyahu's watch, settlement construction and violence against Palestinians has soared in the occupied West Bank, where Mr. Abbas' Palestinian Authority exercises limited self-rule.

Ministers in Mr. Netanyahu's hard-right coalition have openly called for Israel's annexation of the West Bank and advocated policies encouraging Palestinians to leave the territory as well as the war-ravaged Gaza Strip.
Mr. Netanyahu led Israel in a devastating war which has left much of Gaza in rubble following Hamas's unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack.
Israel has since 1967 occupied the West Bank, where more than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements illegal under international law among some three million Palestinians.

articles.title: Experts warn of wider spread as Ebola outbreak reaches plateau
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A major challenge in Congo is limited contact tracing and collaboration with affected communities; health workers sometimes spend more time trying to convince locals to work with them than giving care
The Ebola outbreak in Congo passed a grim milestone this week — 10,000 confirmed cases — and spurred questions about whether health authorities are losing their ability to contain it.

Nearly half the infected people in this outbreak have died, and some experts say there are reasons to worry this could grow into the worst Ebola outbreak in history. Others don't think it will reach that level. Researchers are currently working on updated projections.

Current circumstances suggest it's unlikely to spark significant problems in most other countries, some researchers said. But about 30 confirmed cases have already popped up in other nations. And the risk that more will appear outside Congo will grow if the outbreak isn't tamed, said Justin Lessler, a University of North Carolina researcher who studies the dynamics of infectious disease outbreaks.
Experts also are hopeful that a vaccine will become available next year that could help control it.

At a virtual summit of African health ministers on Wednesday, Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya said the continent is “not winning” the fight against Ebola and needs to do more after it spread to multiple African countries. “Together, we agreed to prepare every country, coordinate across our borders and keep those borders open while watching them closely,” Kaseya wrote on X.
Steady case numbers raise concerns about spread beyond Congo

About 400 to 500 new confirmed cases have been reported in Congo each week, and that number seems to be holding steady. It's good news that “cases are not rising exponentially,” at least for the moment, said Dr. Boghuma Titanji, an Emory University infectious disease specialist.
“But they're not coming down, either," she said. "It's at a plateau. And the plateau is at a very, very high set point."

A major challenge in Congo is limited contact tracing and collaboration with affected communities; health workers sometimes spend more time trying to convince locals to work with them than giving care.

Fewer than a quarter of new cases are coming from people known to have been in contact with an infected person, showing there are ongoing chains of transmission that health authorities are not aware of.

As cases mount, the likelihood grows that more infected people travel to other countries, Titanji and other experts said. France, Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda also have reported cases tied to the Congo outbreak.

Travel restrictions, like those imposed by the US, can make it harder for the virus to leave Africa. And in many places where a traveller's infection may surface, health officials should be able to quickly isolate an infected person and find any contacts, experts say.

articles.title: ICMR funds study to identify genetic links, potential therapies for autoimmune diseases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The findings could help scientists better understand the disease processes involved and identify potential targets for developing new therapies

The Indian Council of Medical Research has funded a four-year study to investigate the genetic and immunological mechanisms underlying autoimmune diseases by studying families with multiple affected members, AIIMS doctors said on Thursday, appealing to SLE patients to get enrolled in the study.

The project titled ‘Genomic Profiling and Identification of Targetable Shared Immunopathogenic Events in Multiplex Families with Autoimmune Diseases’ has been awarded to Dipyaman Ganguly of Ashoka University, Sonipat, Haryana, and Ranjan Gupta, additional professor in the Department of Rheumatology, AIIMS, Delhi.

The study aims to build a nationwide cohort of 200 families in which multiple members are affected by autoimmune diseases. Each participating family must have at least one member diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), commonly known as lupus, Gupta said.

The researchers will conduct genetic and immunological assessments of the enrolled patients and their family members to identify shared biological mechanisms that contribute to the development of these conditions.
The findings could help scientists better understand the disease processes involved and identify potential targets for developing new therapies, he said.

Autoimmune diseases occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own tissues. A family history of such conditions is associated with an increased risk of developing them, highlighting the importance of investigating genetic and shared immunological factors, Gupta said.

The four-year project will involve clinical centres at AIIMS Delhi; AIIMS Bibinagar, Telangana; Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGIMS), Lucknow; St John's Hospital, Bengaluru; Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad; and the Kolkata Medical College. These centres will contribute clinical data and biological samples for the study.
Patients diagnosed with lupus and residing in Delhi-NCR can contact the centre at AIIMS Delhi to check their eligibility for participation, Gupta said.
Participation will be subject to eligibility assessment and the study's enrolment requirements.

articles.title: Heat-related deaths up 36% since Paris Agreement as climate action lags: Lancet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The analysis represents the work of 146 multidisciplinary researchers from more than 100 institutions across more than 30 countries. It tracks 54 indicators of the health impacts of climate change and the health effects of climate action

Some of the health harms of climate change grew faster in the decade since the Paris Agreement entered into force (2016-2025) than in the previous decade (2006-2015) as climate action fails to keep pace, according to the 10th Lancet Countdown Report on Health and Climate Change .
The report, which was released on Wednesday, said the annual average heat-related deaths rose by nearly 36% globally after the Paris Agreement was introduced.
"In 2023 alone, heat was linked to a record 710,000 deaths with more than 70 per cent of that toll attributable to human-caused climate change," it said.

The analysis represents the work of 146 multidisciplinary researchers from more than 100 institutions across more than 30 countries. It tracks 54 indicators of the health impacts of climate change and the health effects of climate action.

The report highlights that cleaner energy, more resilient health systems, more health-protecting legislation and growing scientific evidence have brought real health benefits to local communities since the Paris Agreement, but these gains are still too slow, too insufficient, and too inconsistent to offset the growing risks.
"Rising overall energy demand and slow system change means fossil fuels still supply over 80% of the world's energy, and climate-heating emissions reached a record high in 2024," it said.
The report added that despite gains in some countries, fossil-fuel air pollution still kills an estimated 2.8 million people a year worldwide.
Moreover, adaptation funding is falling far short of what's needed.

According to the report, the health adaptation needs quantified so far by developing countries put the minimum cost at $3.3 billion a year, based on data from only 48 of the 79 countries that have completed these estimates.
However, only around a third of this declared need, $1.1 billion, was committed in 2024.

"This substantial financing gap is reflected in countries' ability to translate adaptation priorities into action, with finance and human resourcing identified as the top barriers to implementation of Health National Adaptation Plans," said the report.

articles.title: Why India rejected a patent application for shorter drug-resistant TB treatment | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The decision could open the door to greater generic competition, but its impact on treatment costs will depend on drug availability, pricing, and access to care

The story so far: The Indian Patent Office has rejected a patent application filed by the U.S.-based Global Alliance for TB Drug Development (TB Alliance) for the combination of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid, known as BPaL. The six-month, all-oral regimen is recommended by the World Health Organisation (WHO) for eligible patients with certain forms of drug-resistant tuberculosis.

BPaL — bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid — provides a shorter, more effective treatment for people with highly drug-resistant tuberculosis, for whom older regimens could involve 18–24 months of treatment, multiple medicines and, in some cases, painful injections.

articles.title: Financial protection for patients cannot be achieved through a single intervention: former National Health Authority CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Former NHA CEO Indu Bhushan says the government needs to address how services are purchased, how providers are paid, how patients access treatment, and how the system assures quality

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority’s (NPPA) decision to cap trade margins on 137 anti-cancer medicines is an important step towards reducing the financial burden of cancer treatment, but its success will depend on whether the savings reach patients, Indu Bhushan, healthcare policy expert and former CEO of the National Health Authority, said.

In an exclusive interview with The Hindu , Dr. Bhushan said the intervention could substantially reduce costs for patients requiring prolonged treatment. The revised prices are to take effect from November 9.

fullParagraphs: People living with lupus describe how symptoms such as fatigue affect their work and daily lives. Studies show that patients and doctors may view the impact of the disease differently, highlighting the need to better understand patients’ experiences and concerns

When Nisha Panwar,30, was diagnosed with lupus in December 2013, she felt relieved. After months of recurrent fever, rashes and worsening symptoms, she finally had an explanation for what was happening to her body. Before the diagnosis, she says, several doctors had told her she had no disease and that it was “all in my head” and was referred to a psychiatrist.

For Tabassum Sultana, 28, a Bengaluru-based content creator, the diagnosis of mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), with features of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), in 2024 was followed by another setback. She developed avascular necrosis of the right hip and underwent surgery in September 2025. Her recovery was slow, she became dependent on her mother for everyday activities and had to stop working. Recurring flare-ups continue to affect her mental health.

articles.title: Aavin to invest proceeds from sale of sweets in welfare of dairy farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Aavin will plough back 90% of the proceeds from the sale of sweets this festive season to invest in the welfare of dairy farmers, official sources said. “We have not increased milk prices, despite the procurement prices having gone up. We are balancing the welfare of the farmers’ cooperatives and our loyal consumers with quality goods at affordable prices,” a source said.
People have been supporting Aavin for its quality. Many corporates have booked sweets and savouries in bulk for supply in the run up to Deepavali, the source added.

All of Aavin’s major outlets in the city and elsewhere are already stocking 250 gram packets of ghee badhusha (₹205), nuts halwa (₹200), kaju pista roll (₹340) and kaju katli (₹280). The sweets come in assorted packets too – 250 grams and 500 grams priced at ₹240 and ₹475 each. They also have savouries – 200 gram packets of butter murukku priced at ₹95 each and similar sized packets of special mixture priced at ₹110 each.

Like in the previous years, Aavin is producing sweets using its own ghee, butter, and khoa at its Ambattur dairy. “We are following FSSAI norms and are ensuring that sugar is added in the right proportions. Single use oil is used to fry the eatables. We do not use hydrogenated vegetable oil. Quality check is being done at all stages,” another source said.

articles.title: ED searches premises linked to Mudrex, Instadapp over alleged ₹4,600-crore FEMA violations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials of the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Thursday conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh in connection with an investigation into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) involving unauthorised cross-border money transfers through cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins.

The searches were conducted by the ED’s Bengaluru Zonal Office on October 27 under Section 37 of FEMA. The investigation concerns entities associated with cryptocurrency platforms Mudrex and Instadapp, which allegedly facilitated cross-border financial transactions by using virtual digital assets (VDAs) to bypass authorised banking channels.

According to an ED press release issued on October 29, the investigation was initiated following complaints alleging large-scale FEMA violations by Bengaluru-based RPAS Technologies Private Limited, which operates the platforms Mudrex and Saber.money.

The agency said its preliminary findings revealed the alleged circumvention of FEMA regulations through an unauthorised cross-border payment system using crypto tokens, particularly USDT/USDC stablecoins. The entities allegedly advertised instant international money transfers through cryptocurrencies without the required authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The platforms reportedly offered services to buy, sell, and swap cryptocurrencies, as well as convert fiat currency into crypto assets and back, facilitating international transfers.

The ED said its investigation had identified large-volume over-the-counter (OTC) deals involving shell entities, particularly those incorporated in Canada, Lithuania, the United States and other jurisdictions. These entities allegedly operated foreign-based cryptocurrency trading platforms to facilitate unauthorised cross-border transfers.

The agency also alleged that the entities used foreign-based cryptocurrency platforms to purchase or sell foreign-based crypto assets and settle transactions through Indian bank accounts, in violation of FEMA provisions. It further alleged that expenses in foreign countries were being paid using cryptocurrencies in contravention of the law.
The ED said its preliminary findings indicated that unauthorised cross-border transfers and crypto balances held on foreign platforms amounted to more than ₹4,600 crore. The investigation is ongoing.
