articles.title: DVAC searches premises linked to ex-Minister K.N. Nehru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The search at Mr. Nehru’s residence, carried out by a team headed by a Deputy Superintendent of Police, began around 7 a.m.

Multiple teams of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted searches at the residence of former Minister K.N. Nehru of the DMK in Tiruchi, and four other places in the district on Thursday in connection with the alleged multi-crore cash-for-jobs scam. Searches were also conducted at multiple locations across the State.

Headed by a Deputy Superintendent of Police of the agency, the searches at Mr. Nehru’s residence at Thillai Nagar in Tiruchi commenced around 7 a.m. Several DMK members gathered in front of his residence. The searches came against the backdrop of the Madras High Court clearing the decks for the DVAC to investigate the case filed against the former Minister.
K.N. Nehru cash-for-jobs scam case: Madras High Court clears decks for DVAC probe
What did the ED dossiers against T.N. Minister K.N. Nehru contain | Explained

During the nearly eight-hour operation, investigators seized a tablet computer and a few documents connected with the case, DVAC sources said. Mr. Nehru, who was the Municipal Administration Minister in the DMK government of 2021-2026, was present at the time.

Similar searches were conducted at the residence of DMK town secretary Murali at Thuraiyur in Tiruchi district, and the residence of a person named Mohanraj at Manapparai. Searches were also conducted at the residences of two individuals at Srirangam and Tiruvanaikoil in Tiruchi, police sources said.
DVAC officials also conducted searches on the premises belonging to Mr. Nehru’s brother on Tiruchi Road and at GV Residency in Coimbatore.
DVAC conducts searches at the residence of businessman J. Sekar alias Sekar Reddy at Gandhi Nagar, Katpadi in Vellore on October 29, 2026 | Photo Credit: C. Venkatachalapathy

The DVAC had registered a case against Mr. Nehru and others on the basis of a complaint filed by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED). In a letter to the then Director-General of Police and Head of Police Force, the central agency had levelled serious allegations of corruption in the recruitment of 2,538 Assistant Engineers, Junior Engineers, and Town Planning Officers in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department when Mr. Nehru was holding the portfolio.
In Namakkal, the DVAC officials searched the residence of former DMK MLA Ramalingam. They also visited the house of Durai, a relative of Mr. Nehru, but it was locked.

Searches were also conducted at premises linked to former DMK MLA from Vellore’s Anaicut Assembly constituency A.P. Nandakumar, and industrialist and former member of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) J. Sekar Reddy at Katpadi in Vellore. It is learnt that the searches were part of the ongoing probe against Mr. Nehru.
Mr. Nehru said the searches at his residence could be a diversionary tactic by the TVK-led government in the wake of a spike in crimes in the State and a jailbreak in Theni.

articles.title: NIA takes over probe into alleged arson attack at Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Keralam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police cite suspected cryptocurrency payments, alleged reconnaissance videos and possible international terror links as grounds for a wider probe
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the investigation into the alleged arson attack on the premises of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in Ernakulam.
The move follows a directive issued by the Union Home Ministry.
Last week, the Kochi City police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against Ebin Paul, the accused in the case.

He was charged under Sections 15 and 18 of the Act, which deal with offences relating to a terrorist act and conspiracy, respectively. The provisions were invoked in view of the sensitive nature of the site allegedly targeted by the accused.

The police found that instructions had allegedly been passed on to the accused by other individuals. He is also suspected to have received certain payments in cryptocurrency. The police further claimed to have recovered videos showing him conducting reconnaissance of the location and rehearsing the crime.
The accused is suspected to have been involved in three arson incidents in Ernakulam district. Investigators had also found indications that he had identified targets outside the district.

Alleged communications recovered from the accused’s phone, containing references to sensitive targets, including Jewish places of worship, were among the reasons cited for a wider probe by the NIA. The police believed that the possibility of international terror links, the identities of individuals suspected of sending messages to the accused, and the financial transactions connected to the case warranted a thorough examination.

Last week, the Kochi City police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against Ebin Paul, the accused in the case.

He was charged under Sections 15 and 18 of the Act, which deal with offences relating to a terrorist act and conspiracy, respectively. The provisions were invoked in view of the sensitive nature of the site allegedly targeted by the accused.

The police found that instructions had allegedly been passed on to the accused by other individuals. He is also suspected to have received certain payments in cryptocurrency. The police further claimed to have recovered videos showing him conducting reconnaissance of the location and rehearsing the crime.

The accused is suspected to have been involved in three arson incidents in Ernakulam district. Investigators had also found indications that he had identified targets outside the district.

Alleged communications recovered from the accused’s phone, containing references to sensitive targets, including Jewish places of worship, were among the reasons cited for a wider probe by the NIA. articles.title: Foreign Secretary to visit Kathmandu as plans get underway for Nepal PM’s India visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nepal PM Balendra Shah is expected to visit Delhi by the end of the year, in what would be his first bilateral visit abroad, as he has been focused on domestic issues

In a visit to fine-tune the details of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah ’s planned trip to India, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri is expected to reach Kathmandu on November 4, along with newly designated Indian ambassador Sudhakar Dalela, a Nepali diplomatic source has told The Hindu .

Mr. Shah is expected to visit India by the end of the year, even as his seven-month-old government continues to deal with the aftermath of the devastating floods in the Bhote Koshi River while also planning a slew of administrative and political reforms.

If it materialises, this will be the first bilateral visit abroad by Mr. Shah, who rose to prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising in Nepal that overthrew the government of former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Shah, who belongs to the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) led by former media personality Rabi Lamichhane, had vowed to focus on domestic priorities while deprioritising foreign interlocutors. In fact, Mr. Misri was earlier scheduled to travel to Kathmandu to meet Prime Minister Shah in May but the visit was postponed, ostensibly because of the new leader’s resolve to focus on domestic challenges.

Subsequently, RSP chairman Mr. Lamichhane was hosted in New Delhi and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 3, after which Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal visited Delhi on June 5, in the first Minister-level representation to India from the new government, and met his Indian counterpart S. Jaishankar. This was followed by the visits of Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle in September and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who participated in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) Home Ministers’ meeting held on October 13. Mr. Gurung also met Mr. Jaishankar before he returned to Kathmandu. Mr. Wagle paid a repeat visit to New Delhi to participate in a private media conclave on October 23, when he also had a courtesy meeting with the Prime Minister.

Despite the flurry of visits, the Embassy of Nepal here has been left without an Ambassador for some months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Diplomatic sources said that the appointment of a new Nepali Ambassador to India will feature in the talks with Mr. Misri.

Nepal now has a complex new process to appoint envoys, as the new government announced that top ambassadorial posts would be selected through a public application process. In all, around 4,400 candidates had applied for the vacant ambassadorial positions. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu that Kathmandu is awaiting the agrément (diplomatic permission) from India for Nischal Nath Pandey’s arrival in the Nepali Embassy in Delhi. Of the top ambassadorial posts in 13 Nepali missions, three remain uncertain, while Mr. Pandey’s name, along with nine others, has received the necessary clearance in Kathmandu.

Mr. Misri’s upcoming visit is also expected to review Nepal’s requirements for dealing with the aftermath of the disaster in the Bhote Koshi River, which affected hundreds of Indian families as well, as many individuals remain missing.

The Foreign Secretary is likely to meet Mr. Lamichhane, who earlier this week paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati. The RSP chairman, who travelled to Uttarakhand by road from western Nepal, had described his visit to these pilgrimage centres as “personal and not political”.

“There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” he said, before starting his pilgrimage in his second visit to India in six months.

Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu may also include stakeholders from other political parties, though a final outlook on that is yet to be firmed up. It is understood that discussions may include a review of the Balendra Shah-led government, which came to power in March after the RSP’s sweeping electoral victory, defeating the Maoist parties and the Nepali Congress. Since coming to power, Mr. Shah has attempted several new initiatives, the latest of which includes an ordinance that will revise retirement age for government officials, bringing it down to 55 years from 58 years.

articles.title: Wicked surprise: On the northeast monsoon
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The northeast monsoon is more unpredictable, and the south must be wary

As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . While contributing only around a quarter of India’s annual rainfall, it is largely focused on the south-east peninsula regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Keralam. The southwest monsoon, influenced by a strengthening El Niño , has already left its desiccating mark. Rainfall from June-September was 759.4 mm against 868.6 mm, a 12.6% deficit, the driest in 11 years. This has impacted kharif sowing and is reflected in food inflation.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that this year, the northeast monsoon rainfall, spanning October to December, would likely be ‘normal’ , meaning in line with a 50-year average and within a 12% error window. Most parts of the country, it said, are expected to receive below-normal rainfall, except some areas of northwest India and southern parts of peninsular India, where rainfall is likely to be normal to above-normal. The wide error window, however, is far less precise than its forecasts for the southwest monsoon with its margin of 5%, and can sometimes make the northeast monsoon the bearer of nasty surprises. For instance, December 1, 2015, saw the city of Chennai deluged by its heaviest rainfall in 24-hours in over a century ; at least 500 lives were lost and 18 lakh people displaced in the State. That year and the present are linked by a common thread: a powerful El Niño. Associated with the heating up of the Central Pacific, the El Niño is linked to the drying up of the southwest monsoon rains but also yoked — not always — with a vigorous northeast monsoon. Other than in 2015, several El Niño years, such as 1997 and 2009, have been associated with above-normal rainfall between October and December in Tamil Nadu though El Niño years, such as 2002 and 1982, saw a poor northeast monsoon (and a predictably bad southwest monsoon). While the climate mechanisms linking a vigorous northeast monsoon and El Niño are still to be fully understood, it appears the warming patterns of the El Niño tend to deflect rain-bearing cyclonic circulations in unpredictable ways. Therefore, the Centre and the southern States ought to take enough precautions: from clearing up stormwater drains, fortifying shelters, making provisions for infrastructure damage and tightening weather warning forecasts to prepare for torrents.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

S.P. Karthikaa, Chief Executive Officer, Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority, has been transferred and posted as Additional Secretary, Social Welfare and Women Empowerment, replacing S. Valarmathi, who has been appointed Director, Rehabilitation and Welfare of Non-Resident Tamils.

S. Sangeetha, District Revenue Officer, Amma Unavagam, Greater Chennai Corporation, has been appointed Director-cum-Mission Director, Integrated Child Development Services, Chennai, replacing K. Santhi, who has been appointed Managing Director, Overseas Manpower Corporation Limited.

N. Kalidoss, Zonal Officer-10, Greater Chennai Corporation, has been transferred and posted as Additional Director (General), Directorate of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, Chennai. R. M. Manimegalai, General Manager, Tamil Nadu Ex-Servicemen Corporation (TEXCO), has been appointed Vice-Chairman and Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Watershed Development Agency, replacing R. Kannan, who was holding additional charge.

Sengottaiyan, Special District Revenue Officer (Land Acquisition), Highways Department, has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chennai Metro Asset Management Limited (CMAML), replacing Sweta Suman. articles.title: CM to release book co-authored by late B. Madhusoodana Kurup
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will release a book co-authored by the late B. Madhusoodana Kurup, founder Vice-Chancellor of the Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies and former Director of the School of Industrial Fisheries, Cusat, at a function in Kochi on Friday (October 29, 2026).
The book, Exploring the Legacy of Fishing and Farming Below Sea Level: Vembanad-Kole Wetlands of Southern India , has been co-authored by Dr. Kurup and Dr. Sileesh Mullasseri.

The School of Industrial Fisheries, Cusat, will organise the function in memory of Dr. Kurup. Fisheries Minister V.E. Abdul Gafoor will preside over the event, which will be held at BTH Hotel at 3.15 p.m.
Former Fisheries Ministers K. Babu and S. Sharma will receive the first copies of the book.

articles.title: SAD-AAP trade barbs on drug menace issue in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia accused Arvind Kejriwal of misleading Punjabis by giving the disproportionate assets case the label of a drug case to suppress the issue

With the drug menace issue emerging as the key poll issue ahead of the 2027 Assembly election, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) were embroiled in sharp war of words.

After the Punjab Vigilance Bureau filed a supplementary chargesheet against senior SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia in a disproportionate assets case before a special court in Mohali, AAP supremo and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal said that the AAP government in Punjab is taking the fight against drugs to its conclusion by filing a chargesheet against Mr. Majithia.

Party’s Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia said, “..The chargesheet filed by the Punjab Police against Bikram Singh Majithia today details how he earned ₹736 crore by selling drugs and deposited the money in bank accounts of his companies. After this chargesheet, Majithia will rot in jail for the rest of his life.”

Hitting out at the AAP, Mr. Majithia accused Mr. Kejriwal of misleading Punjabis by giving the disproportionate assets (DA) case the label of a drug case to suppress the issue of Punjab being pushed into turmoil.

“Mr. Kejriwal was attempting to divert public attention from the situation in Punjab by presenting the case against him as a drug trafficking case,” he said. He added that Mr. Kejriwal had apologised in 2018 for making false allegations against him in connection with drugs. “The AAP leadership was now once again trying to link his name to the drug case for political gains. The Supreme Court had given the government time until March 18, 2025, to establish the allegations against him, but the Kejriwal and Bhagwant Mann governments had failed to do so,” he said.

articles.title: 20 units of illegally mined sand near Ambur seized
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials said that the revenue earned in the public auction will go to the State exchequer
More than 20 units of river sand that was illegally mined from the dry Malattaru River was found at Machampattu village on Wednesday.

Revenue officials said that based on information from farmer and social activist J. Paranthaman, a team of revenue officials and the police inspected a private open land near the river, where huge quantities of river sand were stored in the open.

“Based on preliminary assessment, we have found over 20 units of river sand illegally kept in the private land. We have sealed the premises for further inspection by the Water Resources Department (WRD) team, for public auction of the seized sand,” S. Devi, Tasildar (Pernambut), told The Hindu.

A farming village, Machampattu forms part of Pernambut Panchayat Union in Vellore district. Most of the farmers depend on the river for domestic consumption and irrigation purposes. “Over the years, illegal sand mining has turned the perennial river into a seasonal waterbody. Illegal sand mining in the river also depleted groundwater in surrounding farming villages,” Mr. Paranthaman said.
Along with the local police, revenue officials led by tahsildar Devi had inspected the site where they found a large quantity of river sand stored in the open.

Revenue officials said that as per norms, mining of river sand, including for government purposes like construction of school buildings and Anganwadi centres, is prohibited in the State. For government infrastructure works, sand could be procured at designated government sand quarries in the district.

Revenue officials said that the revenue earned in the public auction will go to the State exchequer. Legal action will also be taken on the landowner, identified as Navin, for illegal mining of river sand. A probe is under way.

articles.title: TN Teachers Education University gets new Registrar-in-charge following allegation of irregularities by civilian group
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Welcoming the move, M. Radhakrishnan of Arappor Iyakkam, in a statement, demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the complaint and legal action against those involved in the “fraud”

The Higher Education Department has appointed M. Kanmani, Dean, Department of Educational Technology, Tamil Nadu Teachers Education University (TNTEU) as the Registrar-in-charge after the incumbent Registrar was removed following allegations of irregularities by corruption watch group, Arappor Iyakkam.

In a notification issued by the TNTEU on October 26, the appointment of Prof. Kanmani was announced “consequent to the relieving of Dr. K. Rajasekaran on 26.10.2026 ... from the post of Registrar i/c of this University”. Arappor Iyakkam had, earlier this month, alleged discrepancies in the affiliation inspection process conducted during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 academic years.
Welcoming the move, M. Radhakrishnan of Arappor Iyakkam, in a statement, demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the complaint and legal action against those involved in the “fraud”.

Additionally, the organisation insisted on publishing full details, including photographs, of faculty members working in affiliated colleges on the university’s website, to prohibit the practice of conducting ‘irregular classes’, implement a monthly online Aadhaar-based biometric attendance system for the faculty, as is the current practice in Anna University, and to publish the resolutions passed by the Syndicate on the university’s website.

After acquiring official records under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005, the organisation had pointed out that physical inspections were carried out in multiple colleges on the same day although they were several kilometres apart. It also said that certain individuals were listed as principals of multiple colleges at the same time.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

However, disinvestment should not be seen merely as a tool for meeting fiscal targets. It is a policy choice aimed at unlocking greater value from public assets, widening public ownership, and improving efficiency and governance through greater market discipline. The 2022 LIC IPO which drew in many first-time retail investors and policyholders remains a prime example.

This was precisely the rationale behind the government’s 2021 New Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) Policy which envisages a “bare minimum presence” of PSEs in strategic sectors. Likewise, the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) re-engines capital via mature public assets. A target of ₹16.72 lakh crore has been set under NMP 2.0 for FY26-30 after having achieved 90% of its Phase 1 goal.

This year, however, until this month, receipts had come mainly through Offer for Sale (OFS) measures which help to broaden ownership but keep the status quo on an enterprise’s operations. The strategic sale of the IDBI Bank since Air India in 2022 is an encouraging sign. From an industry perspective, the IDBI sale is more than a one-off sale. It is one of the largest Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) deals in India’s financial sector and constitutes as the first step towards a ‘Privatisation 2.0’ framework. More importantly, this framework is premised on being investor-led, professionally managed and time-bound. Two changes would help to turn into a template.

First, the selection criteria for disinvestments of PSEs should move to a demand-based approach instead of being led by the government. It would work better to first gauge interest across a wider pool and prioritise PSEs that draw strong bids at expected valuations, with structured investor feedback flagging procedural and regulatory hurdles early. Second, a rolling three-year privatisation stream, based on investor interest and the government’s strategic priorities, would give investors time for due diligence, which means deeper participation and better price discovery.

Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure. CII analysis suggests that bringing the government’s stake down to 51% across 95 listed PSEs could fetch about ₹9 lakh crore, with the government remaining the single largest shareholder. PSEs where the government holds 75% or less could be taken up in the first two years, followed by those with higher government holdings. A dedicated body, with a ministerial board, industry experts as advisers and a management team, could steer the process.

To be sure, none of the above makes a case for fiscal complacency. Deficits and public debt tend to rise in uncertain times and stay elevated long after the shock subsides. Staying on the path of fiscal prudence is essential to ensure that the government can continue investing in health and education without crowding out private investment.

Amidst various global headwinds, a healthy progress on disinvestments with more big-ticket sales such as the IDBI will provide the Centre the required cushion to stay on course with fiscal consolidation.
Chandrajit Banerjee is Director General, Confederation of Indian Industry

📈 Economy & Finance 📅 29 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Disinvestment as key economic strategy

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates

Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

However, disinvestment should not be seen merely as a tool for meeting fiscal targets. It is a policy choice aimed at unlocking greater value from public assets, widening public ownership, and improving efficiency and governance through greater market discipline. The 2022 LIC IPO which drew in many first-time retail investors and policyholders remains a prime example.

This was precisely the rationale behind the government’s 2021 New Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) Policy which envisages a “bare minimum presence” of PSEs in strategic sectors. Likewise, the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) re-engines capital via mature public assets. A target of ₹16.72 lakh crore has been set under NMP 2.0 for FY26-30 after having achieved 90% of its Phase 1 goal.

This year, however, until this month, receipts had come mainly through Offer for Sale (OFS) measures which help to broaden ownership but keep the status quo on an enterprise’s operations. The strategic sale of the IDBI Bank since Air India in 2022 is an encouraging sign. From an industry perspective, the IDBI sale is more than a one-off sale. It is one of the largest Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) deals in India’s financial sector and constitutes as the first step towards a ‘Privatisation 2.0’ framework. More importantly, this framework is premised on being investor-led, professionally managed and time-bound. Two changes would help to turn into a template.

First, the selection criteria for disinvestments of PSEs should move to a demand-based approach instead of being led by the government. It would work better to first gauge interest across a wider pool and prioritise PSEs that draw strong bids at expected valuations, with structured investor feedback flagging procedural and regulatory hurdles early. Second, a rolling three-year privatisation stream, based on investor interest and the government’s strategic priorities, would give investors time for due diligence, which means deeper participation and better price discovery.

Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure. CII analysis suggests that bringing the government’s stake down to 51% across 95 listed PSEs could fetch about ₹9 lakh crore, with the government remaining the single largest shareholder. PSEs where the government holds 75% or less could be taken up in the first two years, followed by those with higher government holdings. A dedicated body, with a ministerial board, industry experts as advisers and a management team, could steer the process.

To be sure, none of the above makes a case for fiscal complacency. Deficits and public debt tend to rise in uncertain times and stay elevated long after the shock subsides. Staying on the path of fiscal prudence is essential to ensure that the government can continue investing in health and education without crowding out private investment.

Amidst various global headwinds, a healthy progress on disinvestments with more big-ticket sales such as the IDBI will provide the Centre the required cushion to stay on course with fiscal consolidation.

Chandrajit Banerjee is Director General, Confederation of Indian Industry

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The 12-member FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation

The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market -- the Fed’s other mandate -- has been largely stable.
“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

articles.title: Pioneering U.S. labour leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Dolores Huerta took the reins of the U.S. farmworker movement in the 1960s with Chavez
Dolores Huerta, the U.S. labour leader and civil rights icon whose union work changed the lives of migrant workers, has died, her family said Wednesday (October 28, 2026). She was 96.

For nearly four decades, Huerta was vice president of United Farm Workers, the union she founded with Cesar Chavez, organising strikes and walkouts that won improvements in working conditions for the millions of men and women who labour in U.S. fields.
"We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," said a family statement.
"We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognise and celebrate her incredible life and legacy."
Erik Olvera, a spokesman for her family, told AFP on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) that Huerta died of cancer in the morning surrounded by loved ones.
Born in New Mexico and raised in California, Huerta took the reins of the U.S. farmworker movement in the 1960s with Chavez.
U.S. activists to raise funds to help agitating farmers
At the time, she was raising seven children -- she later had more -- while going through a divorce.
While Huerta was the organising force behind the union, Chavez was its charismatic leader and the public face who became an icon to generations on the left, even after his death in 1993.
But that fame and the seemingly tight relationship between him and Huerta hid a dark secret that came to light this year, when Huerta said she was one of a number of women Chavez had raped.

"The first time... I didn't feel I could say no because he was someone that I admired, my boss and the leader of the movement I had already devoted years of my life to," she said in a statement to the New York Times , which broke the story.
"The second time I was forced, against my will, and in an environment where I felt trapped."

articles.title: What has driven the high Arab turnout in Israel’s elections?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Arab voter turnout is estimated to be nearly 80%, the highest in at least a decade, according to exit polls

Israel’s October 27 legislative elections recorded a massive voter turnout of 77.7%, the highest since 1999. The country’s Arab citizens, who turned up in massive numbers to vote, remained one of the main factors, contributing to the surge.

While the official figures for voter turnout among Israeli Arabs are yet to be released by the Central Elections Committee, exit polls recorded by Channel 12 estimate Arab voter turnout to be nearly 80%. This implies that the voter turnout among Arab citizens in Israel would be the highest in at least a decade.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: What has driven the high Arab turnout in Israel’s elections?. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: India must build a holistic care system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework

India’s development story over the past decade has been one of infrastructure: highways, metro lines, electrification and digital public platforms, each treated as a foundation for growth that requires public investment and planning. One foundation on which every household and economy depends has not received the same attention: care.

Everyone needs care at some point in life. How care is organised shapes people’s opportunities, well-being and participation in society and the economy. When services are absent, families, and women most of all, bear the cost in unpaid work, lost earnings, and narrower opportunities.

In the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025, 44.4% of women outside the labour force cited childcare and homemaking as the main reason for staying out of the labour force. India’s Time Use Survey 2024 found that 41% of women aged 15–59 provided unpaid care, spending an average of 140 minutes a day on it. Expanding access to affordable, quality care services can give women greater freedom to pursue employment, leisure and participation in public life. With an ageing population, the need for accessible care services will only grow.

Yet care rarely features in India’s growth strategy. For a Viksit Bharat 2047, the question is not only how to expand women’s economic participation, but how to build the care system that makes such participation possible. The Anganwadi network, strengthened through Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, anchors early childhood care and nutrition. Palna, under Mission Shakti, supports crèches, while Mission Vatsalya, social security and provisions for persons with disabilities and senior citizens address other needs. The challenge is architecture, not ambition. Four gaps stand out.

First, fragmentation. Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework. This can leave gaps such as crèches that close before factory shifts end or eldercare needs that fall outside of existing schemes.

Second, coverage. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) estimates that 9–10 million women in low-income urban households need childcare. Similarly for eldercare, 24% of older persons face limitations in daily activities, while national data on service availability and coverage remain limited.

Third, the workforce. Care depends on frontline workers; from Anganwadi workers to home-based caregivers and domestic workers — many of whom remain inadequately remunerated or engaged on an honorary basis. Building on NITI Aayog’s proposals, clear standards, certification, decent working conditions, social protection and career pathways would recognise care as skilled and paid work.

Finally, financing and norms. Care is still budgeted as welfare rather than investment, and workplace policies assume that caregiving is women’s work. The Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) recommends statutory paid paternity leave in the private sector.

Comparable economies are building their own care ecosystems. Colombia’s 2025 National Care Policy brings 34 government entities under one framework. Brazil’s 2024 National Care Policy and 2025 National Care Plan set up inter-Ministerial committees to steer implementation. In Nepal, care mapping was used to fund care pilots.

In India, NITI Aayog’s Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047 report proposes a National Caregiving Council to strengthen coordination. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is consulting States and Union Territories; its May 2026 national workshop discussed a National Care Economy Mission with inter-Ministerial governance, aligned financing and shared data. State-level care roadmaps can make this practical. States can map needs, services and demographic trends, identify gaps in childcare, eldercare and disability support, and prepare costed plans with clear responsibilities.

Building on UNDP’s research and lessons from UN Women’s TransformCare initiative in more than 50 countries, the two agencies are supporting this agenda under government leadership, from mapping care services and skilling care workers to backing women-led childcare enterprises with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and Women Entrepreneurship Platform.

India has the programmes, policy vision and evidence. On this International Day of Care and Support, the task is to connect them, finance them and hold them to account: to build care the way India builds infrastructure.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 29 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

India must build a holistic care system

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework

India’s development story over the past decade has been one of infrastructure: highways, metro lines, electrification and digital public platforms, each treated as a foundation for growth that requires public investment and planning. One foundation on which every household and economy depends has not received the same attention: care.

Everyone needs care at some point in life. How care is organised shapes people’s opportunities, well-being and participation in society and the economy. When services are absent, families, and women most of all, bear the cost in unpaid work, lost earnings, and narrower opportunities.

In the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025, 44.4% of women outside the labour force cited childcare and homemaking as the main reason for staying out of the labour force. India’s Time Use Survey 2024 found that 41% of women aged 15–59 provided unpaid care, spending an average of 140 minutes a day on it. Expanding access to affordable, quality care services can give women greater freedom to pursue employment, leisure and participation in public life. With an ageing population, the need for accessible care services will only grow.

Yet care rarely features in India’s growth strategy. For a Viksit Bharat 2047, the question is not only how to expand women’s economic participation, but how to build the care system that makes such participation possible. The Anganwadi network, strengthened through Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, anchors early childhood care and nutrition. Palna, under Mission Shakti, supports crèches, while Mission Vatsalya, social security and provisions for persons with disabilities and senior citizens address other needs. The challenge is architecture, not ambition. Four gaps stand out.

First, fragmentation. Care is split across multiple Ministries, from women and child development to housing and urban affairs. Each runs valuable programmes, but without a common framework. This can leave gaps such as crèches that close before factory shifts end or eldercare needs that fall outside of existing schemes.

Second, coverage. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) estimates that 9–10 million women in low-income urban households need childcare. Similarly for eldercare, 24% of older persons face limitations in daily activities, while national data on service availability and coverage remain limited.

Third, the workforce. Care depends on frontline workers; from Anganwadi workers to home-based caregivers and domestic workers — many of whom remain inadequately remunerated or engaged on an honorary basis. Building on NITI Aayog’s proposals, clear standards, certification, decent working conditions, social protection and career pathways would recognise care as skilled and paid work.

Finally, financing and norms. Care is still budgeted as welfare rather than investment, and workplace policies assume that caregiving is women’s work. The Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) recommends statutory paid paternity leave in the private sector.

Comparable economies are building their own care ecosystems. Colombia’s 2025 National Care Policy brings 34 government entities under one framework. Brazil’s 2024 National Care Policy and 2025 National Care Plan set up inter-Ministerial committees to steer implementation. In Nepal, care mapping was used to fund care pilots.

In India, NITI Aayog’s Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047 report proposes a National Caregiving Council to strengthen coordination. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is consulting States and Union Territories; its May 2026 national workshop discussed a National Care Economy Mission with inter-Ministerial governance, aligned financing and shared data. State-level care roadmaps can make this practical. States can map needs, services and demographic trends, identify gaps in childcare, eldercare and disability support, and prepare costed plans with clear responsibilities.

Building on UNDP’s research and lessons from UN Women’s TransformCare initiative in more than 50 countries, the two agencies are supporting this agenda under government leadership, from mapping care services and skilling care workers to backing women-led childcare enterprises with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and Women Entrepreneurship Platform.

India has the programmes, policy vision and evidence. On this International Day of Care and Support, the task is to connect them, finance them and hold them to account: to build care the way India builds infrastructure.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India has the programmes, policy vision and evidence. On this International Day of Care and Support, the task is to connect them, finance them and hold them to account: to build care the way India builds infrastructure.

articles.title: Chennai Corporation council meeting: streetlight maintenance across 12 zones proposed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The work includes the daily monitoring of streetlights, repairing faulty lights within 24 hours of receiving complaints from officials or the public, and maintaining feeder boxes, junction boxes, poles and associated electrical components

The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has proposed to maintain 2,33,267 streetlights and 443 high-mast lights across 12 zones for one year, excluding the cost of materials. This was stated at the GCC general council meeting chaired by Mayor R. Priya and attended by Commissioner G.S. Sameeran on Thursday (October 29, 2026), at Ripon Buildings.

The maintenance work would cover the following 12 zones – Tiruvottiyur, Manali, Madhavaram, Tondiarpet, Thiru-Vi-Ka Nagar, Ambattur, Teynampet, Kodambakkam, Valasaravakkam, Alandur, Perungudi, and Sholinganallur.

The work includes the daily monitoring of streetlights, repairing faulty lights within 24 hours of receiving complaints from officials or the public, and maintaining feeder boxes, junction boxes, poles and associated electrical components. The contractor will also have to provide the required workforce, vehicles fitted with aluminium or hydraulic ladders, and other facilities needed for the work, according to the resolution.
In addition, streetlights in Ambattur Zone, which has 28,417 streetlight poles and 69 high-mast lights, would be maintained at a cost of ₹5.01 crore for one year, the resolution mentioned.

The contractor will have to ensure that lights are switched on and off according to the GCC’s schedule and submit reports every 15 days. Penalties will apply for delayed repairs, staff shortages and failure to provide vehicles in proper working condition, according to the proposed resolution.
Notably, the Chennai Corporation had identified 2,079 streetlights that were not functioning during a city-wide night inspection recently.
The inspection was conducted to ensure that all 3,11,285 streetlights in the city remained operational, on September 16, 2026, following the Commissioner’s directions.

articles.title: Opposition leaders, activists urge SEC to delay Bengal civic polls till SSR to enrol voters is complete
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several Opposition leaders and activists on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) met the State Election Commissioner Krishna Gupta and urged to delay the upcoming municipality polls in West Bengal till the ongoing Special Summary Revision (SSR) exercise is not over.

Amid the recent protests across the country against the special intensive revision (SIR) and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Election Commission of India (ECI) declared the SSR exercise on October 15 across 17 States and Union Territories to include the new voters and also the ones left out during SIR.
The draft roll of the SSR is likely to be published on November 12 while the final roll will be out on January 4.
Editorial | A necessary corrective: On the SSR, the special summary revision of electoral rolls
However, the election for the civic bodies is likely to be held in several municipalities including in Kolkata and Howrah that worried the leaders.

Citing the large-scale deletion of voters in the State during the SIR, the delegation of Opposition leaders and civil rights groups said that around 1.2 lakh appeals for the inclusion under the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) area are pending before the Tribunal. The corresponding figure is about 39,000 within the jurisdiction of Howrah Municipal Corporation.
In a memorandum submitted to the SEC, they said that 100% of the appeals in Kolkata and 99% of the appeals in Howrah, so far disposed by the Tribunal have been decided in favour of inclusion.

"Hence, excluding around 1.6 takh Tribunal Appellants in KMC and HMC jurisdictions from the electoral roll for the above-mentioned municipal corporation or municipality elections-would disenfranchise them for the second time, after the Assembly polls," the delegation said in its memorandum to Mr. Gupta.

They have urged the SEC to conduct the civic bodies elections only after the completion of the SSR exercise on January 4 or such other extended date as decided by ECI. Meanwhile, they have also requested the SEC to excercise its statutory powers to include the names of all Tribunal appellants to the electoral rolls of KMC and HMC and other municipal corporations or municipalities for the election.

The letter included the signatures of Congress State president Subhankar Sarkar, MP Saugata Roy, former Rajya Sabha MP Jawahar Sircar, Communist Party of (Marxist-Leninist) (Liberation) leader Palash Ghosh, advocate and activist Avik Saha, economoist Prasenjit Bose, human rights activist Sujato Bhadra etc.

articles.title: SCR digital life certificate drive from November 1 to 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pensioners can submit their annual life certificates through digital process without visiting pension disbursing offices

South Central Railway (SCR) will launch the Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 5.0 across its jurisdiction from November 1 to 30, enabling pensioners to submit their annual life certificates through a simple digital process without visiting pension disbursing offices.

The campaign is aimed at ensuring the seamless continuation of pension payments through Aadhaar-based biometric authentication and facial recognition technology. Under the initiative, pensioners can submit their life certificates using smartphones by installing the “Aadhaar Face RD (Early Access)” application developed by UIDAI and the “Jeevan Pramaan” application available on the Google Play Store.

After completing the authentication process, pensioners will be required to provide details such as their name as per Aadhaar, type of pension, pension payment order (PPO) number, pension account number, sanctioning authority and disbursing agency details.

Once the required information is entered and the declaration is accepted, the application will generate a Digital Life Certificate. Following successful authentication, pensioners will receive an SMS containing a Jeevan Pramaan ID (Pramaan ID) and a link through which the certificate can be downloaded and accessed online.

The digital facility eliminates the need for pensioners, particularly senior citizens and those with mobility challenges, to physically visit pension offices every year for verification. The campaign posters were unveiled by SCR Principal Financial Adviser Hema Suneetha, as per a press release issued on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

articles.title: India ready to share 'battle-tested' anti-terror expertise with ASEAN, its dialogue partners: Rajnath Singh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Defence Minister flagged concerns over disruptions in certain maritime trade routes and asserted that India will continue to act as a "trusted net security provider" in the Indian Ocean region and the wider Indo-Pacific

India is ready to share its "battle-tested" counter-terror expertise with ASEAN and its dialogue partners, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday (October 29, 2026) as he described Operation Sindoor as a declaration of New Delhi's clear approach against state-sponsored terrorist activities.
The Defence Minister also said that India supports an Indo-Pacific that is secure and resilient -- one where peace and stability are not merely aspirations, but the outcome of collective efforts.

In an address at a conclave of defence ministers of ASEAN member states and the bloc's dialogue partners in Cebu in the Philippines, he flagged concerns over disruptions in certain maritime trade routes and asserted that India will continue to act as a "trusted net security provider" in the Indian Ocean region and the wider Indo-Pacific.

"Today, when global trade routes are facing new types of international threats, merely issuing statements on maritime security is not enough," he said at the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting Plus (ADMM-Plus) conclave.

However, what drew more attention was Mr. Singh's call for concerted efforts to combat terrorism. "India is fully prepared to share its practical and battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ADMM-Plus partners," he said.
"Through joint military exercises, capacity-building programmes, and robust intelligence sharing, we can further strengthen our collective capabilities," he added.

The Defence Minister said that a major example of India's approach against terrorism was last year's Operation Sindoor when a large number of terrorist infrastructures were destroyed. "This was also a declaration of India's clear approach against state-sponsored terror," he said.

India's experience in the field of counter-terrorism is not just classroom or theoretical knowledge, but rather an experience gained over decades while confronting cross-border security challenges, he said, referring to Pakistan's use of terrorism against India.
"Every strategy of ours against terrorism has been tested and proven in actual operations and has demonstrated its success," he said.

Mr. Singh also outlined India's vision for the Indo-Pacific. "We support an Indo-Pacific that is secure and resilient -- one where peace and stability are not merely aspirations, but the outcome of our collective efforts," he said.

He said India considers maritime security to be an issue connected to peace, security, and prosperity in the region. "India's emphasis on the rule of law, and particularly on the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), as well as its advocacy for freedom of navigation and overflight, is not against any country. Rather, its purpose is to protect the collective interests of all regional stakeholders," he said.

Mr. Singh’s remarks came amid consistent demands by several ASEAN member states as well as democratic nations for adherence to UNCLOS in the face of Beijing's increasing military muscle flexing in the contested South China Sea.

The Defence Minister said that a major example of India's approach against terrorism was last year's Operation Sindoor when a large number of terrorist infrastructures were destroyed. "This was also a declaration of India's clear approach against state-sponsored terror," he said.

India's experience in the field of counter-terrorism is not just classroom or theoretical knowledge, but rather an experience gained over decades while confronting cross-border security challenges, he said, referring to Pakistan's use of terrorism against India.

"Every strategy of ours against terrorism has been tested and proven in actual operations and has demonstrated its success," he said.

Mr. Singh also outlined India's vision for the Indo-Pacific. "We support an Indo-Pacific that is secure and resilient -- one where peace and stability are not merely aspirations, but the outcome of our collective efforts," he said.

He said India considers maritime security to be an issue connected to peace, security, and prosperity in the region. "India's emphasis on the rule of law, and particularly on the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), as well as its advocacy for freedom of navigation and overflight, is not against any country. Rather, its purpose is to protect the collective interests of all regional stakeholders," he said.

Mr. Singh’s remarks came amid consistent demands by several ASEAN member states as well as democratic nations for adherence to UNCLOS in the face of Beijing's increasing military muscle flexing in the contested South China Sea.

articles.title: How brown mussels sustain livelihoods along Thiruvananthapuram’s coast
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: From the auctions at Vizhinjam fishing harbour to seafood markets across the region, brown mussels sustain a community of divers whose livelihoods depend on the sea and its seasonal bounty

A few minutes before nine in the morning, colourful catamarans streaked with blue, green and crimson glide into Vizhinjam fishing harbour, nearly 16 kilometres from Thiruvananthapuram city. Powered by motors or wooden oars, they carry wicker baskets piled with brown-shelled mussels, still speckled with dirt and barnacles.

As the boats reach the shore, the fisherfolk get to work. Two labourers carry each overflowing basket to the centre of the market, where the day’s catch is auctioned. Within seconds, bidding begins, with one lot eventually fetching ₹15,000.
An auction process for mussels in progress at Vizhinjam harbour | Photo Credit: NIRMAL HARINDRAN

Along Thiruvananthapuram’s rocky coast, mussel harvesting peaks between September and February. Fishers collect the shellfish between 6am and 10am, diving underwater with broad metal knives to pry them off rocks. Depending on the location, they either head out in boats or dive straight into the sea from the rocks.

Babu Sukumaran, 61, has been diving for mussels since he was 15. He emerges with a cloth sack of mussels tied around his waist. Up close, his body is covered in bleeding cuts. “Our bodies have many wounds. But these don’t hurt me, and they dry up quickly in the saline water,” he says.
Babu Sukumaran, a seasoned diver | Photo Credit: NIRMAL HARINDRAN

According to Jasmine K, president of the Diving Workers Welfare Society, more than 280 people harvest and trade brown mussels in Vizhinjam alone. Divers also collect them from Kovalam, Azhimala, Poonthura and Muthalappozhi, among other coastal areas. But the work depends on the sea’s temperament. “Our job depends on how peaceful or turbulent the sea is. When the waves are high, we can’t go in,” says Balu Kovalam, a veteran diver with 20 years of experience. He earns ₹2,000 daily collecting the shellfish.
A fisherman returning from the inter tidal rocky area of Kovalam coast | Photo Credit: NIRMAL HARINDRAN

“In Keralam, two types of mussels are found — green and brown,” says MK Anil, principal scientist at the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CMFRI) unit in Vizhinjam. Brown mussels (Perna indica or Perna perna ) occur along the coast from Kollam district to Tiruchendur in Tamil Nadu, while green mussels ( Perna viridis ) are found elsewhere.

In Kannur, Kozhikode and Kasaragod, green mussels are cultivated in lakes because they can tolerate low-salinity water. “However, due to the rise in the construction of sea walls, we are witnessing a rise in green mussels in Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam,” says Anil, who has researched mussels for over a decade. The two varieties also differ in texture: brown mussels are soft and fleshy, while green mussels are firmer.

In Thiruvananthapuram, mussels have been largely a part of the coastal diet. “Mussels steamed with sweet potatoes is a delicacy. They are also fried, roasted and made into thoran ,” says Jasmine. In northern Keralam, where mussels are known as kadukka , they are extremely popular . One local favourite is arikadukka , a snack made by stuffing the shells with spiced rice-and-coconut dough and steaming them.
A fisher woman sorting the day's mussels catch at Kovalam coast | Photo Credit: NIRMAL HARINDRAN

articles.title: Karnataka SIR: 64.5 lakh voters potentially missing in rolls, majority of them young
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Elector-to-population ratio released officially by Karnataka CEO shows under-enrolment of about 64.5 lakh electors, of whom roughly 38.41 lakh are in the 18 to 29 age group.

Around 64.5 lakh electors are potentially missing from the final electoral rolls of Karnataka released after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), based on the Elector-to-Population (E-to-P) ratio of 66.11 released by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO).

The State’s E-to-P ratio quoted in the CEO’s statements was calculated as the ratio between the total number of electors on the rolls and the estimated population in 2026 in all age groups, including those below 18 years of age and not eligible to vote.

articles.title: U.S. judge rejects Trump administration’s interference in California midterm vote
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Those registered on California’s voter roles “must not be deprived of a core right merely because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors,” U.S. District Judge David O. Carter said

A federal judge on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) rejected the U.S. Department of Justice's efforts to set aside the ballots of more than 20,000 California voters it said might not be citizens , slamming the move as brazen pre-election "interference."

The case sparked an uproar ahead of the November 3 midterms, in which President Donald Trump's Republican Party is at risk of losing its control of Congress, and appears to represent another attempt to cast doubt on electoral results.
Democratic Party leaders have sued the Trump administration over the request, accusing Republicans of aiming "threats and intimidation" at State and local officials before the vote.
U.S. District Judge David O. Carter agreed, refusing to order the seizure of the ballots and siding with the Government of Democratic-led California.
Donald Trump rallies on Republican turf as midterm fears mount

"Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a State and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch," Mr. Carter wrote in his decision.
"Constitutional rights and our democracy are at stake. The public interest favors their protection," he added.
Those registered on California's voter roles "must not be deprived of a core right merely because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors."
The federal government in recent months had accused California of having 1,90,000 illegal voters on its books.
It recently revised the figure to 20,000 and filed an emergency lawsuit about 10 days ago, after early voting had begun, to stop the State from sending ballots to them.

A similar controversy arose in neighboring Nevada, where the allegations fizzled. The Trump administration had initially identified 16,000 non-citizen voters there, but after verification procedures that number dropped to 185, and then to zero.
"The DOJ's actions are indicative of a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference by federal officials," Mr. Carter wrote in his decision.

articles.title: At least 68 dead after two trains collide in Spain’s Toledo Province
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The second such accident to strike Spain this year will raise fresh questions about the country’s rail safety, with the Transport Minister speaking of an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that led to the collision.

A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed at least 68 people and injured scores more on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), with the toll likely to rise, authorities said, in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century.

The second such accident to strike Spain in 2026 will raise fresh questions about the country’s rail safety, with the Transport Minister speaking of an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that led to the collision.

AFP reporters on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha saw one train embedded into another and some carriages lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment.
Dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour.
ALSO WATCH Deadly train collision in Spain: What we know so far
Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene that 68 people had died, raising an earlier toll of 64 and having already warned of more victims being found.
A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha regional government told AFP that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition.

State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo.

People check an information screen displaying a message that the high-speed train line between Madrid and Andalucia has been interrupted following the collision of two high-speed trains between the towns of Mora and Orgaz at Atocha train station in Madrid, Spain, on October 28, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters
Pablo Mejia, 42, with blood staining his grey jumper, told AFP that he had miraculously survived after changing his seat, as he awaited a transfer to the southern city of Seville.
He recounted “a very strong hit. It lasted a long time until it stopped, lots of people on the floor, on top of each other, seats ripped out, suitcases, a lot of chaos”.
A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz who lives in the village of Urda close to the site of the accident, around 130km south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Flavio Bolsonaro said; U.S. President Donald Trump said he “won’t get involved” in Mr. Bolsonaro’s claim

Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) he is his country's rightful leader, after fleeing to the United States to start a self-imposed exile.

Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's defiance on arrival in Florida signalled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election on Sunday (October 25, 2026).

"I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil's election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny," Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming "electoral fraud."
"I will lead the opposition from here," he said. In a subsequent statement, he revised his claim, saying he is the "leader," rather than "president."
Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, touched down earlier on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) in a private jet at Opa-Locka Executive Airport near Miami.

Rogerio Marinho, the leader of Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's Liberal Party in the Senate, told reporters in Brasilia that he was in "solidarity" with the former candidate, describing him as a "political exile."
However, he distanced himself from Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's statement, and refused to back up claims of electoral fraud.
"The Liberal Party cannot make that claim," he said. "There is no evidence of that."
Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro "is an expression of the right in Brazil today...he calls himself a leader and it's true: he's a leader," Mr. Marinho told reporters.

U.S. President Donald Trump's hard-right administration has strong links to Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro and his father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.
Mr. Trump reiterated his stand that Brazil's election was "very strange" but told reporters he "won't get involved" in Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's claim to the presidency.
Details of how Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to U.S. soil are still emerging.
