articles.title: AI summit: How AI is reshaping agriculture and gender dynamics in the global south
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: At the India AI Impact Summit 2026, conversations were largely dominated by debates over existential risks, technological singularity, and the automation of white-collar work. Yet, quietly released alongside the main-stage panels were a series of AI Impact Casebooks that told a markedly different story. Among them, the AI Impact Casebooks on Agriculture and Gender Empowerment stand out not for their futuristic speculation, but for their gritty, first-mile pragmatism.

Developed by the IndiaAI Mission in collaboration with UN Women, For All Women and Girls, the World Bank, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICMR), the AIAIC, and Wadhwani AI, these compendia prove that AI’s most profound impact is happening far from Silicon Valley. It is happening in the sugarcane fields of Maharashtra and the rural courts for domestic violence survivors. These casebooks demonstrate that when AI is purposefully directed at structural inequalities, it ceases to be a mere tool for efficiency and becomes an instrument for profound systemic equity.

Agriculture in the Global South is a high-stakes gamble against forces smallholder farmers cannot control: erratic monsoons, invisible soil chemistry, and fragmented markets. Furthermore, traditional agricultural extension systems are severely strained; in some parts of Sub-Saharan Africa, the ratio of extension agents to farmers is as staggering as 1:50,000, leaving millions without timely guidance. The Agriculture Casebook showcases how AI is stepping in to bridge this massive intelligence gap.

Rather than relying on generic, season-wide crop calendars, AI is delivering hyper-localised, precision agronomy. Take MapMyCrop, an AI platform monitoring sugarcane farms across India. By fusing multi-sensor satellite imagery with super-resolution algorithms, it acts as a digital twin for farms, predicting the precise 15-day window when sucrose levels will peak. This has helped farmers boost yields from the traditional 98-148 tonnes per hectare to up to 358 tonnes—a staggering 57% improvement.

Similarly, the Chemistry-Aware Crop Yield Prediction system by Alt Carbon bypasses the limitations of traditional soil testing. By employing physics-guided machine learning and multi-temporal satellite data, it reads the invisible chemical makeup of soil to detect hidden toxicities and nutrient imbalances, allowing farmers to reduce nitrogen use by 28% while boosting yields.

For the average smallholder, accessing this intelligence is as simple and affordable as making a phone call. Platforms such as Maharashtra’s MahaVISTAAR and Africa’s FarmAdvice employ natural language processing and voice-first interfaces to mitigate literacy barriers. Farmers simply speak in their local dialects to receive expert-vetted advice on pest outbreaks or weather anomalies, democratising predictive capabilities that were once the exclusive domain of massive agribusinesses.

If the Agriculture Casebook addresses the seed-to-harvest journey, the Gender Empowerment Casebook addresses the socio-cultural one. Developed with UN Women and For All Women and Girls from a pool of over 235 global submissions, this compendium showcases 23 case studies that shatter the myth that technology is inherently gender-neutral. When AI systems are not designed with the lived realities of women and girls in mind, they often replicate and amplify existing exclusions.

The solutions highlighted here actively reverse this trend by embedding gender-responsiveness directly into their product design and engineering constraints. In the realm of justice, NyayaSakhi-SWATI is an AI-supported legal assistant deployed in Maharashtra to guide survivors of domestic violence. Trained on women-specific legal judgments, it helps women privately understand their rights, likely legal remedies, and case timelines before they ever set foot in a courtroom or pay a lawyer.

In education, the AtenIA initiative in Peru is actively combatting the cultural stereotypes that exclude girls from STEM fields. Using a phygital model—blending physical books with a cloud-hosted conversational AI—the system mentors young girls, intentionally redirecting biased prompts to highlight women’s leadership in engineering and science. The results speak for themselves: participants’ intention to pursue STEM careers jumped from 9% to 76%.

Safety in the digital age is also a critical frontier. The YASHODA AI program is rolling out across India to build AI safety literacy among women. Through localised, peer-led training, it teaches women in rural and semi-urban areas how to identify AI-driven harms like deepfakes and financial scams, translating digital rights from abstract concepts into practical self-defense.

Perhaps the most compelling narrative emerges where these two sectors intersect. Women contribute over 60% of agricultural labour in India, yet receive only 6% of formal credit and are systematically excluded from digital advisory services.

Innovations like the MetsaQ platform are deliberately rewiring this dynamic. Operating in states like Odisha, MetsaQ uses small language models to deliver voice-based agricultural advisories. Because it was designed with intentional inclusion—partnering with women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and ensuring offline functionality—42% of its users in Odisha are women. By giving women farmers verifiable digital records of their farming activities, the platform has helped 34% of participating farmers access formal credit, compared to a baseline of just 11%.

articles.title: Former MLA Muthukumar surrenders in bribery case involving ex-Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Wednesday dismissed his anticipatory bail petition, following which he surrendered on Thursday morning

A special court in Chennai on Thursday (October 29, 2026) remanded until November 12, former MLA Muthukumar, a co-accused who surrendered in the alleged bribery linked to school approvals during the tenure of former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi (DMK).

The Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Greater Chennai City Police registered the case following allegations that crores of rupees were collected during the previous DMK regime in exchange for granting recognition and other approvals to private schools. The police have claimed to have evidence of the irregularities.

The prime accused in the case, B.T. Arasakumar, was arrested and remained in prison for more than 90 days before securing conditional bail. Mr. Poyyamozhi was arrested on October 26 and remanded in judicial custody.

Mr. Muthukumar, considered a key player in the alleged scam and a close associate of Mr. Poyyamozhi, had been absconding. He was elected an MLA from the DMDK and later joined the DMK. The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) dismissed his anticipatory bail petition, following which he surrendered before Judge L.S. Sathyamurthy of the Special Court for Prevention of Corruption Act cases in Chennai on Thursday morning.

During the proceedings, his counsel sought first-class facilities in prison, submitting that Muthukumar was an income-tax assessee and was entitled to such privileges. Accepting the plea, the judge directed the prison authorities to provide him with first-class accommodation and medical assistance, if required.
Meanwhile, the same court directed the CCB police to file their response to the bail petition moved by Mr. Poyyamozhi, who is lodged in Puzhal Central Prison.

The CCB police filed a separate petition seeking five days of police custody to interrogate him. The police said they needed to question the former Minister about his alleged links with Mr. Muthukumar, the identities of those who paid money and the amounts collected from each of them. They also sought to establish the role of other alleged intermediaries and trace the money trail.
The bail petition came up for hearing before Judge Sathyamurthy on Thursday. The police sought time to file their response, following which the judge adjourned the hearing to Monday (November 2).
The court also adjourned to Monday the hearing on a separate petition filed by Mr. Poyyamozhi seeking the return of electronic devices seized during searches at his residence.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28) dismissed his anticipatory bail petition, following which he surrendered before Judge L.S. Sathyamurthy of the Special Court for Prevention of Corruption Act cases in Chennai on Thursday morning.

During the proceedings, his counsel sought first-class facilities in prison, submitting that Muthukumar was an income-tax assessee and was entitled to such privileges. Accepting the plea, the judge directed the prison authorities to provide him with first-class accommodation and medical assistance, if required.

Meanwhile, the same court directed the CCB police to file their response to the bail petition moved by Mr. Poyyamozhi, who is lodged in Puzhal Central Prison.

The CCB police filed a separate petition seeking five days of police custody to interrogate him. The police said they needed to question the former Minister about his alleged links with Mr. Muthukumar, the identities of those who paid money and the amounts collected from each of them. They also sought to establish the role of other alleged intermediaries and trace the money trail.

The bail petition came up for hearing before Judge Sathyamurthy on Thursday. The police sought time to file their response, following which the judge adjourned the hearing to Monday (November 2).

The court also adjourned to Monday the hearing on a separate petition filed by Mr. Poyyamozhi seeking the return of electronic devices seized during searches at his residence.

articles.title: CPI(M) leader P. Jayarajan condemns online attacks against Mammootty, says Wayanad visit issue was ‘resolved long ago’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a social media post, Jayarajan said the attempt to revive “an old misunderstanding” and use it to abuse and target the actor was driven by vested interests

CPI(M) State Secretariat member P. Jayarajan has condemned the online attacks targeting actor Mammootty and Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) and Students Federation of India (SFI) leaders who recently visited him, stating that the controversy linked to the Wayanad township visit had been “settled amicably long ago.”

In a social media post, Mr. Jayarajan said the attempt to revive “an old misunderstanding” and use it to abuse and target the actor was driven by vested interests. He maintained that the issue involving Mammootty and CPI(M) Wayanad district secretary K. Rafeeq had been resolved through discussions at the time and that their friendship was well known to the public.

“Mammootty does not belong within the confines of any single political party but is a public figure cherished by people across Keralam. His interactions and friendship should not be judged through political divisions,” Mr. Jayarajan said.
He also defended the DYFI and SFI leaders who visited Mammootty at his invitation, saying that turning the meeting into a controversy reflected a narrow political outlook.

Mr. Jayarajan noted that the student and youth organisations had “earned recognition at the national level through their struggles for democracy and against saffronisation”, and described Mammootty’s willingness to meet their leaders as a recognition of their work.

The controversy had erupted after Mammootty, in March 2026, visited the Wayanad Model Township built for survivors of the 2024 Mundakkai-Chooralmala landslides. During the visit, a video purportedly showed the actor asking Mr. Rafeeq not to remain beside him as people might assume that the visit was organised on behalf of the party.

The footage triggered a wave of criticism on social media, with some Left-leaning accounts targeting the actor. Mr. Rafeeq subsequently clarified that Mammootty had contacted him personally to explain his remarks and appealed to people to end the controversy.

Mr. Jayarajan said that launching personal attacks while claiming to represent the Left was “contrary to Left politics.” He cautioned against attempts to create misunderstandings and provide political opponents with opportunities to exploit the situation.

Emphasising the Left’s cultural values, Mr. Jayarajan said that respecting art and standing by artists were integral to communist culture. He urged those misled by false campaigns to withdraw from them and called for an end to the online attacks against the actor.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab LIVE: New Bay system likely to head for Andhra coast; 300 villages marooned in Ganjam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Arnab’s remnant brings rain to West Bengal, Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh after weakening into a depression

The Indian Coast Guard has airlifted 13 crew members from the Sigma Pearl, a Marshall Islands-flagged bulk carrier stranded off Antarvedi in Konaseema district, an official release said on Thursday. A helicopter operation to rescue the remaining seven was under way. The rescued crew have been taken aboard the Coast Guard vessel Sujay. The 180-metre ship had left Visakhapatnam for Singapore and was caught in the rough sea during Cyclone Arnab.- PTI

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu conducted an aerial survey of flooded paddy, banana and coconut plantations and aqua ponds in Krishna, West Godavari and Konaseema districts on Thursday to assess the damage from Cyclone Arnab.

An Indian Coast Guard helicopter began rescuing stranded people in Odisha’s Ganjam district on Thursday afternoon, the State’s Special Relief Commissioner told PTI. Fifty-four teams from the NDRF, the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and the Fire Service are also working on the ground.

Srikakulam district got the most rain in Andhra Pradesh in the 24 hours to 8.30 a.m. on Thursday, according to the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES-AP). Kanchili mandal recorded 248.5 mm, and gauges in Ichchapuram recorded between 218 mm and 238 mm. The district as a whole averaged about 102 mm.

In the 24 hours to 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28), the heaviest rain had fallen further south, in Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram. Thirty-nine stations there got more than 204.5 mm, which falls in the ‘extremely heavy’ category.
Thursday has been much drier. By 3 p.m., Palasa had the most rain in the State, at about 41 mm. u3FMp-rainfall-over-andhra-pradesh-on-oct.-28-2026-.png
u3FMp-rainfall-over-andhra-pradesh-on-oct.-28-2026-.png

The swollen Bahuda has forced the railways to cancel nine trains and divert 14 on the Howrah-Chennai route on Thursday, the East Coast Railway said. The Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam Vande Bharat Express, the Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam Intercity Express and the Visakha Express to Secunderabad are among those cancelled. Water is flowing above the danger mark at two railway bridges between Ichchapuram and Jhadupudi.
About 550 mm of rain in Odisha’s Ganjam district pushed the Baghalati dam on the Bahuda past its danger mark, the railway said. - PTI

The weather system now over the Andaman Sea is expected to gather strength in the next two days, the IMD said on Thursday. By around October 31, it should grow into a depression. After that, it is likely to strengthen further and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast over the following two days.
What is left of Arnab, meanwhile, has moved deep inland. It was about 110 km south of Raipur in Chhattisgarh by late Thursday morning, IMD said.

Nine districts in eastern Madhya Pradesh could get heavy to very heavy rain and winds of 40 to 50 kmph on Thursday, IMD Bhopal meteorologist V.S. Yadav said. Affected districts include Sidhi, Singrauli, Rewa, Mauganj, Satna, Maihar, Shahdol, Umaria and Anuppur. The weakened system will not enter Madhya Pradesh and is moving towards Bihar, Mr. Yadav told PTI . The weather in eastern Madhya Pradesh is expected to clear by Saturday.

articles.title: Telangana artists to raise awareness on El Nino impact, precautionary measures
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana government will extensively utilise skills of Telangana Samskruthika Sarathi artists, the official cultural wing of the government, to raise public awareness about the potential impacts of El Nino , including rainfall deficiency and water scarcity, said Tourism and Culture Minister Jupally Krishna Rao on Thursday (October 29, 2026).

The Minister asked officials to use songs, plays and traditional folk art forms to educate people, particularly in rural areas , about the possible challenges posed by the climatic phenomenon and the need to take precautionary measures. Artists will communicate these messages through cultural performances to make them accessible and easily understandable to the public.

He stressed the importance of promoting the judicious use of water, energy conservation and the adoption of cropping patterns suited to prevailing climatic conditions. Noting that Telangana Samskruthika Sarathi artists were unavailable in some districts, Mr. Rao directed officials to deploy artists from other districts to areas facing a shortage of performers.
Following the Minister’s directions, the Department of Language and Culture has assigned 18 Telangana Samskruthika Sarathi artists to conduct awareness programmes in Hyderabad district.

articles.title: U.K. PM Andy Burnham's trip to India could take place soon: British Envoy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is keen to visit India and a trip could take place soon, a top U.K. diplomat said on Thursday (October 29, 2026), highlighting the growing partnership between the two countries.

Speaking to PTI, Acting British High Commissioner to India Ben Mellor said Mr. Burnham had conveyed his desire to visit India during a conversation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi after taking office. “I know that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is very keen to come to India," Mr. Mellor said.
"When he and Prime Minister Modi spoke just after he took office as prime minister, he expressed that directly to the prime minister, and I'm sure we'll be able to see that happen soon,” he added.
Mr. Burnham was appointed as prime minister on July 20 this year.
On the India-U.K. economic ties, Mr. Mellor expressed confidence that the two countries would surpass their target of doubling bilateral trade as their economies continue to grow.
The Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force 100 days ago. But actually it was signed just over a year ago. Since then we've already seen new deals worth 12 billion pounds, he said.
Comment | An anchor for India-U.K. ties, their economic partnership
“I have every confidence that as the UK and the Indian economies grow, we will surpass the target of doubling trade between our two countries,” Mr. Mellor added.
India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030.

Mr. Mellor also said the U.K. remained strongly welcoming to Indian businesses and investors, noting that Indian investors had been the second-largest source of new investment projects in the country over the past several years.

He said the India-U.K. Free Trade Agreement (FTA) had further improved the environment for businesses seeking to invest, trade and work across the two countries. “Just two weeks ago, seven mayors from the UK and one local authority brought a large business delegation of over 200 businesses to India to come and look for partners that they could work with,” Mr. Mellor said.
He said the measures announced in Wednesday's U.K. Budget had reinforced that approach by seeking to make the British economy predictable and attractive for investment.

articles.title: Sada ‘Master’, ace guitarist who enriched Ilaiyaraaja’s compositions, dies at 80
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “I am saddened by Sadanandam’s death. He was with me from the early days,” Ilaiyaraaja said in a message
S. Sadanandam, popularly known as Sada ‘Master’, whose guitar enriched many of the finest compositions of Isaignani Ilaiyaraaja, died in Chennai on Thursday (October 29, 2026). He was 80.

Sada ‘Master’ was among the musicians who began working with Ilaiyaraaja in the mid-1970s, starting with Annakili, released in 1976. Both were students of Dhanraj ‘Master’, who trained several accomplished instrumentalists in Tamil Nadu, including A.R. Rahman.
Sada would appear with Ilaiyaraaja and his drummer Purusothaman in the song, Madai Thiranthu Thaavum Nathi Alai Naan in the film Nizhalgal.
Sada ‘Master’ (extreme right) | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

“I am saddened by Sadanandam’s death. He was with me from the early days. I do not see them as dead, as they lived with me and were an integral part of my life. I pray to God that his soul rests in peace,” Ilaiyaraaja said in a message.

Sada ‘Master’ belonged to a family of musicians. His father was the late music director R. Sudarsanam, popularly known as Sudarsanam ‘Master’, who worked as a music director for AVM Studios. His uncle was Govardhan ‘Master’.

Though Sada ‘Master’ attributed his success to Ilaiyaraaja, who meticulously wrote every notation and specified the dynamics, leaving little room for deviation, he had an exceptional understanding of what each composition demanded. His contribution to background scores and theme music speaks volumes about his talent.

Decades later, his guitar passages in songs such as En Iniya Pon Nilave , Vaadi En Kappa Kizhange , Entha Poovilum Vaasam Undu , Raja Raja Chozhan Naan , and Chinna Raasave continue to ring in listeners’ ears. And who can forget the iconic guitar passage in the Hindi song Chura Liya Hai Tumne ?

His guitar could sound like a veena. Ilaiyaraaja used guitar passages in place of the veena in songs such as Thendral Vandhu Ennai Thodum and Aagaya Vennilave . The background scores and interludes continue to mesmerise listeners. Another memorable passage is the prelude to Indha Maan Undhan Sondha Maan from Karagattakaran . It was a technically demanding piece, but Sada ‘Master’ brought it to life with a richness and grandeur that made it truly exceptional.

In Paruvame Puthiya Paadal Paadu , he played both the vibraphone and the guitar, the combination elevating the song to another level. He also played the theme music for Moodu Pani and Mouna Raagam , creating musical motifs that remain memorable.
Writer and director Suka, who shared a close relationship with Sada ‘Master’, recalled his contribution to several memorable songs.

“One can hear his outstanding guitar work in songs such as Thulli Ezhunthathu Paatu; Poove Chempoove; En Iniya Pon Nilave; Nalam Vaazha; and Raamanin Mohanam. In my opinion, he was one of the most talented and brilliant guitarists,” he said.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Fed is expected to keep the rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market economies for foreign investors

The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4.0% at its October policy meeting. The 12-member committee had a 10:2 voting pattern for maintaining the status quo, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal President Beth Hammack voted in favour of a 25 basis points hike.
The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.
While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.
“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

The stock market too traded lower in early trade but trimmed losses, with the Sensex trading 852.58 points higher to 74,098.61 at 2.30 p.m. The Nifty 50 was trading above 22,900. Analysts note that the Nifty must trade below 22,500 for bearishness to pertain.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Rescue teams use cranes, dog teams in search for survivors of fatal crash; death toll stands at 68

Rescuers searched desperately through wrecked ⁠carriages on Thursday (October 29, 2026) in the hope of finding more survivors of Spain’s second deadly high-speed train crash this year, which has so far claimed 68 lives.

Emergency workers were seen carrying what appeared ‌to be a body wrapped in a blanket from one of the trains in a rural area in the central province of Toledo as ‌cranes worked through the night to lift parts of the wreckage of Wednesday’s ‌crash.

“Rescue ⁠teams are still working very carefully, because we still cannot say with ⁠certainty that there are no more victims trapped in the twisted wreckage,” Esther Padilla, a spokeswoman for the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha, told TVE.
“A canine unit was deployed yesterday. They will go back ​in today to make sure that nobody ‌else remains there,” she added.

Meanwhile, train drivers in Spain went ahead with a previously planned strike to press for more investment in railway safety after what is Europe’s deadliest train accident since a 2013 derailment in Spain’s Santiago de Compostela.

The crash, ‌which followed another fatal accident in January involving the same rail companies ​on the same line, has also upended campaigning for a November 29 snap election, with the leaders of Spain’s two main parties suspending campaign ⁠events.
Spain’s government has declared three days of national mourning for those killed when one high-speed train hit another.
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez was ‌due to travel to Toledo on Thursday morning to take part in a meeting to monitor and coordinate the emergency response.
Meanwhile, Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, leader of the centre-right People’s Party (PP), which is currently leading in polls, was due to travel to the town of Urda near the crash site.
The crash has reopened a debate about safety on Spain’s railways, Europe’s longest and until recently a source of pride in the country.

Spanish Transport ‌Minister Oscar Puente said on Wednesday the crash happened after several trains stopped automatically due to a ​signal failure. A state-run Renfe train was then authorised to proceed at normal speed even though there was a stationary Iryo-operated train ahead.
SEMAF, the ⁠Spanish train drivers’ union, said it did not want to speculate on the cause of ⁠the crash.

fullParagraphs: After the Spain train crash, the Indian Embassy in Madrid issued the emergency helpline number +34 650 339 008, the email cons.madrid@mea.gov.in, and Renfe: 900 10 10 20, and Iryo: 900 001 403
A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed at least 68 people and injured scores of people on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) , with the death toll expected to rise, authorities said.
Indian Embassy in Madrid has opened an emergency helpline for its nationals after the accident — one of Europe’s deadliest rail disasters this century.

The Indian Embassy in Madrid advised Indian nationals who were travelling on the affected trains, as well as their family members, to contact the mission for immediate assistance. In an advisory posted on its official X account, the Embassy urged people to share details of its emergency helpline with anyone requiring support.
The embassy issued the emergency helpline number +34 650 339 008, the email cons.madrid@mea.gov.in, and Renfe: 900 10 10 20, and Iryo: 900 001 403.

The collision occurred in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha on Wednesday (October 29) morning when a train operated by state-owned Renfe crashed into the rear of a stationary train belonging to private operator Iryo.
ALSO WATCH Deadly train collision in Spain: What we know so far

The second major rail accident to hit Spain in 2026 is likely to renew scrutiny of the country’s railway safety systems, with Transport Minister Óscar Puente referring to an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that preceded the crash. The accident involved a Renfe AVE service and an Iryo train travelling from Madrid to Seville. The impact caused the rear coaches of the Iryo train to derail and plunge down an embankment near kilometre marker 118.

Mr. Puente said preliminary assessments suggested a possible technical failure at the Atocha control centre involving the LZB safety system, though he stressed that the exact cause remained under investigation.

According to the Minister, an automatic train-control system failed over a 69-kilometre stretch of track, resulting in services being halted. However, the control centre later authorised the resumption of traffic despite the disruption.

“The control centre decided to resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable,” Mr. Puente said, adding that the Renfe train travelled around 25 kilometres before colliding with the stationary Iryo service.
He said the Renfe train had resumed operations about 15 minutes earlier and may have been travelling at speeds of up to 200 kmph at the time of the impact.

Following the collision, several coaches derailed and tumbled down a steep embankment. Debris and twisted metal were strewn across the crash site, and some carriages appeared to have suffered severe structural damage.

articles.title: Israel election 2026: Benjamin Netanyahu is down but not out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israel’s tight election leaves Benjamin Netanyahu with a fractured majority and a possible caretaker role amid a three-bloc divide and looming coalition uncertainties

Israel’s October 27 election was framed by the Opposition as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu. For the country’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw the war on Gaza, attacked Iran twice and vowed not to make concessions to Palestinians, the election was a battle for survival. For the Opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, this was an opportunity to oust Mr. Netanyahu from power. With almost 90% of the vote counted, Israel is divided into three blocs, none of which can govern alone.

On the latest count, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has 53 seats, eight short of the 61 needed for a majority in the Knesset. His Likud is the largest party with 26 seats, down from 32 four years ago. His far-right partners, Otzma Yehudit of Ithamar Ben-Gvir (7) and Religious Zionism of Bezalel Smotrich (6), hold 13 between them, down slightly from 14 in the last election. The remaining seats in his bloc come from the religious parties—Shas and United Torah Judaism—each with seven seats.

articles.title: Hong Kong's Housing Minister resigns after fire investigation finds inadequate oversight
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: During the investigation, an independent committee found that the Housing Bureau's independent checking unit failed in its duties supervising the maintenance work

Hong Kong leader John Lee apologised on Thursday (October 29, 2026) and said his housing secretary resigned after an investigation into the city's deadliest fire in decades found inadequate regulatory oversight.
The massive fire that broke out last November engulfed seven buildings in an apartment complex in a northern suburban district, killing 168 people and displacing thousands of others.

Many former residents of Wang Fuk Court have spent nearly a year waiting to see how the government will address accountability for the disaster that claimed their loved ones and their homes, which were then undergoing building maintenance work.

At the opening of the news conference, Mr. Lee and seven other top officials bowed in apology. Mr. Lee said Housing Secretary Winnie Ho “should bear political responsibility," although no personal wrongdoing was found. He said Ms. Ho had resigned on Wednesday (October 28).
During the investigation, an independent committee found that the Housing Bureau's independent checking unit failed in its duties supervising the maintenance work.
The committee's work is separate from criminal investigations in which seven people and two companies were charged with offences including manslaughter and conspiracy to defraud over the fire.

Authorities alleged that the two companies and some defendants conspired together to defraud the apartment owners by concealing previous litigation records of the company later awarded the renovation project, a contract worth more than 300 million Hong Kong dollars (over $38 million).

articles.title: Activists write open letter to Telangana CM, point at issues in govt hospitals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The signatories called for a broader effort to strengthen the public health and medical system so that ordinary citizens would not be compelled to abandon government hospitals because of inadequate facilities

“If the public is drifting away from government hospitals and being pushed into the clutches of the corporate healthcare system, it is undeniably because politicians and governments lack genuine sincerity,” said 115 citizens and activists in an open letter to Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha.
The letter accused successive governments of failing to strengthen public healthcare, alleging that the lack of basic amenities in government hospitals is driving patients towards private healthcare.

The letter highlights concerns over drinking water facilities, toilets, sanitation and the maintenance of infrastructure at major government hospitals in Hyderabad, including Osmania General Hospital, Gandhi Hospital, Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Niloufer Hospital and Petlaburj Maternity Hospital.

The signatories — comprising social activists, academics, writers, journalists, teachers and other citizens — questioned whether the government’s promises to improve public healthcare translated into better conditions for patients.

The signatories argued that the challenges confronting government hospitals cannot be viewed solely through the lens of shortages of doctors and other medical personnel. The signatories acknowledged that healthcare workers were already working under considerable pressure, but said the absence of basic amenities was adding to the difficulties faced by patients.
“Government hospitals have experienced doctors, medical staff and research capabilities, but inadequate facilities are undermining the healthcare experience,” they added.

Referring to Osmania, Gandhi, NIMS, Niloufer and Petlaburj hospitals, the signatories questioned why patients should have to endure difficult conditions to access treatment when the institutions were expected to provide essential public healthcare services.

They have identified clean drinking water, functional toilets and proper sanitation as among the most pressing requirements in public hospitals. Questioning the government’s responsibility for maintaining these facilities, the signatories asked whether patients should be held responsible for unhygienic conditions and unpleasant odours in hospital toilets, arguing that the responsibility for maintenance rested with the authorities.
They said patients who could afford private healthcare might choose to seek treatment elsewhere, but those unable to bear the additional expense were left with fewer options.

The signatories also cautioned the government against transferring responsibility for maintaining basic hospital amenities to corporate entities under the banner of public participation as doing so would impose an additional financial burden on patients. They called for the government to take responsibility for improving existing infrastructure and ensuring that essential facilities were properly maintained.

They further questioned the emphasis placed on changing photographs on walls and ambulances after a government assumes office, arguing that the same attention should be directed towards providing basic amenities in hospitals.

Beyond immediate improvements to hospital infrastructure, the signatories urged the Telangana government to introduce a strong Right to Health law through consultations with people’s organisations and public. They called for a broader effort to strengthen the public health and medical system so that ordinary citizens would not be compelled to abandon government hospitals because of inadequate facilities.

articles.title: Mother’s feeding practices may influence children’s reluctance to try new foods: NIN study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Food neophobia among children can limit dietary variety and potentially affect nutritional health during crucial years of growth

A mother’s knowledge, attitude and feeding practices can significantly influence a child’s willingness to try new foods , which highlights the need for stronger nutrition counselling for caregivers during early childhood, according to a new study by researchers at the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (NIN).

The study, published in the Journal of Nutritional Science , examined food neophobia, a condition in which children are reluctant to try unfamiliar or diverse foods. Such behaviour can limit dietary variety and potentially affect nutritional health during crucial years of growth.

Researchers assessed 150 mother-child pairs from Addagutta in Hyderabad between August and October 2025 focusing on children aged two- seven years and explored how maternal feeding practices were associated with food neophobia and children’s nutritional status.

The findings revealed that nearly 77% of children showed moderate levels of food neophobia, while 11.3% displayed high levels and 12% had low levels. Boys recorded slightly higher food neophobia scores than girls, although the differences were not statistically significant.

The study also found a link between nutritional status and food acceptance. Children suffering from wasting were more likely to exhibit higher food neophobia scores than those with normal nutritional status, suggesting that reluctance to try new foods may be associated with poorer dietary outcomes.

Researchers observed that maternal knowledge, attitudes and practices played an important role. Children whose mothers demonstrated moderate levels of nutrition-related knowledge and positive feeding practices had lower food neophobia scores than those whose mothers had lower scores.

Karthikeyan Ramanujam, Scientist-C at ICMR-NIN and lead author of the study, said the findings underscore the importance of everyday feeding behaviours. He suggested that caregivers should repeatedly offer a variety of foods without pressure, create positive mealtime experiences and respond supportively when children reject unfamiliar foods.

ICMR-NIN Director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings offer an opportunity to strengthen behavioural feeding counselling through existing government programmes such as the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) and POSHAN Abhiyaan.

Researchers cautioned that the study was limited to a single urban low-income community and a relatively small sample size. They noted that, as a cross-sectional study, it identifies associations but cannot establish direct cause-and-effect relationships, as per a press release.

Karthikeyan Ramanujam, Scientist-C at ICMR-NIN and lead author of the study, said the findings underscore the importance of everyday feeding behaviours. He suggested that caregivers should repeatedly offer a variety of foods without pressure, create positive mealtime experiences and respond supportively when children reject unfamiliar foods.

ICMR-NIN Director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings offer an opportunity to strengthen behavioural feeding counselling through existing government programmes such as the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) and POSHAN Abhiyaan.

Researchers cautioned that the study was limited to a single urban low-income community and a relatively small sample size. They noted that, as a cross-sectional study, it identifies associations but cannot establish direct cause-and-effect relationships, as per a press release.

articles.title: Keralam Assembly: Orders issued to procure 2,159 bottles of SMA drug, says Health Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Replying to a submission, Minister says government is taking several steps through Kerala United Against Rare Diseases scheme to provide timely treatment and life-saving medicines to children affected by SMA

The Kerala government has issued orders for procuring 2,159 bottles of Risdiplam , the first at-home, oral treatment for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), to ensure continued availability of the medicine, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said.

Replying to a submission by P.K. Firos, MLA, in the Assembly on Thursday, the Minister said the government was taking several steps through the KARE (Kerala United Against Rare Diseases) scheme to provide timely treatment and life-saving medicines to children affected by SMA, a rare, life-threatening genetic disorder that progressively weakens muscles, severely impairing both mobility and respiratory function.
Medicines and related treatment were made available through the SMA clinic at SAT Hospital in Thiruvananthapuram, he said.

Keralam used to obtain Risdiplam, under its trade name, at a negotiated price of ₹5.5 lakh per bottle. Since October 19, it had been providing a less expensive generic version of the drug manufactured in the country by Natco Pharma. The drug Natsmart cost only around ₹11,000, significantly bringing down treatment costs and making the medicine available to more children.
Besides medicines, the government also provided physiotherapy, respiratory therapy, respiratory devices, rehabilitation, and surgery, the Minister said.
Keralam has been providing Risdiplam free of cost to children under 12 since 2022 through KARE. Steps have been taken to provide all eligible persons the medicine lifelong, he said.

Referring to two children of a couple who had registered with the SMA clinic at SAT Hospital on October 6 and had Type 2 SMA, the Minister said they were eligible for free Risdiplam. Urgent steps were being taken to provide them with treatment the approval of a technical experts committee. Natsmart was being provided to them. Medicines and treatment would be provided to the couple’s third child through KARE on completion of check-up, he added.

The government would also consider devising more comprehensive programmes in association with the Kerala Social Security Mission to provide treatment and financial and psychological support to the affected children and their families. The government, the Minister said, was committed to ensuring that treatment was not disrupted, medicines were available continuously, and the financial burden on families was reduced.

Amazon cut about 250 ‌jobs on Wednesday in its ​devices and services unit after ⁠weeks of product rollouts including new Kindle e-readers and tablet computers.
The company ‌confirmed the cuts after a Reuters inquiry.
"We've made ‌the difficult decision to eliminate ‌a ⁠small number of roles," a ⁠spokesperson said without elaborating.

Earlier ⁠this month, Amazon pared about ⁠1,000 jobs in its core retail division. The company reports ‌its third-quarter earnings after the market close on Thursday.

articles.title: Uber announces new driver-first initiatives like Bike Intercity and WhatsApp onboarding
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Uber launched ‘Flexible Drive Pass,’ offering subscription passes ranging from six hours to 180 days to accommodate both part-time and full-time schedules

Uber has introduced a range of new features and expanded earning opportunities for over 20 lakh driver partners on its platform in India, at the third edition of its Uber Pragati event in New Delhi on Thursday (October 29, 2026).
Uber launched ‘Flexible Drive Pass,’ offering subscription passes ranging from six hours to 180 days to accommodate both part-time and full-time schedules.

It has also started to simplify the driver onboarding process through ‘Quickstart,’ enabling drivers to sign up directly via WhatsApp, where a will guide them through the entire process, while a third-party will do the necessary background security check.
Uber has also announced the ‘Earn First, Pay Later’ feature that grants eligible drivers an additional credit limit to accept cash trips even when their account balance runs out.

The ride-hailing platform has introduced in-app voice notes as well in which driver can communicate through voice notes to make the discovery easier in case of confusion. It has redesigned driver app too that further streamline communication and earnings management.

Uber will now allow Bike Intercity for shorter trips between neighbouring towns and cities, including routes such as Delhi-Meerut, so that drivers can enhance their earnings. With Uber Direct, bike drivers can also fulfill delivery orders for businesses, while Uber Parcel enables them to deliver personal packages within cities.
Uber highlighted its 24×7 Ambulance Assistance partnership with Dial 4242, which has already provided emergency medical support on 25 occasions in under four months.

Additional safety measures include ‘Record My Ride’ encrypted video recording to assist police in resolving disputed incidents, real-time chat flagging to prevent inappropriate rider messages, and a centralised Driver Safety Hub for quick access to safety settings.

“We are giving drivers the freedom to work on their own terms, the confidence of industry-leading safety protections and more ways to earn,” said Aditya Kapoor, Director – Supply Operations, Uber India and South Asia.

articles.title: Milk price hiked in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: This follows a demand by farmers who are struggling with drought

The price of Nandini milk is set to go up by ₹8 per litre in Karnataka. The State Cabinet took a decision in this regard on October 29 following a demand by farmers for hike in procurement price of milk. Of this, ₹7 will go to farmers, and ₹1 to Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF).

Though dairy farmers had been demanding a hike citing escalation in input cost and the drought in Karnataka, a decision had been deferred because of the election code of conduct being in force owing to Legislative Council polls. The results of the polls were declared on October 27.
Following hike in milk prices, hotels are likely to increase their prices.

articles.title: Gangakatwa canal in Sangareddy to be restored with ₹37 crore: Jagga Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Gangakatwa canal dates back to the time of the seventh Nizam and was designed to irrigate around 3,300 acres of agricultural land across 11 villages

TPCC working president Jagga Reddy said the Gangakatwa canal in Suraram village, Sadasivapet mandal of Sangareddy district would be restored with the government sanctioning ₹37 crore for its renovation.

The Gangakatwa canal dates back to the time of the seventh Nizam and was designed to irrigate around 3,300 acres of agricultural land across 11 villages. The proposed renovation is aimed at restoring the ageing irrigation infrastructure and improving its capacity to serve farmers in the region.

The project is expected to benefit agricultural activity in the 11 villages by improving irrigation access. The sanction is significant for the local farming community, as the canal has long required repairs and renovation.

Mr. Jagga Reddy, who had been pursuing the renovation of the old irrigation system for a long time, apparently submitted 25 representations to various governments pressing for the release of funds. His efforts culminated in Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy sanctioning ₹37 crore for the project.
While inspecting the canal after the funds’ release, Mr. Jagga Reddy jumped into the canal and swam, turning the inspection into a celebration of the proposed restoration work.

articles.title: Days after Theni jailbreak, Tamil Nadu Prisons DGP Sandeep Rai Rathore transferred
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 17 remand prisoners who were lodged at the Thekkampatti sub-jail near Andipatti in Theni district escaped on October 26 and were later recaptured by special teams over the next two days.

Three days after the sensational jailbreak in Theni district where 17 prisoners escaped and were later recaptured, the Tamil Nadu government, on Thursday (October 29, 2026) transferred out the Director-General of Police, Prisons, Sandeep Rai Rathore .
He has been posted as DGP, EB, Vigilance, Chennai. Replacing Mr. Rathore, K. Shankar, ADGP, Enforcement Bureau CID, has been posted as the ADGP, Prisons and Correctional Services.

Earlier on Monday (October 26) night, 17 remand prisoners who were lodged at the Thekkampatti sub-jail in Theni district escaped after claiming that one of the inmates suffered epileptic seizures and required assistance. When a jail warder opened the cell, they overpowered him and fled after attacking other prison warders too.
This was the largest escape of inmates since 1995 when 43 LTTE militants who were detained in a special camp at the Vellore Fort escaped after digging a 153-foot-long tunnel in the Tippu Mahal.
Take action against negligent prison officials: Anbumani
When 43 LTTE militants escaped from Vellore Fort special camp in 1995

articles.title: Stalin demands apology from T.N. CM Vijay for MIDS professor’s detention; TVK denies ‘political vendetta’ claim
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ruling TVK said the inquiry was not related to the professor’s remarks on rising rice prices

DMK president M.K. Stalin on Thursday (October 29, 2026) condemned the brief detention of Kalaiyarasan , an associate professor at the Madras Institute of Development Studies (MIDS), on Wednesday (October 28). Mr. Stalin claimed the academic was detained for highlighting the unprecedented price rise, describing it as the height of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) “fascist attitude”.
He said Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and the police department must apologise for the “arrest” of a renowned academic on false charges.

In a statement, Mr. Stalin said he was shocked by the “illegal arrest” of Prof. Kalaiyarasan by plain-clothes police personnel, who took him away in a rented vehicle. “He is not an ordinary person, nor does he have a criminal background,” he said.

Mr. Stalin said Prof. Kalaiyarasan was a professor at one of Tamil Nadu’s foremost research institutions and had obtained his PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University. “He is one of the authors of The Dravidian Model , published by Cambridge University Press. He was a member of the Central Planning Commission and played a major role in preparing an economic research paper for the Tamil Nadu government. He is still a member of the Department of Environment and Climate Change, headed by the Chief Minister,” he said.

Mr. Stalin said it was unacceptable to dismiss the incident as a case of mistaken arrest. Prof. Kalaiyarasan had been “arrested” for an offence he had not committed, denied his rights and had his mobile phone seized by the police, he alleged.
“What a shame that the government allows criminals to roam free while trying to intimidate an educationist,” he said.

Questioning the grounds for the “arrest”, Mr. Stalin asked whether Prof. Kalaiyarasan had been targeted for highlighting the achievements of the ‘Dravidian Model’ government and exposing the unprecedented price rise under the TVK regime.

“Of course, there is no place for education in the TVK, which is dominated by ignorants. But we never thought that it had such an aversion to knowledge that it would arrest an educationist. The TVK will surpass the BJP in its fascist tendencies. Was the arrest made with the approval of the Chief Minister and officials?” he asked.
The ruling TVK, however, denied any political vendetta in the police inquiry involving the MIDS professor, and said it was not related to his remarks on rising rice prices.
Mr. Gananathan said he had explained to the police personnel that he had known Mr. Kalaiyarasan for 10 years and had outlined the academic’s contributions.

“The police personnel subsequently stopped their attempt to take Mr. Kalaiyarasan to the police station. However, he was left waiting on the road leading to what he termed as embarrassing situation as the police inspector did not answer calls seeking to provide further information,” Mr. Gananathan claimed.
He said he had informed School Education Minister Rajmohan about the incident and claimed the Minister had expressed regret to Mr. Kalaiyarasan.

articles.title: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will resign February 7, nine months early
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde has announced her resignation effective February 7

European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will resign nine months ahead of the end of her term, a move that opens the way for European leaders to choose a successor ahead of France’s presidential election next year.
Ms. Lagarde will leave February 7, the ECB said Thursday (October 29, 2026). Her eight-year term was to end October 31, 2027.
The resignation opens the way for complex political horse trading over her successor and to fill the posts of two other top officials who are leaving next year.

The announcement was not a surprise since there has been speculation that Lagarde would leave early to enable EU leaders to choose a successor while pro-EU French President Emmanuel Macron is still in office. That would guard against the possibility that right-wing presidential candidate Marine Le Pen might win the election and influence the choice.
“That she leaves early is no surprise and does not change the outlook for ECB policies,” said Holger Schmieding, chief economist at Berenberg bank.
European Council President Antonio Costa said that the selection process “will be initiated today and will proceed without delay.”

The term of another top ECB official — chief economist Philip Lane — is to end May 31, while another member of the ECB’s executive board, Isabel Schnabel, is resigning at year end to move to the International Monetary Fund. European leaders are expected to work out a package deal to apportion the three vacancies among member countries in a complex round of political bargaining.
EU leaders would likely seek to reach agreement on all three posts before a summit meeting on December 17-18, said Holger Schmieding, chief economist at Berenberg bank.

He said that leading candidates for Lagarde’s job appeared to be former Netherlands central bank head Klaas Knot and Spain’s Pablo Hernandez de Cos, the general manager of the Bank for International Settlements.

“The European Union is trying to guard itself at least somewhat against the risk that right-wing Marine Le Pen may win the French presidential election in April-May 2027,” Mr. Schmieding wrote in an email. “Lagarde’s successor will still be appointed while the staunchly pro-European centrist Emmanuel Macron still resides in the Elysee Palace.”
MS. Lagarde, the former head of the International Monetary Fund, was appointed in 2011 to succeed Mario Draghi.

articles.title: U.K. PM Andy Burnham’s trip to India could take place soon: British Envoy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is keen to visit India and a trip could take place soon, a top U.K. diplomat said on Thursday (October 29, 2026), highlighting the growing partnership between the two countries.

Speaking to PTI, Acting British High Commissioner to India Ben Mellor said Mr. Burnham had conveyed his desire to visit India during a conversation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi after taking office. “I know that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is very keen to come to India," Mr. Mellor said.
"When he and Prime Minister Modi spoke just after he took office as prime minister, he expressed that directly to the prime minister, and I'm sure we'll be able to see that happen soon,” he added.
Mr. Burnham was appointed as prime minister on July 20 this year.
On the India-U.K. economic ties, Mr. Mellor expressed confidence that the two countries would surpass their target of doubling bilateral trade as their economies continue to grow.
The Free Trade Agreement (FTA) came into force 100 days ago. But actually it was signed just over a year ago. Since then we've already seen new deals worth 12 billion pounds, he said.
Comment | An anchor for India-U.K. ties, their economic partnership
“I have every confidence that as the UK and the Indian economies grow, we will surpass the target of doubling trade between our two countries,” Mr. Mellor added.
India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030.

Mr. Mellor also said the U.K. remained strongly welcoming to Indian businesses and investors, noting that Indian investors had been the second-largest source of new investment projects in the country over the past several years.

He said the India-U.K. Free Trade Agreement (FTA) had further improved the environment for businesses seeking to invest, trade and work across the two countries. “Just two weeks ago, seven mayors from the UK and one local authority brought a large business delegation of over 200 businesses to India to come and look for partners that they could work with,” Mr. Mellor said.
He said the measures announced in Wednesday's U.K. Budget had reinforced that approach by seeking to make the British economy predictable and attractive for investment.

articles.title: Power sector suffers ₹500-crore damage due to Cyclone Arnab, says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inspecting the cyclone-hit areas, Gottipati Ravi Kumar says government has intensified emergency repairs to the damaged infrastructure, with special focus on Palakollu, Bhimavaram and Narsapur, which bore the brunt of the extreme weather event

Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar on Thursday said that Cyclone Arnab caused an estimated ₹500 crore damage to the power sector and that the government has intensified emergency repairs to the damaged infrastructure, with special focus on Palakollu, Bhimavaram and Narsapur, which bore the brunt of the extreme weather event.

Inspecting the cyclone-hit areas in Bhimavaram on Thursday, Mr. Ravi Kumar said a comprehensive assessment would provide a clearer picture of the true extent of the damages, and that around 1,700 personnel were engaged in the restoration works, with an additional 500 employees being mobilised from the three DISCOMs. Another 500 electricity employees from Telangana joined the operations.

The Minister said the government was ensuring that there was no shortage of manpower, funds or equipment for the restoration efforts and that officials were directed to replace damaged electricity poles, repair snapped conductors, and restore damaged transformers on a priority basis.

articles.title: Fishing boat catches fire near Feroke
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident, which occurred when workers were away from the spot, reportedly originated in the boat’s engine and fuel tank

A fishing boat docked beneath the old Feroke bridge caught fire early on Thursday (October 29, 2026) morning, triggering safety concerns among residents. The incident, which occurred when workers were away from the spot, reportedly originated in the boat’s engine and fuel tank.

According to the initial assessment by rescue squads, the blaze broke out in the engine section before spreading to other parts rapidly. Prompt response from emergency personnel helped avert a major disaster. Two officers waded into the river with ropes, swam to the boat, secured it safely, and assisted teams in pulling the vessel closer to the bank.

Fire and rescue services personnel subsequently pumped water to fully extinguish the flames. A rescue officer said a technical malfunction in the boat’s engine caused the fire. He added that further investigations were on to determine the exact cause of the fire.

articles.title: Court directive to add to Kochi Corporation’s Brahmapuram biomining costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Corporation will have to biomine an additional 1.26 lakh tonnes of scientifically capped legacy waste; civic body had agreed to pay ₹1,672 per tonne to biomine 1.96 lakh tonnes at a cost of ₹37 crore
The Kochi Corporation will have to biomine an additional 1.26 lakh tonnes of scientifically capped legacy waste, further adding to its financial burden.

This follows a direction issued by Kerala High Court judges P. Gopinath and Bechu Kurian Thomas during a visit to the Brahmapuram waste treatment plant last month, asking the civic body to include the scientifically capped legacy waste in the biomining process as well. The High Court has been closely monitoring activities at Brahmapuram since a major fire broke out in heaps of plastic waste in 2023 and continued for nearly a fortnight.

Earlier this year, the National Institute of Technology-Calicut (NIT-C) submitted a report to the Corporation estimating the total remaining legacy waste at 3.22 lakh metric tonnes, including the scientifically capped waste. The Corporation had decided not to disturb the capped waste and instead carry out biomining of the remaining 1.96 lakh tonnes at a negotiated rate of ₹1,672 per metric tonne, amounting to ₹37 crore. However, the cost may now have to be recalculated following the directive to include the capped waste as well.

“We will take up the matter with Bhumi Green Energy, the agency entrusted with biomining, once we receive a report on the judges’ visit. Thereafter, we will discuss other aspects, including how long it will take to cover the capped area,” said Mayor V.K. Minimol.

The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had earlier locked horns with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) over the supplementary agreement extending Bhumi Green Energy’s biomining contract without inviting fresh tenders. The agency is already engaged in the work. However, the UDF claimed that intense negotiations had helped bring down the biomining rate by ₹18 per tonne from the previously fixed ₹1,690, saving the Corporation around ₹60 lakh.

“Our position all along has been that there is no need to touch the already scientifically capped legacy waste. We have made it clear in the council as well. It will be an additional burden on the Corporation,” said V.A. Sreejith, LDF parliamentary party leader.

Former Mayor M. Anilkumar had, at a press conference in January, warned the UDF-led governing committee of the Kochi Corporation against overspending at Brahmapuram and overestimating the quantity of waste to be treated there, thereby paving the way for corruption. “Whatever more needs to be done should be done, but taxpayers’ money should not be wasted needlessly,” he had said, referring to the Mayor’s statement that Brahmapuram required new projects to improve its condition.

The Corporation had originally signed an agreement with Bhumi Green Energy on November 4, 2023, to biomine 7 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste within 16 months. The contract, initially scheduled to end on March 3, 2025, was later extended by eight months, until November 30, 2025.

articles.title: ‘Robust monitoring needed to ensure SC/ST sub-plan funds reach intended beneficiaries’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and Social Welfare Minister Adluri Laxman Kumar have directed officials to ensure effective utilisation of funds earmarked under the SC/ST Sub-Plan and to see that welfare and development benefits reach every eligible Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) family in the State.

At a review meeting held at the Secretariat on Thursday, the Ministers stressed the need for a robust monitoring mechanism to ensure that Special Development Funds meant for the socio-economic advancement of SCs and STs are utilised strictly for their intended purpose, without any diversion.

Mr. Vikramarka instructed officials to comprehensively document the benefits accruing to SC and ST farmers through government programmes such as Rythu Bharosa, subsidised seed distribution and agricultural mechanisation initiatives. He also asked departments to explore alternative mechanisms wherever existing guidelines were hindering the optimal utilisation of Sub-Plan funds and to formulate proposals for targeted interventions that would provide greater support to eligible farmers from the two communities.

Mr. Laxman Kumar reiterated that funds allocated for SC and ST development should not be diverted under any circumstances. He called for continuous monitoring of department-wise expenditure, beneficiary coverage and the physical progress of works to ensure that every rupee spent under the Sub-Plan translated into tangible benefits for the intended communities.

Officials informed the meeting that district Collectors had identified around 1,300 acres of vacant government land across the State. Mr Bhatti asked departments to examine proposals for land acquisition wherever required to provide house sites to families without residential plots.

articles.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation into allegations of fraud but cautioned against stigmatising the entire Arab Israeli community, who voted at unprecedented rates

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc on Thursday (October 29, 2026) piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that could hold the key to forming a government after an inconclusive election.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation into allegations of fraud but cautioned against stigmatising the entire Arab Israeli community, who voted at unprecedented rates.

Israel was nearing the completion of ballot-counting from Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) election, in which neither Mr. Netanyahu nor the Opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in the parliament known as the Knesset.
The Netanyahu camp's accusations, which a key Arab party has rejected, could bring uncertainty to the electoral process at a time when the threat of a return to war with Iran looms over the region.

Israel's election saw soaring participation by Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the country's creation in 1948, as outrage boiled at calls by officials such as National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir to treat their community much as Israel has dealt with Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
Following Mr. Netanyahu's accusations of impropriety, Ben Gvir went so far as to encourage Israel to "immediately" order the arrests of Arab party leaders.
Raam party leader Mansour Abbas said he welcomed an investigation into claims of wrongdoing, adding that his moderate Islamist party had "no connection" with the accusations.

The Arab parties together have enough votes to take the opposition bloc over the finish line, but Mr. Eisenkot has baulked after relentless attacks by Mr. Netanyahu, who warned his right-wing Jewish base that voting for the Opposition would put Arabs in power.

Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, a conservative who heads the Central Election Commission, requested an investigation by the Shin Bet security service into allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas.
"The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel's elections have been stolen!" Mr. Netanyahu's Likud party said.
Government officials did not offer evidence to back the allegations, and left-wing candidate Yair Golan accused Mr. Netanyahu of attempting to stir controversy after failing to get a majority.
"Now he is trying to challenge the election results through an ugly delegitimisation campaign against the will of the people, and against the Arab public in particular."

articles.title: India ready to share battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners: Rajnath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the 13th ADMM-Plus in Cebu that India would share its operational experience through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes and intelligence sharing, and proposed a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ with ASEAN countries

India is committed to collective regional security and the eradication of terrorism in all its forms and is ready to share its battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners to strengthen joint capabilities, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday (October 29, 2026).

Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines, Mr. Singh said India’s counter-terrorism experience was not theoretical knowledge but had been acquired through decades of confronting complex security challenges, including cross-border terrorism.
He said India’s strategies had been tested and refined through real-world operations, with Operation Sindoor demonstrating the country’s proactive counter-terrorism doctrine.
During the operation, India dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced a firm red line against state-sponsored terrorism, he said.

Emphasising that terrorism knows no borders, Mr. Singh said India was prepared to share its operational experience with ADMM-Plus partners through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes and intelligence sharing.
Counter-terrorism remains an important area of cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, with India and Malaysia co-chairing the Experts’ Working Group on Counter-Terrorism for the 2024-2027 cycle.

In a significant proposal to deepen regional engagement, Mr. Singh called for the establishment of a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ to strengthen institutional people-to-people connectivity between India and ASEAN countries. The ASEAN members appreciated the move of establishing ‘Youth Bridge’.

The initiative would promote digital innovation and capacity building, while providing greater opportunities for young people to contribute to regional peace and security. The proposal was appreciated by ASEAN members.

Highlighting the importance of maritime security, Mr. Singh said India had designated 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and had conducted the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He reiterated India’s commitment to freedom of navigation, international maritime law and the security of global sea lanes.

Pointing to the Indian Navy’s uninterrupted operational presence in the Gulf of Aden since 2008, he said India had escorted thousands of merchant vessels and thwarted dozens of hijacking attempts, irrespective of the vessels’ flag or nationality.

He reaffirmed India’s commitment to ASEAN centrality and a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, adding that New Delhi would continue to serve as a reliable net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and the wider Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: Bangladesh's tribunal sentences Awami League leader to death
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A three-member tribunal led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury and comprising Justices Md. Manjurul Bashid and Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir delivered the verdict
A special tribunal in Bangladesh on Thursday (October 29, 2026) sentenced Awami League's Joint General Secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death for the killing of six people during the July Uprising.
A three-member tribunal led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury and comprising Justices Md. Manjurul Bashid and Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir delivered the verdict.
"He will be hanged until death,” Mr. Chowdhury ruled after convicting him of killing six people in western Kushtia district during the 2024 violent student-led street protests.

The tribunal simultaneously sentenced to “imprisonment until death” three other Awami League leaders of the district unit on identical charges for their role in taming the protest dubbed the July Uprising that eventually toppled Sheikh Hasina’s government on August 5, 2024, when she fled to India.

All four accused, including Hanif, are absconding. The tribunal also ordered the confiscation of half of their property. Hanif is the 23rd leader of the now-disbanded Awami League to receive the capital punishment after the ouster of Sheikh Hasina.
They were all tried in absentia, with Sheikh Hasina being the first to be sentenced to death on November 17 last year, along with former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal.
Dozens more politicians and officials under the past government were sentenced to life imprisonment or other jail terms, while scores are facing trial in person or in absentia on different charges.

Ms. Hasina and her party leaders have called the tribunal a “kangaroo court” while international rights groups like Amnesty International, U.S.-based Human Rights Watch and prominent jurists questioned the fairness of the trials.
The ouster of the Awami League government installed an interim regime with Muhammad Yunus as its head. The tribunal's chief prosecutor Md. Aminul Islam welcomed the verdict, describing it as timely.

"The tribunal delivered its verdict today after completing the trial in this crimes against humanity case. Today's verdict is very timely. Paying tribute to the July martyrs, we welcome the verdict," he said. The convicts were defended by state-appointed lawyers.

fullParagraphs: Opposition lawmakers in Albania disrupted a parliament session by letting off flares on Thursday (October 29, 2026) ​following weeks of violent anti-government protests called by students ‌demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

"These (ruling lawmakers) are ‌criminals and they deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls and broken bones, not the ‌young people," Opposition leader Sali Berisha said ‌during his ⁠speech before his microphone was cut off.
Other ⁠Opposition members surrounded him during the speech, holding photos of protesters injured by rubber bullets. Some held aloft blue flares, the ​colour of their ‌party.
