articles.title: BRICS parliamentary forum expresses ‘deep concern’ about West Asian hostilities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Joint declaration calls for a two-state solution to Israel-Palestinan conflict; asserts the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, freedom, and an independent, sovereign state

Expressing ‘deep concern’ about the escalating tension and hostilities in West Asia, parliamentary leaders from the BRICS nations slammed “unilateral coercive measures” and “unilateral economic sanctions” imposed in the region as contrary to international law.

A joint declaration issued after deliberations led by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, at the end of the two-day 12 th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on Tuesday, also reiterated the need for a ‘two-state’ solution to the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

“We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia and, recalling our respective national positions, call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation,” the joint declaration said.

The meeting in New Delhi earlier drew attention as the Iranian parliamentary delegation’s chief, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, cancelled his India visit in the wake of growing hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi forces.

Despite the absence of Mr. Ghalibaf, who has been a key interlocutor in direct and indirect negotiations during the ongoing conflict, the forum provided opportunities for the exchange of views among stakeholders in West Asia. Several key policymakers from the region attended, including Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, Chairman of the Defence Affairs, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the United Arab Emirates.

Ties between the UAE and Iran have nosedived, as Iran attacked the Gulf nation as part of its strategy of retaliation against the U.S.-led attacks that began on February 28. Meeting a small group of journalists on the sidelines of the forum, Mr. Al Nuaimi spoke forcefully in favour of the two-state solution for the Israel-Palestinian crisis, without hurting Israel’s interests. “Around 160 countries recognise Israel, and it is a reality in the region. But the tragic situation has shown that the Palestinian state is needed. With this in mind, we need to restart the negotiation for a two-state solution,” Mr. Al Nuaimi said.

The joint declaration also addressed the ongoing conflict in the Gaza Strip. “We reaffirm our unwavering support for the peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict based on the two-state solution, with the two States living side by side, in peace and security, in accordance with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, asserting the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, freedom and an independent, sovereign state.”

The BRICS Parliamentary Forum obliquely addressed the U.S.-Israel attack on Iran and the BRICS stance against attacks on member countries, “We call for the elimination of such unlawful measures which undermine international law and the principles and purposes of the UN Charter,” the joint declaration said.

It condemned acts of terrorism as “criminal and unjustified” and condemned the April 22, 2025 terror strike in Kashmir’s Pahalgam in the “strongest terms”. It added: “We call for an expeditious finalisation and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism in the UN framework. We call for concerted actions against all UN designated terrorists and terrorist entities.”

The joint declaration added that inter-parliamentary exchanges among BRICS member countries provides a channel of communication and build trust among the member states. “Support the peaceful resolution of international disputes,” it said.

articles.title: Are coronary stents necessary?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: There is a crucial distinction between stenting as a life-saving measure to medical treatment via stenting because a narrowing of blood vessels is seen on an angiogram

Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan’s recent remarks questioning “unnecessary” angioplasty procedures have drawn objections from medical organisations concerned that it could undermine public confidence in doctors. But the Chief Minister’s remarks demand more than a reflex response; it requires a thoughtful, honest response built on up-to-date evidence based on clinical and research studies.

Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI), by balloon angioplasty and stent placement, has transformed cardiovascular care. During an acute heart attack caused by a suddenly blocked coronary artery, prompt angioplasty and stents can restore blood flow, save heart muscle and improve survival. There is no debate about this approach and second opinions are unnecessary as time is of essence in such an emergency. Stents also offer substantial relief to selected patients with persistent activity-limiting angina (chest pain caused by lack of oxygen-rich blood).

There is a crucial distinction between stenting as a life-saving measure in the above situations to medical treatment via stenting because a narrowing of blood vessels is seen on an angiogram. A coronary angiogram shows the anatomy of the arteries; it does not, by itself, establish that a narrowing requires intervention. The decision to intervene and how to intervene must take account of the patient’s symptoms, the severity of the blockage, its effect on blood flow, the overall pattern of coronary disease and the expected benefit of intervention.
Kerala CM’s statement on angioplasty becomes a talking point among doctors
Public apprehension over unnecessary medical procedures should not delay treatment, say cardiologists in Keralam

The landmark ISCHEMIA trial , published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2020 , enrolled 5,179 patients at 320 sites in 37 countries with stable coronary artery disease and moderate to severe ischemia (restricted blood flow to the heart). The patients were assigned either to an initial invasive strategy — angiography followed by angioplasty or coronary bypass surgery — or to a conservative strategy of optimal medical treatment, with revascularisation reserved for those who had an acute event or angina. After a median follow-up of 3.2 years, there was no significant difference between the two groups in composite outcomes (cardiac arrests, hospitalisation for unstable angina or heart failure) and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality were similar. After a follow-up of 5 years, there was still no significant difference between the two groups in composite outcome or mortality. The core lesson is that most patients with stable coronary artery disease with ischemia on optimal medical treatment would do as well as those who undergo stenting or bypass surgery.

The growing scale of PCI in India deserves careful examination. National Interventional Council figures show that annual PCI procedures rose from approximately 1,13,000 in 2008 to more than 7,26,000 in 2024 — an increase of more than six-fold. In contrast, PCI procedures in the U.S. fell by about 40% between 2003 and 2016, reflecting progress in prevention and treatment.

These figures do not by themselves prove that stents are overused in India considering its large population, the substantial burden of premature coronary disease, the socio-economic progress in the past decades and the improved access to cardiac care centres. Nevertheless, the divergence in trends between the two countries raises an important question: how much of the increase in PCI is a reflection of fulfilling a genuine clinical need, and how much of it is a reflection of differences in practice patterns, financial incentives and gaps in knowledge on the efficacy of optimal medical treatment?

Optimal medical therapy, based on evidence-based guidelines, is the foundation of care for all coronary artery disease patients. The elements of optimal therapy include LDL-cholesterol lowering, appropriate anti-platelet treatment, blood-pressure control, evidence-based diabetes management and lifestyle changes. A coronary stent treats a specific narrowing; it does not cure the underlying disease of atherosclerosis or eliminate the risk of future heart attacks. Patients remain vulnerable to disease elsewhere in the coronary arteries and must continue preventive treatment.

The way forward is neither condemnation of cardiologists nor unquestioning acceptance of every recommendation for angioplasty. Most doctors strive to act in their patients’ best interests, but no profession is immune to inappropriate practice. The ultimate test of healthcare is not how many procedures are performed, but how many lives are saved and whether patients receive the right treatment at the right time at an affordable cost.
Dr. Enas A. Enas is Preventive Cardiologist and Physician-Scientist, Founding President of the CADI Research Foundation USA; Dr. Basil Varkey is Professor Emeritus of medicine

articles.title: Singareni seeks Angul Collector’s support for road laying to transport coal from Naini
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chairman and Managing Director of the Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) Dr. Buddhaprakash Jyoti on Tuesday met District Collector of Angul (Odisha) Mohammad Abdaal Akhtar to discuss land allocation and other support required for the company’s proposed projects in Odisha.

The plans include establishment of a thermal power plant near the Naini coal mine, an R&R colony for project-affected families and roads for coal transportation. The Collector responded positively to the proposals and assured necessary support.

Issues such as land acquisition, approvals and other requirements for the proposed works were discussed at the meeting also attended by Singareni Directors Gowtam Potru and L.V. Suryanarayana, Executive Director (Coal Movement) B. Venkanna, General Manager (Coordination) T. Srinivas, Naini General Manager Debdulal Baidya and others

.The Singareni CMD requested the Collector to allot suitable land for an R&R colony for the 40 families displaced by the Naini coal mine. He also sought an early meeting of the Rehabilitation and Periphery Advisory Committee (RPDAC) to take decisions on implementing the R&R package, acquiring land for the colony and addressing other rehabilitation-related matters.

On the Singareni’s plan for setting up a thermal power plant near the Naini coal mine, the company identified land in Tukuda and Jarapada villages as suitable for the project and requested the Collector’s support in acquiring it. On the road for coal transportation, the CMD stated that Singareni had already deposited ₹35 crore towards the proposed bypass road between Chandipara and Jarapada villages, which will connect coal from the Naini block to the nearby Jarapada railway junction.

The CMD requested the departments concerned to support completion of the road, which could serve as a coal corridor for other coal-producing industries as well. Further, he sought suitable land for a Singareni office and staff colony in Odisha as the company was expanding its operations there.

He requested support for constructing the Majhika bypass road to transport coal without causing inconvenience to local residents, assuring that it would provide funds required for land acquisition for the road. The District Collector assured the company of all necessary cooperation, stating that they would support Singareni’s efforts to meet the country’s power requirements.

The Singareni team later visited Jindal’s coal gasification plant in Angul district, the first coal gasification plant in the country. They learned about the process of producing gas from domestic coal and its use by Jindal Steel.

The team also discussed with experts the prospects and feasibility of coal gasification using coal from Singareni’s closed underground mines, as well as incentives offered by the Central Government. Singareni coal from the Naini mine is also transported to the Jindal plant.

articles.title: Women protests force Ladakh administration to discuss ‘declaring region a dry UT'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials disclosed that this year, only one retail vendor was functional and the number of functional bars attached to restaurants offering retail sale of liquor had increased by 17 newly issued licences, taking the total to 40

Facing women-led protests in Ladakh over the opening of liquor shops, the Lieutenant Governor administration on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) agreed to discuss declaring Ladakh a dry Union Territory (UT), saying the matter requires “careful deliberation and consultation with all concerned stakeholders”.

“The demand for declaring Ladakh a completely dry UT is a significant matter that requires careful deliberation and consultation with all concerned stakeholders, for which all agreed,” said Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra.

The L-G administration held a meeting with the representatives of the All Ladakh Gompa Association, Ladakh Buddhist Association, the Anjuman Imamia-Leh, the All Ladakh Gompa Association and the All Ladakh Tour Operators Association. It came in the wake of local women in Leh holding a sit-in for the past six days. The women protesters raised slogans “shame, shame” and were carrying placards reading ‘Don’t trade public health for government revenue’. They were demanding that “the liberal liquor policy” should be rolled back.

On May 31 this year, the L-G administration introduced a new liquor license policy and decided “to increase retail outlets from two to 20 and extend sales to remote pockets such as Nubra, Changthang, Sham, and Zanskar”, regions frequented by tourists from across the country. The new excise policy allowed consumption of liquor within hotel rooms, simplified licensing procedures by reducing required documents from 16 to 6, and removed the requirement for district administration approval for licences.

Mr. Kundra said the meeting with the civil society groups “provided an opportunity for the representatives to present their views and underscored the need for continued engagement and dialogue towards a balanced and informed consideration of the issue”.

“The administration was flexible in its approach to public policy and would be amenable to a middle-ground solution in the matter. If required, another meeting with a larger set of stakeholders would be convened soon,” said Mr. Kundra.

Mr. Kundra, while referring to States like Bihar and Haryana, said the complete prohibition had led to serious consequences, including the proliferation of spurious liquor and drugs. “This is also a cultural issue, and the community needs careful consideration of the consequences of declaring Ladakh as a dry territory. There are also issues of employment, tourism and economic activity and consultation with the hotel industry is also crucial in this regard, particularly given that tourism is the primary economic activity in the territory,” said Mr. Kundra.

He called for “a broad-based consultative process involving religious organisations, hotel associations, tour and travel operators’ associations, and other relevant stakeholders, keeping in view the social, cultural and economic dimensions of the issue”.

Meanwhile, an official spokesman said the representatives of Ladakh groups were informed that “in response to public sentiment, the Excise Policy 2026–27 had been rolled back and now the Excise Policy 2025–26 was in force”.

Officials disclosed that this year only one retail vendor was functional and the number of functional bars attached to restaurants offering retail sale of liquor, which was earlier 23, had increased by 17 newly issued licences, taking the total to 40.

articles.title: India’s ‘balancing act’ risks eroding Russia’s trust
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: New Delhi’s performative diplomacy could undermine its longstanding friendship with Moscow

The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31-September 1, 2026, and the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026, were remarkable. Iran received considerably more attention and support from members of both the groups, far more than anticipated. More consequential, however, was the shift in India’s stance on the United States-Israel war against Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine.

Traditionally, the SCO and BRICS summits have offered the three major powers — Russia, India and China — an opportunity to demonstrate their mutual solidarity. For Russia, it is a platform from which it can signal to the West that it is not isolated and still has powerful allies. The expansion of the SCO and BRICS under China’s leadership showcases its growing power to the West. For India, the SCO and BRICS have been useful for demonstrating its strategic autonomy. India has sought to remain welcome in both western and non-western forums, from the G-7 to the SCO and BRICS.

At Bishkek, however, India sprang two surprises. First, it endorsed the Bishkek Declaration, which condemned the attacks on Iran as violations of international law, reaffirmed Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and mourned the killing of its Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, in U.S.-Israeli air strikes on February 28, 2026.
PM Modi, Vladimir Putin direct officials to expand cooperation, target $100 bn trade by 2030: Envoy
India is discussing agreements on grains and maritime safety with Moscow and Kyiv: Jaishankar
PM Modi has ‘good ideas’ for settlement of Ukraine conflict: Putin
Russia welcomes India’s contribution to end Ukraine crisis: Kremlin spokesperson
India in continuous touch with Ukraine and Russia to help end the conflict: Jaishankar

Although the declaration did not name the U.S. or Israel, its meaning was unmistakable. India reaffirmed its opposition to military strikes on Iran by endorsing the Bishkek Declaration, which condemned the attacks and reiterated support for Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Second, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made an unusually blunt appeal to Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring Russia’s seemingly endless war in Ukraine to an end.

India has generally sought to avoid directly condemning the U.S. or Israel for their military actions against Iran, even though Iran, like India, is a member of both the SCO and BRICS. India had previously avoided explicitly accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza, although it had supported UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire and reaffirmed its commitment to Palestinian statehood. Indeed, New Delhi had emphatically declared that it stands with Israel, while often working in multilateral forums to soften language that is critical of Washington and Tel Aviv. But in both the Bishkek and Delhi Declarations, India signed on to very strong criticism of Israel as well as very strong affirmation of Palestinian rights and the two-state solution.

One interpretation of this pivot in policy is that India may have signed on to the declaration to avoid alienating Mr. Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and thereby jeopardising their attendance at India’s BRICS summit. Without the two leaders, India’s presidency of BRICS this year would have been a complete failure. Since Operation Sindoor (2025), India has faced a growing perception of diplomatic marginalisation. Meanwhile, Pakistan has gained diplomatic prominence through Washington’s selection of Islamabad as a mediator in the conflict with Iran, while several Gulf nations have sought defence agreements with Pakistan. Consequently, India needed a successful and high-profile BRICS summit, which it got.

While there is a shift in India’s policy, New Delhi has not abandoned Washington entirely. Mr. Modi’s public appeal to Mr. Putin to end the endless war in Ukraine can therefore be read as a counter-signal to Washington. Had the message been intended only for Moscow, it could have been conveyed privately. Delivering it publicly suggested that Mr. Modi was also reassuring the West. India may have joined the SCO and BRICS consensus on Iran to secure a successful BRICS summit, but it was now leaning more toward the western position on Ukraine than before.

India has sought to remain welcome in both western and non-western forums, from the G-7 to the SCO and BRICS.

articles.title: Small fish: On Operation Trident
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: SIR: Over 99.32 lakh names struck off voter list in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Karnataka’s electorate now stands at 4,55,00,011, down from 5,54,32,314 voters before the SIR began

A whopping 99.32 lakh names have been struck off the electoral rolls of Karnataka following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with the final list published on Tuesday (October 27). The rolls now include 4,55,00,011 voters, down from 5,54,32,314 before the exercise began.
The constituency-wise electoral rolls can be accessed on the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) website.

At the draft stage, the electorate had shrunk to 4.46 crore, with over 1.07 crore names deleted. The final roll has seen a net addition of 8.19 lakh names compared with the draft roll. However, the net additions have barely offset the deletions, knocking off nearly a crore from the pre-SIR electorate.

The net addition figures given by the CEO’s office does not indicate how many people who were wrongly excluded have managed to get back on the rolls. Nor does the figure provide a separate break-up of young or first-time voters added during the exercise, making it difficult to ascertain how many of those deleted have been reinstated.

“Karnataka has more than 6.87 crore total population (projected as on the proposed publication year 2026), as per the Population Projections for India and States 2011-2036 published by National Commission on Population Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and 4.54 crore (general electors) in the number of electors in the final roll,” CEO V. Anbu Kumar said, adding that the population-to-electors ratio should ideally be between 60 and 70, and that Karnataka’s ratio stood at 66.11.

However, Mr. Kumar did not explain how the gap of about 2.33 crore between the projected population and the electorate is accounted for, including how much of it comprises people below 18 years, non-voter residents and eligible voters who may have been left out.
ALSO WATCH How did 37 people declare themselves dead in Karnataka’s voter rolls?

The final electorate comprises over 2.25 crore male voters, 2.29 crore female voters and 2,841 third-gender voters. It includes over 6.83 lakh young voters aged 18-19 and more than 3.92 lakh voters aged above 85, besides 44,322 service electors.
The largest pool of electors, 1,02,57,680, belongs to the 30-39 age group, followed by 94,17,853 voters aged between 40 and 49.

Those who applied for inclusion through Form 6 within the claims and objections period, which ended on September 23, will have their names included in the final roll if their applications are accepted. Those who applied after the deadline will be included in supplementary lists, which will be published every quarter after the SIR.

Between June 16 and September 23, the last date for claims and objections, over 7.87 lakh Form 6 applications were received. Of these, 76,231 were rejected and 3,193 remained pending, while 7.08 lakh were accepted, as The Hindu previously reported. The CEO’s office said that over one lakh Form 6 applications submitted after the claims period were also processed to ensure maximum additions.

Till October 26, a total of 10.62 lakh Form 6 applications had been received (since June 16), of which 83,806 were rejected on grounds including applicants having applied unknowingly though already registered elsewhere, failure to submit documents and other reasons. The CEO’s office said instructions had been issued to all District Electoral Officers (DEOs) to reach out to applicants whose applications were rejected and include their names if they could be contacted and found eligible.

articles.title: INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC to be held at Kharge's residence on October 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: K.C. Venugopal said 21 parties of the INDIA bloc had planned the “public impeachment of CEC Gyanesh Kumar as a curtain raiser” on October 30 for the November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan on the "vote chori" charge

The INDIA bloc will hold its planned “public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar later this week at the official residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge after the party's attempts to organise the event at the Ashok Hotel and Ramlila Maidan allegedly met with denial of permissions.

Congress MP Jairam Ramesh said Mr. Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg has been finalised as the venue for holding the “public impeachment” of Mr. Kumar on October 30, setting the tone for the “mega rally” INDIA bloc has planned for November 1 at the Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.

The Congress on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) had claimed it was denied permission to hold the "public impeachment" of CEC Kumar and accused the government of trying to "silence" the voice of common people after "destroying" the electoral system.
Congress General Secretary (Organisation) K.C. Venugopal had claimed the government-run Ashok Hotel initially allowed permission to host the event but later denied it after police intervention.
He said the Congress had booked Ramlila Maidan from October 25 to November 3 and decided to shift the event to the site.

He said 21 parties of the INDIA bloc had planned the "public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar as a curtain raiser" on October 30 for the November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan on the "vote chori" charge.

"The day before yesterday, our people came to construct the infrastructure here and the police stopped them. We don't know what the reason is," said Venugopal, who, accompanied by leaders of the Delhi Congress, visited the Ramlila grounds on Tuesday to oversee arrangements for the November 1 rally.
"This means it is not the Delhi Police's decision. It is the decision of PM (Narendra) Modi and (Home Minister) Amit Shah and they are protecting their pet Gyanesh Kumar," he alleged.
"First they destroy the electoral system, and now they are trying all kinds of tricks to silence those who fight to save our democracy.

"Let it be very clear, come what may, we will not rest until Modi-Shah's puppet Gyanesh Kumar is removed. If they stop us here, we will go to Amit Shah's house, PM Modi's house, and stage a massive dharna there. But we will fight to the finish, and until our mission is accomplished," Mr. Venugopal had said in a post on X.
He alleged that the government wants to "shut down criticism" against it.
"How many permissions will you deny, Mr. Amit Shah? How many people will you stop?" he had said.

articles.title: Very severe cyclone Arnab crosses Andhra coast, weakens into severe cyclonic storm: IMD | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The landfall process is complete with the weather system moving entirely over land; CM Naidu says no loss of life reported in Andhra

Thirty-eight flights to and from Visakhapatnam scheduled up to 6.15 p.m. on Wednesday have been cancelled, according to the airport’s flight information page. Nineteen arrivals and 19 departures are off, including international flights to and from Bangkok and Abu Dhabi.
IndiGo said its flights to and from Rajahmundry, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam would remain affected on Wednesday and asked passengers to check their flight status before leaving for the airport.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu held a teleconference with about 32,000 officials and field staff on Wednesday morning and asked them to clear fallen trees and restore traffic within two hours. Power is to be restored as soon as the winds ease and it is safe for crews to work. He also asked officials to prepare early estimates of crop damage.
Chief Minister Naidu told officials to clear fallen trees within two hours and restore power once winds ease after Cyclone Arnab’s landfall in Andhra Pradesh.

Deputy Chief Minister and Jana Sena Party president K. Pawan Kalyan has asked party workers to take part in the government’s relief and rescue work. Heavy rain is likely to continue in the coastal districts even after the cyclone crosses the coast, he said. The government is focusing on moving people from low-lying areas to relief camps and supplying food, milk and other essentials.
Andhra Pradesh has turned 609 school campuses into relief shelters for people moved from cyclone-hit areas on Wednesday. Unsafe buildings have been barricaded.
Schools in 16 coastal districts are closed, and 17,054 NCC, NSS and Scouts volunteers have been mobilised to help.
Andhra Pradesh has turned 609 schools into Cyclone Arnab relief shelters, flagged 78 buildings at risk of collapse and closed schools in 16 coastal districts.

articles.title: Polling underway for phase 2 of Rajasthan Panchayat polls, faulty EVMs delay start at few booths
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The polling began at 7 a.m. for 352 wards of 22 zila parishads and 2,197 wards of 124 panchayat samitis. In some places, however, it was delayed as electronic voting machines (EVMs) malfunctioned
Voting was underway in 22 districts of Rajasthan for the second phase of the Panchayati Raj elections on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) morning.

The polling began at 7 a.m. for 352 wards of 22 zila parishads and 2,197 wards of 124 panchayat samitis. In some places, however, it was delayed as electronic voting machines (EVMs) malfunctioned, according to officials.
Voting will continue till 6 p.m. and those reaching polling stations before the deadline will be allowed to cast their votes.
Each voter will cast two votes, one for a zila parishad member and another for a panchayat samiti member.
Urban Development and Housing Minister Jhabar Singh Kharra was among the early voters and was seen standing in queue at booth number 54 in Bharni village of Sikar district.
In Ganeshwar village of Neem Ka Thana panchayat samiti in Sikar, 95-year-old Mali Devi came with her family to cast her vote.
In Jodhpur's Tiwari panchayat samiti, EVM problems affected voting at two booths. Voting began 30 minutes late at two booths in Ajmer for the same reason, the officials said.
An EVM developed a fault after the first vote was cast at booth number 71 in Muradpur village under Singhana panchayat samiti in Jhunjhunu. Voting resumed after the machine was replaced, they said.

The elections are being held in four phases under a revised schedule. The first phase of zila parishad and panchayat samiti elections was held on October 22 and voting for panch and sarpanch posts was held on October 24.
The remaining two phases of zila parishad and panchayat samiti elections are scheduled for November 3 and 14.

articles.title: EC appoints 11 nodal officers for 2027 Manipur Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Senior IPS officer Kamei Angam Romanus has been named the nodal officer-in-charge of the law and order and security plan, while IAS officer Hungyo Worshang will take charge of excise
Eleven nodal officers have been appointed by the Election Commission for the smooth conduct of the Manipur Assembly polls next year, officials said on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

Senior IPS officer Kamei Angam Romanus has been named the nodal officer-in-charge of the law and order and security plan, while IAS officer Hungyo Worshang will take charge of excise, a notification issued by the Manipur CEO said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) evening.
Konsam Binku will look into election expenditure monitoring, and Khumanthem Diana will be the nodal officer for transport management, it said.
Nodal officers have also been appointed for computerisation, cyber security, communication plan, and other categories.
Assembly elections in Manipur are likely to be held in February-March next year.
Senior officials of the Election Commission had visited Imphal last week to assess poll preparedness across all 16 districts of the northeastern state.

articles.title: Palaniswami, Dhinakaran urge Tamil Nadu government to roll back hike in prices of dairy by-products
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: This government was functioning like a “corporate villain” in feature films, remarks Palaniswami
AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami remarked that the TVK regime in Tamil Nadu had given a “Vettri Deepavali” gift to people by increasing the prices of two dozen dairy by-products.

In a post on his social media handle, he wondered about the mindset of the government in raising prices when it knew that people would buy more ghee and sweets during Deepavali. Traders would increase their sales by providing concessions to the public, but this government was functioning like a “corporate villain” in feature films.

AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran asked whether the price increase was an outcome of the visit of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to a dairy plant recently. Expressing shock over the decision of the authorities, he said this would place an additional economic burden on people who were already finding it difficult to meet their day-to-day needs amid inflation.
The two leaders called upon the government to roll back the price hike.

articles.title: Oil rises over 1% after Saudi Arabian refinery attack reignites supply risk
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said ‌they had hit Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery with a missile, intensifying their strikes against ‌the world’s second-largest crude producer
Oil prices ​climbed more than 1% on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) after an attack on a ‌refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns around supply ​risks from the major exporter.
Brent crude futures gained $1.59, ⁠or 1.4%, to $115.47 a barrel as of 4:35 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude rose $1.43, or 1.4%, to $101.33.

Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said ‌on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) they had hit Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery with a missile, intensifying their strikes against ‌the world’s second-largest crude producer. Saudi authorities did not ‌immediately ⁠confirm the strike on the 550,000 barrel-per-day facility.
Prices ⁠swung higher after dropping nearly $2 on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).
For now, the market is still pricing in a greater likelihood of re-escalation, ING commodity strategists said ​on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).
“Oil prices remain ‌elevated as the market waits for greater clarity on President Trump’s next move toward Iran,” said ING strategists.
“If we get past the elections without renewed strikes on Iran, ‌that might be enough for the market’s risk ​premium to start eroding,” they added.

Meanwhile, U.S. crude oil stocks eased, according to market sources citing data ⁠from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks fell by 2.03 million barrels in the week ended October 23, the sources ‌said.

However, analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 15,000 barrels in the week. The market awaits the U.S. Energy Information Administration’s official weekly inventory report, due later in the day, for more clarity.

The market will also monitor an upcoming industry meeting on Sunday (November 1, 2026), ‌where OPEC+ oil producers are expected to keep their December oil output ​targets steady, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
Production in most of the seven core ⁠OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and ⁠Oman — is below their output targets.
Crude oil exports from Russia’s Baltic and Black Sea ports could fall next ‌month as domestic refiners increase diesel output following a deal with Washington this month, traders said.

articles.title: Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, flydubai crew honoured by UAE President for bravery during mid-air attack
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The medals were presented by His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence

UAE President His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan has conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on Indian Captain Smit Machchhar and fellow flydubai crew members in recognition of their courageous efforts to ensure passenger safety during an attempted mid-air attack aboard a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight.

The medals were presented by His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, who commended the crew’s actions and sense of responsibility, Dubai Media Office said in a statement on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).
Mr. Machchhar and the flydubai crew members received the award at the presidential reception.
The incident occurred on September 30 aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv with more than 170 people on board.

articles.title: Federal Reserve likely to skip rate hike despite elevated inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation

The Federal Reserve is expected to stand pat on interest rates on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) even though inflation has accelerated in the past couple of months as the Iran war has caused spikes in oil and gas prices.

The Fed's latest policy meeting concludes less than a week before the midterm elections, which have focused heavily on concerns about the cost of living and affordability. Consumers have generally soured on an economy weighed down by more expensive gas, groceries, and clothing, among other items.

The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation. The Fed raised its key rate last month for the first time in three years, from about 3.6% to 3.9%, in what many investors and economists perceived was a first step toward a renewed effort to bring down inflation.

Yet Mr. Warsh faces a host of challenges in achieving that goal. President Donald Trump slammed the Fed for raising its key rate last month, though he largely blamed the central bank's rate-setting committee, rather than Mr. Warsh, whom he appointed. And some of the forces driving inflation — specifically the rapid build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure and higher energy prices — won't easily be tamed by higher interest rates.

At the same time, other parts of the economy are already being hit by higher rates, which were lifted by market forces, even before the Fed hiked last month. The average 30-year mortgage rate reached a three-year high of 7.4% earlier this month, though it has since slipped a bit. Higher mortgage rates have made buying a home unaffordable for 5 million more Americans since the beginning of the year, according to Oxford Economics, a consulting firm. Over time, Fed rate hikes can make mortgages, auto loans, and credit card borrowing more expensive, adding to Americans' sense that things like homes and cars are getting pricier.

After the Fed announces its rate decision, Mr. Warsh will speak at a news conference, where his remarks will be closely watched for hints about the Fed's next steps. He will likely repeat the Fed's desire for a “timelier” return of inflation to the 2% target. Some may view that as a sign the Fed will boost its key rate at its next meeting, in December, a move already widely expected by Wall Street investors.

If the Fed keeps rates on hold, Mr. Warsh will be pushed to explain why the central bank hiked rates in September but not this month. Inflation picked up in September, when consumer prices rose 3.7% compared with a year earlier. The increase was much bigger than the 2.4% rate in February, just before the Iran war.

And on a monthly basis, the consumer price index — the most widely-followed inflation gauge — rose 0.3% in both August and September. At that pace over a full year, inflation would rise much more quickly than the Fed's 2% target.

On Thursday (October 29, 2026), a separate inflation measure more closely followed by the Fed, the personal consumption expenditures price index, is forecast to have jumped 3.6% in September from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August. Core prices, which exclude the food and energy categories, are forecast to have risen 3.1%, up from 3% the previous month.

Aditya Bhave, head of U.S. economics at Bank of America, said economists and the Fed have gotten too complacent about above-target inflation. Higher oil and gas prices will likely keep inflation elevated for several more months, he said, and rising diesel costs will elevate shipping prices for nearly every type of good, which could spread inflation more broadly through the economy.
“Unless the Fed takes this problem more seriously and stops essentially making excuses about inflation, I think we're not going to get back to 2% until the next recession,” Mr. Bhave said.

Mr. Warsh will likely seek to keep the Wednesday (October 28, 2026) press conference relatively short. It was about 30 minutes last month. Mr. Warsh's predecessor, Jerome Powell, often held news conferences for about 45 minutes.

articles.title: Netanyahu and rival each claim mandate after tight Israel election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Exit polls showed Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc neck and neck with Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right camp and both well away from the threshold for a majority in Parliament

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot each vowed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) to form a government after both came up short in the first election since the October 7, 2023 attack traumatised the country.

Voters turned out on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on the divisive rule of Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to the Hamas attack.

Exit polls showed Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc neck and neck with Mr. Netanyahu's hard-right camp and both well away from the threshold for a majority in Parliament.

The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Mr. Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel.

Mr. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3 a.m. (0100 GMT), called for a "strong government of the right" and said that the "Jewish and Zionist majority must unite".
The 77-year-old Prime Minister was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory.
Instead, he listed leaders Israel has killed under his orders and again hinted that he was ready for a third bombing campaign against Iran alongside U.S. President Donald Trump, his close ally.
"Israel has a unique opportunity with our partner President Trump to forever eliminate the existential threat of Iran," Mr. Netanyahu said.
Mr. Eisenkot, speaking to his own supporters in Tel Aviv, issued a veiled warning to Mr. Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government.
"Netanyahu, don't you dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Mr. Eisenkot said.
Addressing Israel's security establishment, Mr. Eisenkot said that they served the state and not Mr. Netanyahu, calling him "a caretaker Prime Minister, without a mandate or the people's trust".
Mr. Eisenkot shares many of Mr. Netanyahu's views on security and has backed the Gaza offensive following October 7 that has reduced the territory to rubble.

articles.title: First Israeli election exit polls show narrow edge for Opposition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”

The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday (October 27, 2026), but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

The country’s main pollsters -- Channels 11, 12 and 13 -- projected the Opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats.

Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them.

In the last election, Likud walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Mr. Netanyahu’s traditional allies baulked at the corruption cases the premier was facing.

This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party -- projected to nab 21 to 23 seats -- to form an Opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu.
“The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Mr. Eisenkot said.
Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”.
While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the Opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it.
Tuesday’s (October 27, 2026) poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future.
The following is a party-by-party breakdown of the projected seat count in the first exit polls
Otzma Yehudit, far-right, led by Itamar Ben Gvir: 6 or 7
United Torah Judaism, Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox, led by Yaakov Asher: 6 or 7

🌐 International Affairs 📅 28 Oct 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

First Israeli election exit polls show narrow edge for Opposition

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”

The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday (October 27, 2026), but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

The country’s main pollsters -- Channels 11, 12 and 13 -- projected the Opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats.

Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them.

In the last election, Likud walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Mr. Netanyahu’s traditional allies baulked at the corruption cases the premier was facing.

This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party -- projected to nab 21 to 23 seats -- to form an Opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu.

“The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Mr. Eisenkot said.

Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”.

While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the Opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it.

Tuesday’s (October 27, 2026) poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future.

The following is a party-by-party breakdown of the projected seat count in the first exit polls

Otzma Yehudit, far-right, led by Itamar Ben Gvir: 6 or 7

United Torah Judaism, Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox, led by Yaakov Asher: 6 or 7

articles.title: Google unveils Genie 4 world model powered by Gemini AI models
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Google’s suggested use cases for Genie 4 included creative direction, making historical scenarios, generating immersive photographs, designing interactive experiences, and simulation
Google on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) announced the launch of its new world model Genie 4, which specialises in realism and real-time interactive simulation.

Genie 4 is natively multimodal and powered by multiple models from the Gemini family. World models are rooted in realistic experiences and outputs, aimed at allowing users to generate true-to-life sequences.
For example, creative users can experiment with world-building elements for games and movies, while scientists could explore aerodynamics and collisions.
Google’s suggested use cases for Genie 4 included creative direction, making historical scenarios, generating immersive photographs, designing interactive experiences, and simulation.
Google stressed that the “most dramatic leap” lay in how Genie 4 simulated people, such as natural-looking and responsive characters.
The company highlighted that Genie 4 was its first real-time world model to generate audio natively.

Google assured users that Genie 4 included strict safety guardrails and had gone through internal safety evaluations. All video and audio generated by Genie 4 will include the company’s SynthID watermark.
Users can also join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie.

“A promising path for future progress lies in hybrid world models, which combine the logical, structured reasoning of code and language models with the rich, sensory representation of pixel-level simulation,” stated Google in a blog post about Genie 4’s infrastructure.

“Gemini works behind the scenes to map the structure and plan the narrative timeline, while Genie generates the immediate physical reality—rendering how the world looks, sounds, and responds, pixel by pixel,” Google added.

articles.title: Hark! It’s the season: for flu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: On unheard-of pathogens, pollution and climate-related health risks, regulation in the healthcare sector, our diets, and more

It is officially the flu season with winter and monsoon seasons creeping in on large parts of the world. There is a need to take precautions and be aware of the risks of the season, particularly at a time when we are hearing of old viruses resurging, or new, never-before heard pathogens rearing their heads, even known microorganisms that cause disease among humans, after a zoonotic spillover.

As in the case of the Shamonda virus. Last week France reported the first human Shamonda virus case, a virus usually circulating amongst livestock . The severely immunocompromised patient died, spurring global public health concerns. While France said there was no health risk as a result of this, there are definitely problems when a new pathogen crosses the barrier. For everything we currently know about the Shamonda virus, read Athira Elssa Johnson ’s explainer, here .

She also writes on Melioidosis in India: a potentially deadly infection that may be going undetected . Melioidosis caused by B. pseudomallei which is found in soil and water in tropical and subtropical regions, can cause pneumonia, bloodstream infection, skin and soft-tissue infections, abscesses in organs such as the liver and spleen, septic arthritis and bone infections. It can also affect the kidneys, muscles and prostate.

Meanwhile, as the second patient in Nigeria, a relative of the first case of death from Ebola in the nation, also died of Ebola, some hopeful news came from DR Congo where the Ebola vaccine trial began for the Bundibugyo strain.
In the U.S., where an early U.S. flu season has set in, doctors warned that the current strain may signal a higher risk for younger people ; and urged them to get shots.
Talking of the weather, it is also time to discuss pollution and climate-related health effects. Nikhil M. Babu writes that air pollution in Delhi-NCR has come ahead of winter .

In Mumbai, Yohaan Varghese says another crisis is brewing, as attention remains on the northern States. Mumbai recorded 231 days of ‘good’ or ‘satisfactory’ air quality in 2026 . The BMC has been forced to unveil a winter pollution action plan.
Geetha Srimathi interprets a global report that claims: Extreme weather, harmful chemicals escalating health risks among food workers .

As a bellwether State for healthcare in the country, what happens in Kerala affects the entire nation, in some way. The Spinal Muscular Atrophy controversy, currently brewing in the southern State too could contain lessons for the nation.

First do read C. Maya’s explainer on what this controversy is all about, here . After the government switched the drug in its SMA programme from branded to generic, parents of children living with SMA have been asking for a switch back to the branded version; meanwhile the label on a drug bottle has sparked concerns, and political parties have now latched on to the issue.

Meanwhile, experts have opined that the Row over SMA drug distribution in Keralam is unwarranted and a hospital rejected charges of ‘clinical trial drugs’ given to children . Further a doctor at SAT Hospital said Parents were actually counselled about the generic drug that was to be used ahead of administration .
We are sure to be following up this story until it reaches its logical conclusion.

articles.title: Google begins rollout of app marketplaces programme outside the U.S.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The initiative, known as the Registered App Stores programme, allows rival app marketplaces to compete at a higher level on the Android platform
Google announced that eligible app stores outside the U.S. can apply to be part of the company’s programme that allows them to access simplified installation perks.
The initiative, known as the Registered App Stores programme, allows rival app marketplaces to compete at a higher level on the Android platform.
Once an App Store is registered with Google, users will be able to install apps listed on those stores with just one tap. Users will now have a choice beyond Google’s own offering.

It remains to be seen if this measure will translate to profitable results for Google’s rivals, who have complained about anti-competitive measures on Android that favour Google’s app marketplace over others.

Android defined registered app stores as a “third-party app store that registers with Google to access additional platform capabilities, including one-tap installs, while upholding core ecosystem trust, security, and performance standards.”
The programme is the result of multiple antitrust challenges against Google over the way it operates its app marketplace on Android devices.
While rivals want their own app marketplaces to get a fair chance at drawing in users on Android devices, Google has claimed that its restrictions are aimed at maintaining user security and privacy.

However, rival app stores will still have to pay steep prices to be part of the programme. Participation costs start at $10,000 a year, and the programme is only supported on Android devices running the latest versions of Android 17, which means a number of users around the world are walled out.
Google announced the Registered App Stores programme in March, and it is set to launch in December.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Google announced the Registered App Stores programme in March, and it is set to launch in December.

articles.title: What is ‘human composting’ — how does it work?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: What should happen to your body after you die? It’s hardly a topic you’d bring up over dinner, but it’s a decision that will eventually need to be made, either by you or by those you leave behind.

In Australia, the choice has traditionally been between burial and cremation. However, concerns about environmental impact, limited cemetery space and the desire for more sustainable alternatives have encouraged interest in other approaches.
These include natural burial, water cremation and shrouded cremation — where no coffin is used.

Now, New South Wales has become the first Australian state to pass legislation allowing another option: “human composting”, technically known as natural organic reduction, and legally termed “terramation”. The process uses microorganisms to transform human remains into a compost-like material.
📢 So-called terramation will become legal in NSW, with several MPs revealing they want their own bodies turned into soil after they die. [image or embed]
The idea of turning a human body into compost might sound unusual, or even unsettling. But how does it actually work? Is it a better alternative to existing methods?
To answer these questions, we first need to understand decomposition and its essential role in nature.
Throughout history, humans have developed rituals to protect, preserve and dress the dead. Some want a quick return to the earth, while others seek to preserve the body.
From ancient burial vessels and elaborate tombs to coffins, shrouds and embalming, these practices reflect cultural and religious beliefs. They also affect how bodies decompose.
Decomposition begins shortly after death. As cells break down, microorganisms already living inside the body, along with those from the surrounding environment, begin breaking down its tissues.

Carrion insects, particularly flies and beetles, can feed on soft tissues remarkably quickly when temperature, moisture and access to the body are favourable. This is nature’s way of recycling organic matter and returning nutrients to the environment.
The body does not simply disappear. But the timescale and extent of its transformation depend on the conditions, processes and materials involved.

articles.title: Alleged Israeli spy company heavily targeted Starlink users, sources say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Finding ways to track Starlink ‌users has become a cottage industry as governments around the world try to get a grip on the spread of satellite internet terminals

Experts at a digital defense firm recently found that an Israeli ad tech company was heavily targeting users of Starlink’s ‌satellite internet service in a likely effort to spy on them, according to six people familiar with the matter.

Researchers at ​TrendAI, a unit of Tokyo-based cybersecurity company Trend Micro, concluded the Israeli company Discover-Tech was one of the biggest sources of digital ⁠ads shown to users of SpaceX’s Starlink service and that the ads were likely being used to geolocate or otherwise surveil them, according to the six people.

The researchers, who drew on digital advertising data in TrendAI’s telemetry for their conclusions, found that Discover-Tech had become one of the world’s leading bidders for ads aimed at Starlink ‌users and that it was the No. 1 bidder on Starlink traffic in more than 100 countries, including several where Starlink itself was banned or restricted. Bidding refers to the complex auction system by which advertisers secure space inside people’s browsers and apps.
SpaceX ‌did not respond to requests for comment. Discover-Tech and its chief executive did not respond to requests for comment over the past two ‌weeks.

articles.title: Trump drastically loosens oil and gas methane rules
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran
U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) a sweeping rollback of rules that stop oil and gas producers from emitting methane, a greenhouse gas super pollutant.
Mr. Trump made the announcement at a rally in support of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who faces a tough battle for a U.S. Senate seat in November 3 midterm elections.
The regulations were put in place by Republican Trump's Democratic predecessor Joe Biden.
"Tonight, I'm officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers $45 billion," Mr. Trump said at the rally in Lubbock, Texas.
To cheers from the crowd, Mr. Trump added that the move would "unlock vast quantities of Texas natural gas." Texas is by far the country's leading fossil-fuel-producing state.
An Environmental Protection Agency statement earlier this month gave the same $45 billion figure in cost savings, without offering a detailed breakdown of the savings.

"Americans must be able to afford to heat their homes in the winter and fill up their car and drive to work," said EPA administrator Lee Zeldin. "They can't do that when the people producing the energy are weighed down by unnecessary burdens."
Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran.
Polls show Republicans could lose control of Congress to the Democrats in next week's vote.

Methane, the main component of natural gas, is the second-largest cause of global warming behind carbon dioxide — responsible for about a third, or 0.5°C, of total planetary heating since the pre-industrial era.
A molecule of methane traps far more heat than carbon dioxide, but persists in the atmosphere for only seven to 12 years, whereas carbon dioxide can last for hundreds of years.

The changes take aim at rules to curb methane emissions from oil and gas operations. Emissions occur at every stage, from extracting gas held underground, to processing, transmission and distribution.

articles.title: Karnataka Council polls: BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four seats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The biggest upset for the Congress came from Bengaluru Teachers constituency where five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman Puttanna lost to NDA candidate A.P. Ranganath.

In a setback to the ruling Congress, the BJP-JD(S) alliance won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats that went to polls on October 23 — two teachers’ and two graduates’ constituencies. Congress earlier held one of the four seats.

The biggest upset for Congress came from Bengaluru Teachers constituency where five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman Puttanna lost to NDA candidate A.P. Ranganath. BJP candidate Shashil G. Namoshi secured his fifth victory in the North-East Teachers’ constituency, defeating Congress nominee Sharanappa Mattur.

In the West Graduates’ constituency, S.V. Sankanur secured his third consecutive victory , defeating Congress’s Mohan Limbikai. In South East Graduates’ constituency, BJP candidate K.M. Suresha defeated Congress candidate Shashi Hulikuntemutt.

The result has rejuvenated the NDA partners, who were jolted earlier this year after cross-voting of 11 of its MLAs during the poll to seven Legislative Council seats in June. The Congress had won five out of seven seats and the saffron party had won two. Earlier in May, the Congress had also won Davangere South and Bagalkot bypolls , retaining both the seats despite strong internal differences.

The victory is being seen as a result of the co-ordinated effort betwee the BJP and JD(S) that paid off. It has shown that the partners can transfer their support to each other’s candidates. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar acknowledged the defeat and said that they would introspect on it, but insisted that it was no “precursor” to the future elections as interpreted by the NDA partners.
Though the Council election results will not affect the stability of the Congress government, the strong performance of the NDA partners will give the opposition a momentum.

articles.title: SCR rolls out GPS tracking devices for 1,800 patrolmen across three divisions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Railway patrolemn check for loose fish bolts, defects in switches and crossings, damaged fittings on girder bridges and open-top culverts, broken or burnt sleepers, damaged plates and tie bars, and other track-related issues

South Central Railway (SCR), in order to further enhance the safety in train operations , has introduced 1,800 GPS tracker devices to the patrolmen/trackmen covering all the three divisions of Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Nanded.

These devices are intended to assist patrolmen and track maintainers who play a crucial role in ensuring the safe and punctual movement of trains. These frontline railway workers inspect tracks, bridges and other infrastructure round the clock to detect defects and prevent accidents.

Every day and night, patrolmen walk along railway lines and bridges carrying essential equipment while keeping a close watch on track conditions. Depending on the section assigned, they cover distances ranging from three kilometres on single-line routes to six kilometres on double-line routes during each patrol.

Their responsibilities include checking for loose fish bolts, defects in switches and crossings, damaged fittings on girder bridges and open-top culverts, broken or burnt sleepers, damaged plates and tie bars, and other track-related issues. They also monitor water levels and the flow of water near railway infrastructure, particularly during adverse weather conditions, according to senior railway officials.

Whenever a patrolman notices a broken rail, damaged weld, ballast washout, theft of fittings or any other serious defect, he is required to immediately protect the track as per railway safety rules, take preliminary corrective measures wherever possible and alert the nearest Station Master, Permanent Way Inspector and his supervisor.
South Central Railway (SCR) patrolman at work | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT

The GPS-enabled devices will also allow supervisors to monitor patrolmen’s movements in real time. Each tracker, fitted with a SIM card, will be mapped to an individual patrolman and must be carried and switched on while on duty. The system will also alert supervisors if a patrolman deviates from the designated patrol route.

“This device will also help ensure the personal safety of patrolling staff by identifying their exact location. It has three alert buttons to contact immediate supervisors and an ‘SOS’ button for emergencies,” said SCR Chief Public Relations Officer A. Sridhar. The GPS devices will store movement data for up to six months, which can help railway authorities verify ground conditions and investigate any untoward incidents, he added.

articles.title: Supreme Court terms cybercrime as digital dacoity, refuses consolidation of cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Strongly condemning the organised cybercrime rackets targeting senior citizens through digital arrests, the CJI said those involved must face stringent action

Terming cybercrime as “digital dacoity”, the Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) refused to consolidate over 30 criminal complaints pending against two persons in 12 states for allegedly allowing the use of their company’s account as a mule for the commission of various offences.

“Digital arrests and such cyber offences are digital dacoity… there is no question of giving any judicial forum to such persons,” a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said.
Strongly condemning the organised cybercrime rackets targeting senior citizens through digital arrests, the CJI said those involved must face stringent action.
“An 81-year-old from Ernakulam (Kerala) was defrauded of ₹1.90 crore and his money was deposited in your mule account,” the CJI said.
“You decided to use the account of your company for cybercrime like digital arrest,” the Bench said while refusing to entertain the plea of Gourab Kumar Saha and Nidhi Bhandari.
The Bench refused to allow the accused to use such proceedings to disrupt investigations in different States.
Justice Bagchi asked as to why victims should be forced to travel to Delhi merely for the convenience of an accused seeking consolidation.

“Your right to seek transfer of cases to a place of your convenience cannot override the right of the victims and the investigating agency… We can consider it if Delhi police say so for the convenience of investigation. We do not take your weight to dilute the investigation across the country,” Justice Bagchi said.

The CJI asked if a victim, whose defrauded money was deposited in Hong Kong and Bangkok, could be asked to go there for redress. The petitioner ultimately withdrew the plea. Thirty-five criminal cases pertaining to cybercrimes are pending against the accused in states including Delhi, Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana and Gujarat.

“You decided to use the account of your company for cybercrime like digital arrest,” the Bench said while refusing to entertain the plea of Gourab Kumar Saha and Nidhi Bhandari.

The Bench refused to allow the accused to use such proceedings to disrupt investigations in different States.

Justice Bagchi asked as to why victims should be forced to travel to Delhi merely for the convenience of an accused seeking consolidation.

articles.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear challenge to definition of ‘industry’ in new Central law
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Trade Union Congress Tamil Nadu’s petition challenged the definition of ‘industry’ under the Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020 as “deliciously vague”; The senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan said the definition in the IRC Code did not meet the requirements of the ‘triple test’

The Supreme Court agreed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) to hear a petition filed by the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) Tamil Nadu challenging the definition of ‘industry’ under the Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020 as “deliciously vague”, especially when the new law exempts a wide array of institutions from charitable to sovereign functions of the government.

The IRC affords legal protections to workers who are employed in institutions which come under the ambit of ‘industry’. Section 2(p) of the IRC defines industry as any institution engaged in a “systematic activity carried on by co-operation between an employer and worker for the production, supply or distribution of goods or services with a view to satisfy human wants or wishes”.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan and advocate Aarthi Rajan, for the trade union, referred to the exceptions to ‘industry’ listed in the Code.

Mr. Sankaranarayanan submitted that the exceptions to ‘industry’ included institutions wholly or substantially engaged in charitable, social or philanthropic service to “any activity of the appropriate government relatable to sovereign functions” to “any other activity as may be notified by the Central government”.
“Is there a problem with the definition of ‘industry’?” Chief Justice Kant asked.
Editorial | Triple test, adrift: On the ruling on definition of ‘industry’

The senior counsel said the definition in the Code did not meet the requirements of the ‘triple test’. A 1978 seven-judge Constitution Bench judgment, authored by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer, in the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa case, had laid down conditions that any activity which was systematic or organised, operated on the basis of employer-employee cooperation and dealt in the production of goods and services to satisfy human wants came within the ambit of ‘industry’. The judgment had brought even hospitals, educational institutions and municipalities within the fold of ‘industry’.

In August 2026, a nine-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Kant had reviewed the interpretation given by Justice Iyer in 1978 to the definition of ‘industry’ under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. However, the nine-judge Bench had been preceded by the coming into force of the 2020 Code, which largely made the reference to it infructuous.

The majority on the nine-judge Bench in August this year had held that ‘industry’ under Section 2(p) of the Industrial Relations Code (IRC), which came into force in November 2025, would not be “burdened” by the interpretation in the 1978 judgment of Section 2(j) of the 1947 Act.

In his majority opinion, Chief Justice Kant had clarified that the 1978 judgment and its conclusion would not act as the “sheet anchor” or the foundation for any future interpretation of Section 2(p) of the IRC.
“The future of ‘industry’ in Section 2(p) of IRC is not burdened by the interpretation of 2(j) in the Industrial Disputes Act,” Chief Justice Kant had observed in the August 2026 judgment.

In fact, the CJI’s opinion had even suggested a “refinement” of the 1978 triple test. While acknowledging that the core principles of the test had stood the test of time in deciding industrial disputes, the CJI said its elements could have been “articulated differently so that the scope and contours of 2(j) could have been better reflected”. However, the CJI had said this was only a “considered opinion”, and should not be used to displace the governing legal position on pending proceedings or dig up decided cases.
