articles.title: Mizoram aims to be first state to complete Census 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Secretary Khilli Ram Meena chaired a State-level conference here to review preparations for the second phase of the census, including training and field arrangements

Mizoram aims to become the first state to complete Census 2027 , with the State government stepping up preparations for the population enumeration exercise, officials said on Saturday (October 10, 2026).
Chief Secretary Khilli Ram Meena chaired a State-level conference here to review preparations for the second phase of the census, including training and field arrangements.
Mr. Meena stressed the need to ensure accuracy and thoroughness, noting that census data would play a crucial role in policymaking and in achieving the national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
He said the second phase would require greater effort than the first and urged officials to work with dedication to ensure its timely completion.
He also called on them to make Mizoram the first state to complete the exercise, a target the state had set during the first phase as well.
Deputy Director of Census Operations Jamil R. Swer explained the procedures for the second phase and proposed training arrangements.
All 16 Scheduled Castes in Mizoram will be counted, and refugees residing in the state will also be included in the census, officials said.
The inclusion of refugees would not confer Indian citizenship, they said.
Officials also said people who do not wish to share their Aadhaar numbers must not be compelled to do so.
Those excluded from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls for any reason will be counted in the census, they added.
Training for master trainers, field trainers, enumerators and supervisors is scheduled to be completed in November. Each enumerator is expected to cover around 800 people.
The Centre has allocated ₹19.19 crore to Mizoram for conducting the second phase of Census 2027, officials said.

articles.title: Israel elections: Understanding how Knesset polls work vs India’s system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israel’s political clash after the October 27 national vote pits Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu against former military chief Gadi Eisenkot in a neck-and-neck fight to form a government, as neither major bloc won a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat Knesset
Israel faces a high-stakes political standoff after the October 27 national election, the country’s first vote since the 2023 Hamas attack.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his chief rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot of the Yashar party, have both claimed a mandate to form the next government after exit polls showed their respective camps in a neck-and-neck fight without an outright majority, leaving the outcome dependent on the final seat tally and negotiations with smaller parties.

The main difference between Israeli and Indian elections lies in how votes translate into seats. Israel operates under a nationwide system of proportional representation, treating the country as a single voting constituency without separate geographic districts or local MPs. Israelis do not vote for individual candidates. Instead, they cast a single ballot for a closed party list and the 120 seats in parliament, known as the Knesset, are allocated in direct proportion to each party’s share of the national vote.

Meanwhile, India employs a first-past-the-post system (FPTP) across 543 parliamentary constituencies. Indian citizens cast ballots for local candidates in their respective constituencies and whichever candidate secures a majority vote in a constituency wins that seat.

No single political party has ever won an outright 61-seat majority in Israel’s history. With the exit polls on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) too predicting no outright majority for any bloc, forming a coalition government appears to be their only way to go. To enter the 120-seat Knesset, a political list must clear an electoral threshold of 3.25% of the national vote, which equals roughly four seats. Parties that fall short of this line lose all their votes without representation, making party mergers and alliances pertinent ahead of candidate submission deadlines.

For instance, Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition comprises his own right-wing party Likud, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s pro-settler Religious ⁠Zionism and ​National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s far-right Jewish Power.

To form a ruling government in Israel, a coalition must assemble at least 61 seats. This is a requirement that grants small niche factions a disproportionate sway as political kingmakers. If internal divisions cause a minor party to withdraw its support, the entire administration can quickly fall apart. In contrast, Indian political parties frequently build post-poll or pre-poll alliances. Additionally, major national parties in India can and often do win single-party majority mandates without relying on minor regional partners for survival.

In India, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party secured outright single-party majority in back-to-back general elections, winning 282 seats in 2014 and 303 seats in 2019, well above the 272-seat majority mark in the 543-member Lok Sabha. But in the 2024 general elections, the PM Modi-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) bagged only 286 seats, with the BJP winning 240 seats and falling 32 short of the majority mark of 272 seats, prompting a coalition with their allies.

After the official results are published, Israel President Isaac Herzog will consult representatives of the elected parliamentary factions before assigning a lawmaker the task of forming a government.
The President generally selects the candidate considered best placed to secure parliamentary support, rather than being required to choose the leader of the largest party.

The first nominee has 28 days to form a government, with the President able to grant extensions of up to 14 additional days. If the attempt fails, another lawmaker may be given an opportunity. If subsequent efforts also fail, the process could lead to another election.

articles.title: Two trains collide in Spain’s Toledo province; at least 30 dead
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The accident was between two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital, Madrid, to Seville in southwestern Spain

A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) in central Spain, according to local media.
Spanish authorities initially reported 10 deaths, but Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the Castilla La Mancha region, added “that number will surely rise.”
Spanish state-owned news agency EFE and other media reported later that the death toll had risen to at least 30.

People check an information screen displaying a message that the high-speed train line between Madrid and Andalucia has been interrupted following the collision of two high-speed trains between the towns of Mora and Orgaz at Atocha train station in Madrid, Spain, on October 28, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters
It was the second major train accident in Spain this year.
Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning (October 28, 2026) in the province of Toledo. Rail service was suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.

Ms. Padilla told state broadcaster TVE that the accident was between two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital, Madrid, to Seville in southwestern Spain. One ran into the tail of the other that had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track. She said the cause of the crash was not known.

The crash, which occurred in a flat stretch surrounded by fields in between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, left one car shredded into bits of metal and other material, scattering debris down a gravel slope.

Spanish Health Minister Mónica García told TVE that emergency workers were focusing on rescuing survivors and bodies from the two most damaged train cars. She said that the injured are being sent to different hospitals in the area.
“It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy,” Mr. García said.

The accident involved a train from Spain’s state-owned RENFE company and the private rail company IRYO. It appeared the RENFE train rammed the IRYO train, Spanish media reported. Trains from those two companies were also involved in a deadly crash in January.
Ms. Padilla said that 397 passengers were in the RENFE train and 147 passengers in the IRYO train.

articles.title: Israel polls: Golan urges Eisenkot's bloc to form government with Arab parties to oust Netanyahu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Several allies in the Opposition's change bloc have rejected the proposal to include Arab parties in a governing coalition, while some have also ruled out relying on their support from outside

Yair Golan, leader of Israel's Democratic Party, on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) urged the Opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form a government in partnership with Arab-led parties to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, highlighting divisions within the opposition over such cooperation.
Several allies in the Opposition's "change bloc" have rejected the proposal to include Arab parties in a governing coalition, while some have also ruled out relying on their support from outside.
"Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120. 65 is more than 55. That's how Israeli democracy works. Period," Mr. Golan, a former deputy chief of staff of the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), wrote on X.
Mr. Golan called for an end to what he described as racism and fear of political cooperation with Arab citizens.

"The picture of reality must teach us one resounding lesson: We have no future here if we don't stop being afraid. And if we don't stop with the racism. We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," he wrote.

"The voice of an Israeli citizen voting in Taybeh is worth exactly as much as the voice of an Israeli citizen voting in Givat Shmuel. No less. Not approximately. Exactly," he said, arguing that Arab citizens' votes should carry the same weight as those of Jewish citizens.
"Anyone who tries to erase the voices of Arab citizens is surrendering to Netanyahu and giving up on Israel," he added.

Mr. Golan's proposal faces resistance from Opposition figures who have ruled out forming a government that includes Arab-led parties. The Opposition remains divided over whether Arab parties should join a governing coalition or support it from outside.
Mr. Golan also challenged Mr. Netanyahu's allies over their claims to represent Zionism, criticising ultra-Orthodox parties in the Prime Minister's bloc for opposing universal military conscription.
"In Netanyahu's bloc sit 16 Knesset members from non-Zionist Haredi parties, who promote mass draft evasion while our children are fighting and dying," Mr. Golan wrote.
He argued that the opposition had a Zionist majority of its own, saying, "The Change bloc has a Zionist majority: 49 against 39. The Change bloc has an Israeli majority: 65 against 55."

Urging Opposition leaders to cooperate with Arab citizens, Mr. Golan said: "We have a majority. We have responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel's Arab citizens. A government that will serve all Israeli citizens."

articles.title: Can you punish laxity by forfeiting the right to vote forever, Supreme Court asks ECI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Form 6 is ‘cast in stone’ and cannot be changed, says SC, adding that the Bihar judgment is not a binding precedent and that it allowed ‘logical discrepancy’ in West Bengal as an ‘interim arrangement’; top court tells ECI to extend Delhi SIR

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) questioned the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) authority to deprive citizens forever of their right to vote simply because they were lax in returning enumeration forms during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which has disenfranchised nearly 13 crore voters across the country.

“Let us say a voter was lax, inert or did not respond, will that be a ground for you, the Election Commission of India, to forfeit his or her right to vote forever? We will answer that,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi, a judge on the Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, addressed the poll body.
The court said the ECI was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral roll, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Petitioners, activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, represented by advocates Prashant Bhushan and Neha Rathi, submitted that the ECI was compelling voters to misrepresent themselves as new applicants, an offence which attracts imprisonment.

“You cannot touch these Forms. Form 6, Form 7 [for objection to proposed inclusion/deletion of names in the existing electoral roll], and Form 8 [application for shifting of residence] are cast in stone… You cannot make changes to them,” Justice Bagchi said.
Senior advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, for the ECI, said the court’s Bihar SIR judgment on May 27 had mentioned that the poll body had “residuary powers”.

Justice Bagchi asked why the ECI had not then used these residuary powers to reach out to voters who had not responded to enumeration forms. “You could have asked for a declaration, giving them a chance, giving them time to explain why they did not respond to the enumeration forms,” the judge said.
Besides, Justice Bagchi clarified that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent”.

“First and foremost, in Bihar SIR, the EC had not undertaken ‘logical discrepancy’ as a category. We had permitted you in West Bengal as an interim arrangement… We have not finally adjudicated on the legality of ‘logical discrepancy’,” Justice Bagchi spoke for the Bench.
Justice Bagchi asked how voters, included in the 2003 electoral roll after an intensive revision, could be purged in the name of ‘logical discrepancy’ in 2026.
Mr. Bhushan said the ECI’s approach to voters in the Delhi SIR was short-sighted.

“It ran like ‘you were absent at your address when we came with the enumeration form, you are deleted from the electoral roll’. Of the 1,45,10,299 electors in Delhi at the start of the SIR, 47,56,722 were marked as having not returned their enumeration forms on account of being absent, shifted, dead or duplicate entries,” he submitted.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “It ran like ‘you were absent at your address when we came with the enumeration form, you are deleted from the electoral roll’. articles.title: Rockfall disrupts traffic in Idukki
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A large mass of rock and soil collapsed onto the road, halting traffic on the highway for nearly half an hour.

A rockfall and debris slide occurred at Amalagiri on the Kuttikkanam–Mundakayam stretch of the Kottarakara–Dindigul National Highway on Wednesday morning. According to local residents, a large mass of rock and soil collapsed onto the road, halting traffic on the highway for nearly half an hour. Local residents and officials rushed to the spot, cleared the debris, and restored vehicular movement.

​Meanwhile, repeated incidents of rockfalls and landslips along the highway continue to pose a serious threat to commuters. The Mundakayam–Kuttikkanam stretch is a vital route connecting Idukki with Kottayam and Pathanamthitta districts.

​Two months ago, a major landslip occurred along this stretch, causing widespread traffic disruptions. Following the incident, the district administration banned night travel on the route for several days to prevent casualties.

articles.title: Food Commission reviews nutrition supplies in Attappadi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The inspection followed reports of infant deaths in Attappadi, suspected to be linked to malnutrition

The State Food Commission has directed officials to ensure the quality of nutrition supplies distributed at anganwadis and schools in Attappadi. A team led by Commission chairperson Jinu Zacharia Oommen and member Murukesh Cherunali inspected anganwadis in Donigundu, Vadakottathara and Vechappathy hamlets, and the tribal high school at Mattathukad in Attappadi on Wednesday.

The inspection followed reports of infant deaths in Attappadi, suspected to be linked to malnutrition. The commission sought an explanation after finding packets of pulses and chickpeas at anganwadis without expiry dates.
The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) district programme officer said wheat supplies to anganwadis had declined because wheat meeting fair average quality (FAQ) standards was unavailable.

The Commission said nutrition supplies were being distributed to pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers and children in areas where child deaths had been reported. It added that the families of the deceased children had also received the supplies.
The Janani Janma Raksha scheme was being implemented as prescribed, it said. The Commission also checked the mid-day meal programme at the school.

District Supply Officer A.S. Beena, Taluk Supply Officer V. Manoj, Mannarkkad Taluk Supply Officer M.K. Anees, Assistant Taluk Supply Officer Ranjini, ICDS District Programme Officer T.V. Minimol, Child Protection Officer Sreelatha and other officials were also present.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc at Odalarevu fishing villager, over 100 boats destroyed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nearly one hundred boats have broken, another hundred more boats were scattered and dozens of boats were sunk in the backwaters near the confluence of Godavari river into the sea after cyclone Arnab made its landfall near Odalarevu village

Following the landfall of Cyclone Arnab, the coastal village of Odalarevu faced near the confluence point where the Vynateya branch of the Godavari River meets the Bay of Bengal faced severe devastation as violent winds and surging backwaters swept away and destroyed a large number of fishing boats anchored along the riverbanks.

Fishermen and their families scrambled to recover their boats, engines and equipment from the water. Women joined the men in the recovery efforts. Wading through neck-deep water and harsh weather conditions, they spent hours cutting through the tangled fishing nets and pulling their boats out of the water as they tried to salvage whatever they could.
Fishermen recovers a boat with crane at Odalarevu village in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district where cyclone Arnab made landfall on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU
Of the approximately 300 boats anchored at the Odalarevu fish landing centre, over 100 were broken into pieces, while nearly 100 others were scattered along the riverbanks or submerged under water.

Individual families reported losing boats worth over ₹3 lakh each. Additionally, specialised nets used to catch prawn, pomfret (chanduva), and tuna were damaged beyond repair after becoming entangled in the wreckage.
Local residents said that instead of catching fish to earn a living, families were forced to spend hours searching for their destroyed boats from the water.
Uprooted coconut trees at Bandamurulanka village in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU

The cyclone’s impact was equally severe onshore. Dozens of coconut trees were uprooted across Odalarevu, blocking roads and snapping power lines, leaving the village without electricity. Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc at Odalarevu fishing villager, over 100 boats destroyed

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Nearly one hundred boats have broken, another hundred more boats were scattered and dozens of boats were sunk in the backwaters near the confluence of Godavari river into the sea after cyclone Arnab made its landfall near Odalarevu village

Following the landfall of Cyclone Arnab, the coastal village of Odalarevu faced near the confluence point where the Vynateya branch of the Godavari River meets the Bay of Bengal faced severe devastation as violent winds and surging backwaters swept away and destroyed a large number of fishing boats anchored along the riverbanks.

Fishermen and their families scrambled to recover their boats, engines and equipment from the water. Women joined the men in the recovery efforts. Wading through neck-deep water and harsh weather conditions, they spent hours cutting through the tangled fishing nets and pulling their boats out of the water as they tried to salvage whatever they could.

Fishermen recovers a boat with crane at Odalarevu village in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district where cyclone Arnab made landfall on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU

Of the approximately 300 boats anchored at the Odalarevu fish landing centre, over 100 were broken into pieces, while nearly 100 others were scattered along the riverbanks or submerged under water.

Individual families reported losing boats worth over ₹3 lakh each. Additionally, specialised nets used to catch prawn, pomfret (chanduva), and tuna were damaged beyond repair after becoming entangled in the wreckage.

Local residents said that instead of catching fish to earn a living, families were forced to spend hours searching for their destroyed boats from the water.

Uprooted coconut trees at Bandamurulanka village in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU

The cyclone’s impact was equally severe onshore. Dozens of coconut trees were uprooted across Odalarevu, blocking roads and snapping power lines, leaving the village without electricity. Local residents estimate the total damage to exceed ₹3 crore, and fear it could take up to a year for the fishing community to fully recover.

articles.title: Mysuru e-Khata drive receives 708 applications across nine zones
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Eligible applicants to receive e-Khatas by 4 p.m. on October 31

The special Prajaseva e-Khata drive organised by the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) on Wednesday received 708 applications across the city’s nine zones, reflecting a good response from citizens seeking faster delivery of the property document service.

The drive was held at the old Council Hall which was overseen by Regional Commissioner Nitesh Patil, who is also the MCC Administrator. The MCC provided an opportunity to the property owners to get e-khata certificates at ₹175, including ₹165 service charge and ₹10 registration charge. Property owners from all nine zones attended the drive.

The drive was conducted under the guidance of Regional Commissioner, MCC Commissioner M.K. Savita, Zonal commissioners, revenue officers, assistant revenue officers, revenue inspectors and other corporation staff participated in the programme.

Zone-3 received the highest number of applications at 144, followed by Zone-2 with 124 and Zone-9 with 91. Zone-7 received 82 applications, Zone-8 received 69, Zone-1 received 55, Zone-5 received 48, while Zones 4 and 6 received 44 applications each.
The MCC has said that applications will be scrutinised and applicants will be informed of deficiencies if the required documents are missing or if discrepancies are found in the submissions.

Eligible applications that meet the prescribed requirements and are accompanied by the necessary documents, including the Encumbrance Certificate (EC), will be processed for e-Khata issuance by 4 p.m. on Saturday.
The special drive was organised to simplify the e-Khata process and expedite the delivery of services to citizens.

articles.title: Thunderstorm forecast for 12 Telangana districts for October 29
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A day after v arious parts of Telangana received rain under the impact of cyclonic storm Arnab , isolated places in 12 districts are likely to receive thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds on Thursday (October 29). The very severe cyclonic storm crossed Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Wednesday morning, before weakening into a severe cyclonic storm.

The 12 districts where thunderstorms have been forecast are Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanumakonda districts, as per the India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre’s latest weather bulletin.

On Wednesday, various parts of Khammam, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Suryapet and Mahabubabad received rainfall between 10 mm and 31 mm till 6 p.m. And, less than 10 mm rainfall was recorded in some parts of Mancherial, Nalgonda, Hanumakonda, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Jayashankar Bhupalapally, Warangal and Medchal Malkajgiri, as per the Telangana Development Planning Society’s data. In Hyderabad, overcast skies hovered till the evening at least.

The cyclone had an impact on temperatures as they dropped by 3C to 6C in various parts of the State in the past 24 hours, as per IMD’s report issued late on Wednesday evening. The sharpest drop of 5.8C was recorded at Bhadrachalam weather observatory, followed by 5C in Nizamabad and Hyderabad, and 4.5C in Hanumakonda.

articles.title: India and Mexico sign Terms of Reference for preferential trade agreement negotiations to begin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal visited Mexico for the signing. The two sides also discussed a possible business delegation from Mexico visiting India in the first quarter of 2027
India and Mexico on Wednesday signed the Terms of Reference (ToR) to start negotiations on a trade deal between the two countries, the government announced following the signing in Mexico.

The signing of the ToR follows an understanding reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum during their meeting on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Canada in June 2025.

“Mexico and India take an important step towards strengthening their economic and trade relations with the signing of the Terms of Reference for negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA), which establish the framework, scope, modalities and roadmap for negotiations aimed at creating new economic opportunities for both countries,” the government said in a release.

During the signing, the Indian side was represented by Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal, who held discussions with Mexico’s Undersecretary of Foreign Trade Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez Romano, who participated on behalf of Secretary of Economy Marcelo Ebrard Casaubon.

“The Terms of Reference cover key negotiating areas, including market access for goods, rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, dispute settlement, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade and trade remedies,” the release said.

“With its strong linkages to global value chains, Mexico is an important market for Indian exporters and investors,” it added. “Sectors with significant potential for cooperation include automotive, chemicals, electronics, pharmaceuticals, agri-food, energy, critical minerals, medical devices and advanced manufacturing, among others.”
Mr. Agrawal and Mr. Romano also discussed the possibility of organising a Mexican business mission to India during the first quarter of 2027.

“The proposed mission would facilitate business-to-business meetings, help identify commercial opportunities and strengthen commercial ties between the productive sectors of the two countries,” the government said.

articles.title: Israel president urges against new vote despite inconclusive result
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: With more than 85% of ballots counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority in the election

Israel's president voiced hope on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) for avoiding a second election after a hard-fought vote produced no clear winner, leaving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the Opposition scrambling for options and making Israeli Arab parties possible kingmakers.

With more than 85% of ballots counted, Mr. Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority in Tuesday's (October 27) election, the first since the October 7, 2023 attack that led Israel to wage war in Gaza and across the region.

Both Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister who is allied with far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, and Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief leading a broad opposition bloc, said they would seek to form the next government.
But neither looks set to reach the 61-seat threshold, with Mr. Netanyahu's bloc projected to win 53 of the 120 seats in parliament and Eisenkot's opposition set for 48.
The final results could still change, but one place of clear gains was among Israeli Arab lists, which were set to jump to 19 seats.

"We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections," said President Isaac Herzog, who is tasked with determining which candidate to tap to form a government, and who urged parties to keep "an open mind".

Yousef Jabareen, head of the leftist Arab-majority Joint List, said the Israeli public had voted for new leadership and "anyone who wants to offer a substantive and genuine alternative to Netanyahu's blood-soaked government will have to talk to us".
"It's either the continuation of racism, the continuation of exclusion and the continuation of supremacy, or a genuine Jewish-Arab partnership," he said.

Voters from the Arab community, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel's creation and make up around 20% of the population, have been enraged by the Netanyahu government's ultra-nationalist Jewish vision for the country and the Palestinian territories.
Mr. Netanyahu, during the campaign, relentlessly attacked the opposition by saying it would put Arabs in power, running on the slogan: "Either the Right or Palestine."
Yair Golan, the head of Israel's main left-wing party and a member of Eisenkot's camp, became its first to call for an alliance with the Arab lists.
"We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes," Golan said in a social media post.

articles.title: Two trains collide in Spain’s Toledo Province; at least 64 dead
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The accident was between two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital, Madrid, to Seville in southwestern Spain

The death toll from a high-speed train collision south of Madrid on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) has more than doubled to 64, Spanish regional authorities said, warning the figure was still likely to increase.

"We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more," the leader of the central region of Castilla-La Mancha, Emiliano Garcia-Page, told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31.

People check an information screen displaying a message that the high-speed train line between Madrid and Andalucia has been interrupted following the collision of two high-speed trains between the towns of Mora and Orgaz at Atocha train station in Madrid, Spain, on October 28, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters
It was the second major train accident in Spain this year.
Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning (October 28, 2026) in the Province of Toledo. Rail service was suspended between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia.

Ms. Padilla told state broadcaster TVE that the accident was between two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital, Madrid, to Seville in southwestern Spain. One ran into the tail of the other that had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track. She said the cause of the crash was not known.

The crash, which occurred in a flat stretch surrounded by fields in between the towns of Urda and Los Yébenes, left one car shredded into bits of metal and other material, scattering debris down a gravel slope.

Spanish Health Minister Mónica García told TVE that emergency workers were focusing on rescuing survivors and bodies from the two most damaged train cars. She said that the injured are being sent to different hospitals in the area.
“It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy,” Mr. García said.

The accident involved a train from Spain’s state-owned RENFE company and the private rail company IRYO. It appeared the RENFE train rammed the IRYO train, Spanish media reported. Trains from those two companies were also involved in a deadly crash in January.
Ms. Padilla said that 397 passengers were in the RENFE train and 147 passengers in the IRYO train.
IRYO, an Italian-owned company, said in a statement that it has “activated its security protocols and is closely working with authorities.”

articles.title: Israeli Arab parties hold key as Netanyahu falls short of majority
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: With more than three-quarters of the vote counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority

Results from Israel's hard-fought election pointed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026)to no clear winner as a leader of the Arab minority appealed to a hesitant opposition to join forces to end the divisive reign of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

With more than three-quarters of the vote counted, Mr. Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority in Tuesday's (October 27) election, the first since the October 7, 2023 attack, which has led Israel to wage war in Gaza and across the region.

Both Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister who is allied with far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties, and Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief leading a broad opposition bloc, vowed that they would seek to form the next government.
But neither looks set to reach the 61-seat threshold for a majority. With 77% of ballots counted, Mr. Netanyahu's bloc had 54 of the 120 seats in parliament and Eisenkot's opposition had 49.
The final results could still change but one place of clear gains was among Israeli Arab lists which were set to jump to 17 seats.

Voters from the community, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel's creation and who make up around 20% of the population, have been enraged by the Netanyahu government's ultra-nationalist Jewish vision for the country and the Palestinian territories.

Yousef Jabareen, head of the leftist Arab-majority Joint List, said the Israeli public had voted for new leadership, and "anyone who wants to offer a substantive and genuine alternative to Netanyahu's blood-soaked government will have to talk to us".
"It's either the continuation of racism, the continuation of exclusion and the continuation of supremacy, or a genuine Jewish-Arab partnership," he said.

Mr. Eisenkot has resisted allying with Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu, during the campaign, relentlessly attacked the Opposition by saying it would put Arabs in power, running on the slogan: "Either the Right or Palestine."
Yair Golan, the head of Israel's main left-wing party and a member of Mr. Eisenkot's camp, became the first member of the Opposition camp to call for an alliance with Arab parties.
"Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120," Mr. Golan said in a social media post. "We must no longer accept Netanyahu's racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes."
But Mr. Eisenkot's camp also includes right-wingers who share many of Mr. Netanyahu's hawkish views and have adamantly rejected working with Arab lawmakers.

articles.title: Vehicle data shared only in masked form: ULIP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Clarification comes after Road Ministry sought audit of users accessing the Centre’s logistics portal following complaints that multiple apps and websites are selling vehicle information

After the Road Ministry sought an audit of users accessing the Centre’s logistics portal following complaints that multiple apps and websites were selling vehicle information, the Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) rejected the allegations of its misuse. It said all data were masked and called for broader scrutiny of the platforms involved.

“ULIP relays information in the format received from the source API. For example, vehicle owner names, chassis and engine numbers retain their masking, and the mobile number field remains null in both the source response and the response provided to users. ULIP does not independently generate, unmask or enrich the underlying data,” ULIP wrote in response to a story in The Hindu .

The Road Ministry sought an audit after finding that some entities were extracting data in large volumes from ULIP with some as many pulling out as many as 50 lakh records a month. The Road Ministry shares vehicle information with multiple government agencies and private firms from its portals such as VAHAN, SARATHI, e-Challan and PUCC portals.

ULIP says it uses sufficient safeguards that include screening of entities that have access to its portal, their proposed use cases, binding terms and conditions, IP whitelisting, phased onboarding and continuous monitoring of API usage. This framework complies with the Road Ministry’s Policy for Data Sharing from the National Transport Repository, which prescribes authentication, secret keys, masking of personally identifiable information (PII) and defined approval mechanisms, ULIP added.

Referring to multiple apps selling vehicle information data in unmasked form, ULIP said there needed to be a “scrutiny of wider ecosystem of platforms and channels through which such information is being made available”.

The Road Ministry has written to the government’s nodal agency for investigating cybersecurity incidents, Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), seeking a forensic audit of VAHAN, SARATHI, e-Challan and PUCC portals, which hold a range of vehicle-owner information.

It has also sought the intervention of the Ministry of Electronics and Information and Technology (MEITY) for a review of its data sharing policy and suggest ways to strengthen it. The Road Ministry also plans to audit various enforcement agencies that access its portals for data.

The Ministry’s action follows reports that apps and websites were selling vehicle-linked personal data for as little as ₹5. A Cyderes investigation found that a Telegram-based broker could retrieve an owner’s name, contact details, addresses and other records from a vehicle registration number, along with driving licence, challan, FASTag and registration certificate information. The Ministry has asked major app-store operators, including Google, to remove such apps.

articles.title: How imaging offers a window to treat wake-up strokes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: One in five ischaemic strokes is a wake-up stroke. “This means a person wakes up from his/her sleep with symptoms of stroke. The symptoms include facial drooping, difficulty speaking, sudden vision problems and weakness on one side of the body

Time is brain, when it comes to the treatment of strokes. But a stroke occurring during sleep may go unnoticed until a person wakes up with symptoms, leaving doctors without a clear timeline of its onset. This is where brain imaging helps doctors identify patients with wake-up strokes and assess the extent of injury to pave the way for prompt treatment. Neurologists underscore the need to seek medical care immediately to ensure timely treatment.

M. Radha, head of department and professor of neurology, Government Kilpauk Medical College (KMC) Hospital, Chennai, said that the prevalence of wake-up strokes is 20% - one in five ischaemic strokes is a wake-up stroke. “This means a person wakes up from his/her sleep with symptoms of stroke. The symptoms include facial drooping, difficulty speaking, sudden vision problems and weakness on one side of the body,” she said.

If a patient arrives at a hospital within 4.5 hours of stroke symptoms, then thrombolysis can be done, she said, adding: “However, in wake-up stroke, we cannot calculate the time of the onset of symptoms. We do not know the window. So, acting fast is important. In case of any symptoms, patients should reach the hospital on time.”

In wake-up strokes, imaging helps give a clear picture for the doctors. “An MRI brain scan should be taken immediately. If it is not available, a CT angiogram should be taken. The scans help us assess the extent of brain injury and blood flow to different parts of the brain. They can determine whether there is diffusion-perfusion mismatch. The difference may represent brain tissue that is still salvageable and can be potentially saved. Like in regular strokes, ‘time is brain’ in wake-up strokes too, making prompt diagnosis and treatment crucial,” she explained.

Shubha Subramanian, senior consultant - neurology, Kauvery Hospitals, Chennai, said that in ischemic strokes, thrombolysis is used to dissolve the blood clot if a patient presents within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. “In cases involving a large vessel occlusion, mechanical thrombectomy is performed within 24 hours of symptom onset, depending on the patient’s eligibility. In wake-up strokes, we do not know when the stroke started; it could be at night or early in the morning. What we do next is crucial. This is why we rely on imaging techniques,” she added.

“MRI has a lot of sequences. articles.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer’s roguelike racing mechanics is not for all
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Any racing game with a high-risk nitro booster called RamJet, is a game you need to play right now, and Star Wars Galactic Racer has plenty of it

Ask anyone what the best part of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace is, and every one of them will say the thunderous, high-octane chaos-filled, pod racing sequence. Now, ask anyone what their favourite arcade-style racing game is, and the Burnout series will pretty much be high up on that list.

Burnout was a racing game built around spectacular car crashes, back when burnout meant wrecking cars rather than your mental health. Now, fuse both Episode 1 Racer and Burnout — the chaos, speed and fiddly unpredictability of racing hovering death traps across the galaxy with aggressive vehicular destruction, and you get Star Wars Galactic Racer . Fuse Games, made up of former Burnout developers, has delivered the insanity.

Everyone knows a Kestar Bool in their circles — the spoiled rich kid who makes sure everyone is pushed down so he can succeed. He has been trained by Sebulba (who folks will recognise from The Phantom Menace , as the evil champion of the pod racing circuit), who has passed not only his racing skills to Kestar, but also his nasty ways.

You play as Shade who is tasked with taking down Kestar’s toxic dominance in the Galactic League, a high-stakes illegal racing circuit where many of the top pilots have a place to earn big bucks after the Empire fell. A story that feels quite Star Wars with a healthy dash of Fast and the Furious with aliens, robots and anti-gravity cars.

The game features a Forza Horizon -esque opening sequence that is every bit as cinematic, allowing you to take control of several types of repulsorcraft, which is the fancy sci-fi name for these floating vehicles. The story usually unfolds in quiet walkabout encampment areas where you get to interact with your opponents in a more stationary setting.

It also gives you a chance to speak to various memorable characters, interact with your cute monkey-like mechanic Hibi, and the founder of the League Darius Pax, a mechanic himself and the person who has brought on Shade to help him deal with Kestar. Once you are all storied up, the action then shifts to the high-speed arenas of the Galactic League.

Star Wars Episode 1 Racer was one of the best games of its time when it came out, and it still holds up today. Even if its graphics are dated, the screams, whines and mechanical shivers of those giant engines powering through levels will always be burned in your brain.

There are four distinct types of repulsorcraft you get to scream around corners with — the trusty, souped-up variants of the Landspeeder, which are big, fast moving slabs that look and handle like muscle cars, with a proper drift. Then, there are the speeder bikes, which have absolutely no protection for the rider, but possess a cool kinetic burst-through that swings you out of corners.

The Skim Speeder gives Sony’s Wipeout racing feels with its extended fins and is designed to go very fast, with an ability to tilt vertically to fit through tight gaps. And lastly, there is the return of the Pod Racer, which you only get to pilot in certain events, sadly. Pod Racers are like chariots, but instead of being drawn by horses, they are pulled by massive engines.

These craft absolutely rip through incredible courses. This game is built on aggressive speed and constant danger, and I love how unpredictable the races are. There were moments I was absolutely sure I was going to finish sixth, but after some clever turns and punting a few opponents into oncoming debris, I netted myself a near first. You have to race dirty, pulling off your special moves like forcefields to gain every edge. Managing your boost is key — spit out too much and your craft is going to be panting.
The game introduces a lovely feature called RamJet, which is a secondary-state boost that adds a lot of risk, but if done right you can punch further.

The best part of the whole pod racing sequence is when Anakin’s pod starts malfunctioning, and he has to fiddle with switches to redirect power, fix the kaput engine, then run a very cool-looking, firing up sequence even as the pod is running at a mindblowing speed.

articles.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is a massive improvement over the original
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Send your pawns that back-to-work notice because Dark Arisen, the new expansion of Dragon Dogma 2, has a new area to explore and a whole host of improvements in tow

This October is turning out to be a case of thanking yourself for holding out on playing certain open world games, starting with the Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition which launched on October 1, 2026 with its new expansion that made the game complete. Now it is the turn of 2024’s Dragon Dogma 2; Dark Arisen that not only brings a massive new area, but also fixes quite a lot of the original’s flaws.

Capcom surprising gamers with a sequel to one of their lesser known, but much loved open world RPG’s Dragon’s Dogma, which is now getting a massive expansion, convinces us of the house of Resident Evil ’s motives to make sure all its IPs get the right treatment.

Welcome to Norgon, a cut-off frigid northern land that is harsh, cold and full of unforgiving monsters. At the centre of it all, there is a mysterious new entity known as a Fallen Dragon, that you as an Arisen and your trusty pawns must travel to. Inspired by Norse and Celtic mythology and influences, Norgon may be a smaller region than the main game’s sprawling kingdom, but it has got heights to scale and unknowns lurking in dark ruins.

Guided by a mysterious wanderer Eir, Dark Arisen switches up the political intrigue to a more ancient evil with deeper answers into the dark side of the cosmic cycle that lies at the heart of this world.

But, wait! Norse influence, dragons, cold mountains and ruins, is that you Skyrim? Yes, there is some of that Skyrim vibe to Norgon in there, but it is just atmosphere. The story feels right in Dark Arisen — it is short, focused and has a few memorable characters. Addressing some of the feedback from the original base game, which had a lot of half-baked, Game of Thrones -type stuff happening (read royal conspiracies and political intrigue), Dark Arisen has a strong, fairly linear, mystery at its core. Eir’s role in all this paints quite a picture.
The peeling off those layers to uncover that mystery as you go along is done well, with clear motives laid out for all its strong characters.

One of the strong points of Dragon’s Dogma is in its action system, where you play an Arisen, a being chosen by a dragon by tearing out your heart. This gives you the ability to pull out pawns from a space called the Rift, leaving you a steady source of party members with ready knowledge of other player’s games.

While you have your main pawn as your companion, you can balance your party out with the ones that offset your weaknesses or you can use them as fodder. Dark Arisen pawns however, come with two extra active weapon skills that bump them up from four to six, with skill options. This matters a lot because you do not just craft individual builds, but design complete party wide synergies.

This versatility can let you experiment more while dealing with the fresh monsters and enemies you encounter in this new area. The pawn system, coupled with an excellent fighting system, is what makes Dragon Dogma 2 really sing, especially when you get your builds right. You can now start melting monsters on sight, which was also one of the big problems of the base game.

Norgon functions as a high-level zone, and as a result, you are at the bottom of the food chain again, so you need to grind to get better weapons. This is good because the challenge of facing off and defeating monsters is back. If you have been playing the base game, hitting level 30 automatically puts you into a power fantasy and it can get boring. Monsters now are tougher and you will need to choose the right classes to stand a chance.

Thankfully, there are a lot of side quests and ruins to explore to net relic weapons. Another point of note, there have been multiple patches before Dark Arisen that have massively balanced and optimised the main game, so if you are starting anew, it is not a bad idea. However, it is worth remembering that no amount of patching fixes the main campaign’s insipid slog of a story.

Enemies are tougher, and in the expansion as well, the game seems to regurgitate similar enemy types throughout, though there is some variety, which was one of the big issues of the main game too. But, what the game lacks in variety it makes up for in dropped weapons called relics.

articles.title: Will the price caps on cancer drugs help bring down the cost of treatment?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: For cancer patients in India, the struggle to stay alive is as much about the disease as about the arithmetic of fighting it. Experts call the government’s price caps a tokenistic, short-term measure. Patients will not benefit unless structural changes including tackling pricing at the manufacturing end, and large-scale government procurement to stabilise prices are put in place Will capping trade margins on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs bring down the overall cost of treatment?

When Sarojini Nadimpally was diagnosed with HER2-positive breast cancer in June 2025, the Delhi-based public health researcher was staring at a hidden reality as daunting as the tumour. One dose of the targeted combination drug she had been prescribed would cost around ₹2.7 lakh — and she needed 18 doses.

As someone who works on access to medicines, she closely followed the government’s recent decision to cap trade margins on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs at 30%, extending a 2019 cap that covered 42. The government claims that the cap, which takes effect on November 9, can save patients about ₹2,500 crore a year.
“Any intervention to lower the prices of cancer drugs is a welcome step,” says Ms. Nadimpally. “But it remains to be seen how this cap will actually reduce what patients pay.”

Cancer is said to be India’s leading cause of catastrophic health spending . India’s out-of-pocket share for cancer care — estimated by various studies to be 50%-80% of direct treatment costs — is far higher than in most high-income systems, where insurance or tax-funded care generally absorbs the bulk of these expenses.

Experts say that drugs make up around over half the costs of cancer care. “High costs of treatments such as targeted therapies and immunotherapy can lead many patients to defer treatment, opt for cheaper but less effective alternatives or give up altogether,” says Vedant Kabra, principal director, surgical oncology, Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Gurugram.

When pills threaten to outrun savings , the standard of care is down to a cruel trade-off between effectiveness and affordability. For example, at about ₹1.25 lakh a month, a lifetime course of osimertinib, the drug of choice in fighting EGFR-mutated lung cancer while reducing the risk of brain metastases, is beyond the reach of many. “These patients switch to gefitinib, which costs only about ₹2,500 a month, but return with brain secondaries and disease progression,” says Narayanankutty Warrier, senior consultant oncologist, MVR Cancer Centre and Research Institute, Kozhikode. “About 30% new-generation drugs are really good,” he says. “The rest are mostly claims. But even a slight improvement in survival means they become monopoly drugs.”

With its latest order , the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) is setting a common trade-margin ceiling on a broad range of cancer medicines, including patented, chemotherapy, targeted, immunotherapy, hormonal and blood cancer drugs. Manufacturers are required to report formulation-level information, including brand name, composition, pack size, PTS (price to stockist) and revised MRP.

The order spells out that a drug with a PTS of ₹70 and an MRP of ₹300 can have an MRP of no more than ₹100, excluding GST. Experts argue that the permitted margin — which amounts to 42.8% of the PTS — is a sizeable mark-up, especially for expensive drugs.

In effect, the government is putting a ceiling on the profit, not the underlying price. For example, the actual prices at which hospitals buy drugs, often after steep discounts negotiated for bulk purchases, are hidden from sight. “A cap on trade margins means little to patients if hospitals and dealers do not pass those savings on, and there is no way of knowing whether they do,” says Ms. Nadimpally.

On October 28, the NPPA published a revised price list for the 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs based on data submitted by companies. The MRPs of 37 drugs remain unchanged, offering an early indication of what the final list may look like. The list also reveals margins that manufacturers, including some Indian generic makers, have had. For instance, palbociclib’s MRP for one brand is down from about ₹40,421 to ₹2,720 a pack, and thiotepa’s from about ₹80,072 to ₹7,150 a vial — drops of more than 90%.

The latest order also counts the cap from the PTS, not from the ex-factory price or the landed cost (price paid after discounts and freight), leaving out upstream additions. The mark-up for cancer medicines is unjustified, says Malini Aisola, co-convener, All India Drug Action Network. “With few middlemen involved in the distribution of these high-value, low-volume products, a hospital or distributor gets to keep nearly all the margin. That legitimises profiteering.”

When it comes to patented, mostly imported medicines, we are price-takers, insists Ms. Aisola. “The government is averse to using its legal powers under the Indian Patent Act and TRIPS (Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights) — such as government use and compulsory licensing — to increase competition.”

articles.title: UNICEF urges media to promote inclusive early childhood development, report responsibly on AI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Workshop seeks to promote ethical, child-sensitive and non-stigmatising reporting, and raise awareness of AI-related risks, including misinformation, deepfakes, bias, privacy violations, and fabricated content

The early years of a child’s life are critical for lifelong health, learning, emotional well-being, and social development. Inclusive early childhood development (iECD) seeks to ensure that every child, including those with developmental delays, disabilities, autism and other forms of neurodivergence, has equitable access to healthcare, nutrition, nurturing care, early learning, protection, and early intervention, Deepa Bhaskaran, Director, Child Development Centre (CDC), Thiruvananthapuram, said.

Speaking at a media workshop on inclusive early childhood development and the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for effective storytelling, organised by UNICEF India in association with the Press Information Bureau, Dr. Bhaskaran said early identification and interventions were vital to ensure that children with disabilities and developmental delays were included at home, in learning environments, and in their communities.
“We train and support medical staff and caregivers, improve early identification and intervention, and provide advanced disability inclusive services,” she said.

Amar Fettle, State Nodal Officer for Adolescent Health, speaking at the workshop, added that while medical infrastructure and personnel were geared towards clinical care, research, teaching, and community outreach, it was equally important to shape public understanding of children’s issues and government programmes.

“Families and the public should understand the services available and help reduce the stigma surrounding disability and developmental delays. The idea is to ensure that children are included in society,” Dr. Fettle said.

The workshop aimed to strengthen understanding of inclusive early childhood development, child rights and disability inclusion, promote ethical, child-sensitive and non-stigmatising reporting, and raise awareness of AI-related risks, including misinformation, deepfakes, bias, privacy violations, and fabricated content.

While reporting, subject matter expertise is essential, Muralikrishna Chinnadurai, trainer with the Google News Initiative India Network, said. Relying on a single AI prompt could produce unreliable information, Mr. Chinnadurai said.
“Humans must be in the loop. AI tools should be used ethically and in an environmentally responsible manner,” he said.

articles.title: MLC polls: In Maharashtra, ruling Mahayuti gets 2 seats, counting continues for other seats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In Maha Vikas Aghadi, NCP SP leads on two seats; setback for ruling NCP prompts senior leader Praful Patel to call for introspection

In Maharashtra, the ruling Mahayuti won two seats in the Legislative Council elections. The results for two of the five teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies in the State were officially declared by the Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer late at night on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). The Bharatiya Janata Party won the Pune Teachers’ constituency, while the Shiv Sena won the Amravati Teachers’ constituency.

Counting was going on for the remaining three seats for the second consecutive day on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). The result for the third seat of the Pune Graduates’ constituency was expected to be declared late at night on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). NCP Sharadchandra Pawar group was leading on the seat till this report went to print.

Meanwhile, the election proved to be a major setback for the ruling NCP, which could not open its account. The dismal trend and the lead taken by NCP SP on the single seat allocated to NCP irked senior leader Praful Patel. “Today’s Vidhan Parishad election results serve as a definitive wake-up call. The time has come for urgent introspection to rebuild trust, realign our priorities, and fix our organisational structure,” he posted on his social media handle X. He had earlier expressed displeasure at the party being denied the Pune seat during the seat distribution talks with allies.

The Teachers’ constituency of Pune had drawn attention in the State for the fight between the Mahayuti partners. The seat was with Congress, which lost in the battle between the two alliance partners. During the seat-sharing talks, the seat was officially given to the BJP, and the Shiv Sena had backed another candidate. On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade defeated Shiv Sena-backed candidate Sachin Sanap and Congress’ sitting MLC Jayant Asagaonkar. Mr Sanap was an OSD to Sena minister Uday Samant.

Shiv Sena’s Kiran Ramrao Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachers’ constituency for the second time, despite internal strife and rebellions in the Mahayuti. He defeated Congress’ Aditi Pohare and independent candidate Shrikant Deshpande. In Amravati Teachers’ constituency, the BJP and the Shiv Sena have traditionally fought against each other. After the seat was declared to the Shiv Sena in the seat distribution talks, some BJP leaders had rebelled. Three BJP rebels had filed nominations as independents. The party had to expel all three of them. Thereafter, Maharashtra minister and BJP leader Chandrashekhar Bawankule had appealed to Eknath Shinde to act against Sena rebel Shrikant Deshpande. On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), Shiv Sena’s official candidate Mr. Sarnaik, defeated him.

The counting for the three other seats continued for the second day on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). Results were likely to be declared for the third seat of the Pune Graduates’ constituency, where NCP SP’s candidate was leading in the rounds of votes counted till then.

fullParagraphs: An Integrated Village Development Programme (IVDP) was launched in Nanjangud by Nestle India on Tuesday in the presence of Nanjangud MLA Darshan Dhruvanarayan.

The programme focuses on strengthening village-level infrastructure and improving quality of life through a range of community-led interventions, including improvements to schools and Anganwadis, installation of Reverse Osmosis (RO) water purification units, pond restoration and other development initiatives, said a statement here.
The IVDP seeks to reaffirm the company’s commitment to supporting inclusive and sustainable community development.
Apart from Mr. Darshan Dhruvanarayan, the programme was attended by Rodrigo Aja Prado, factory manager, Kalale Keshavamurthy, former MLA, and other key government officials.

Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Dhruvanarayan said sustainable rural development requires collective effort and a focus on the needs of local communities. “Initiatives such as Nestlé India’s Integrated Village Development Programme can play an important role in strengthening essential infrastructure and improving access to vital services,” he said.
Factory manager Rodrigo Aja Prado said the company believes that “meaningful community development begins with understanding local needs and working together to address them”.

Through the Integrated Village Development Programme, the company aims to support communities through interventions spanning education, access to safe drinking water and restoration of local resources.
The initiative underscores the importance of collaboration between industry, government and communities in building a more inclusive and sustainable future, a statement from the company added.

articles.title: UNESCO expert committee seeks stronger community participation in Hampi conservation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four days after the UNESCO experts committee visited the World Heritage Site, Hampi, the experts shared preliminary observations with the senior Tourism Department officials in Vidhana Soudha on October 28.

According to the officials, they have identified areas requiring continued attention, including stronger participation of local communities, enhanced institutional capacity for the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority (HWHAMA), continuity in heritage administration and systematic Heritage Impact Assessments for future development projects. A detailed UNESCO expert committee report is expected by mid-December.

UNESCO expert, George Abungu of Kenya described Hampi as an exceptionally significant World Heritage Site and expressed satisfaction with the physical condition of the monuments and the conservation efforts undertaken by the authorities.
He said, “The delegation had come as friends and partners not as investigators, to work with the state and national authorities in identifying strengths, challenges and the way forward.”
Stressing that Hampi is a living community, Prof. Abungu said local people must be active participants in conservation and must also benefit from tourism and heritage development.
Meanwhile, Ichida Shimoda of Japan, another UNESCO expert recommended strengthening HWHAMA with specialised manpower and adequate financial resources.

Development Commissioner and Additional Chief Secretary Uma Mahadevan who was present in this meeting, said, “Hampi’s Outstanding Universal Value (OUV) must be protected without compromise. At the same time, conservation must include the local community. Strong institutions, expert-led planning and administrative continuity are essential for sustainable heritage management.”

articles.title: Manufacturers told to focus on value addition, design-led innovation, tech ownership
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Speakers at the inaugural session of a CII conference on advanced manufacturing said this underscoring the need for India to move beyond manufacturing scale

The need for India to move beyond manufacturing scale towards greater domestic value addition, design-led innovation, technology ownership and globally competitive manufacturing ecosystems was emphasised by speakers at a CII conference on advanced manufacturing here on Wednesday.

Addressing the inaugural session, Special Chief Secretary to the State government Navin Mittal highlighted the significant opportunities emerging at the intersection of advanced manufacturing, renewable energy, energy storage, electric mobility, and data centres. “We are literally standing at the threshold of major revolutions in the energy sector,” he said.

Mr. Mittal emphasised the need to strengthen domestic manufacturing across the solar value chain, develop energy-storage capabilities and leverage AI, IoT, digital twins and robotics to improve operational efficiency, CII said in a release.

Chairman of CII Special Taskforce on Advanced Manufacturing Rahul Garg emphasised on the growing role of AI, robotics, Industrial IoT and digital twins in enhancing productivity, product quality and export competitiveness. Founder and Chairman of Cyient B.V.R. Mohan Reddy said India’s next manufacturing phase must focus on technology ownership and design-led innovation rather than production scale alone.

Micron India Managing Director Anand Ramamurthy spoke on the importance of leapfrogging technology, strengthening infrastructure, creating predictable policy frameworks and developing specialised talent to attract and scale advanced manufacturing in India. CII Telangana Chairman M. Goutham Reddy said advanced manufacturing should be sustainability focused.

articles.title: Former MLC moves HC questioning ‘prohibitory list’ of lands, says government targeting BRS leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A writ petition filed by former MLC Elvis Stephenson of BRS seeking suspension of a Government Order placing lands in ‘prohibitory list’ will be heard by a single judge of Telangana High Court.

When the former legislator’s plea came up on Wednesday for hearing initially before it, the bench of Acting Chief Justice P. Sam Koshy and Justice Suddala Chalapathi Rao directed the Registry to place the same before a single judge. The GO Ms. No. 341 issued by the State government on this September 23 was challenged by the petitioner, contending that it aimed at selectively targetting BRS leaders.

According to the petitioner, the GO was being used by the present government to target its political rivals and placed lands of 16 BRS leaders in the prohibitory list. The targetted leaders included former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhara Rao, K.T. Rama Rao, M. Hanumantha Rao (father-in-law of T. Harish Rao), G. Jagadishwar Reddy, Pilot Rohit Reddy, Palla Rajeshwar Reddy Joginapally Ravinder Rao, J. Sowmya and others, the petitioner stated.

The former MLC stated in the plea that he was the complainant in the ‘çash for vote’ case involving present Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. He claimed that Revanth Reddy, who was MLA in 2015 from Telugu Desam Party, offered a bribe of ₹ 50 lakh to him to vote in MLC election as he was nominated MLC from BRS then. The Anti-Corruption Bureau officials registered a case and arrested Mr. Revanth Reddy then, he explained.

The petitioner contended that Mr. Revanth Reddy was the first accused in the case which was pending for adjudication before the Supreme Court now. Mr. Reddy had targetted BRS leaders since he was arrested in the cash for vote case, the petitioner contended.

articles.title: Intensify inspection to stop child labour: ADC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Mysuru district administration has instructed officials to intensify inspection and initiate legal action against those employing children in the district.

While conducting the quarterly review meeting of the district level executive and task force committee of the District Child Labour Project Society on Tuesday, Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) R. Aishwarya directed officials to take immediate action to prevent children from selling pens, pencils, balloons and other items at the Dasara Exhibition Ground.
Employing children below the age of 18 in stalls and shops at the Dasara Exhibition is strictly prohibited, said ADC.

With Deepavali approaching, ADC instructed officials to maintain strict vigilance and create awareness among owners of firecracker manufacturing units and sales outlets against the employment of those below 18 years, according to a press release.

She said that officials who had been notified as inspector under Section 16 and 17 of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986, must conduct minimum 15 inspections every month in their hobli without fail.

The ADC had directed Tahashildars to conduct a regular meeting of taluk-level child labour eradication and rehabilitation committees. She also instructed officials to conduct awareness programmes about Child Labour Act in schools and public places with the co-ordination of government department.

articles.title: Vedanta Group eyeing $20 billion profits over next two years: Chairman Anil Agarwal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Vedanta is targeting $11 billion in profits this year, Chairman Anil Agarwal said.
Vedanta Group is targeting revenue of $50 billion and profits of $20 billion over the next two years, founder and chairman Anil Agarwal said at an industry event in Kolkata.
“This year we would be making $30 billion revenue and $11 billion in profits. In two years, we would scale our revenues to $50 billion with $20 billion in profits,” he said.
The privately-owned diversified commodities producer has interests spanning aluminium, zinc, oil and gas, power, iron and steel, copper and other critical minerals.

Separately, its recently listed Vedanta Aluminium reported more than a doubling of net profit year-on-year to ₹6,187 crore for the quarter ended September. Revenue rose 41% to ₹22,066 crore during the period.
The company increased aluminium production by 5% year-on-year to 649 kilotonnes (KT). Production of value-added aluminium products rose 31% to 432 KT, while alumina output climbed 37% to 895 KT.

Vedanta Aluminium also reduced its net debt by ₹3,090 crore during the quarter compared with the preceding quarter, signalling an improvement in its debt position alongside higher production and earnings.
